titulo: Simplification of Embedding Process in Retrieval Augmented Generation for Optimizing Question Answering Chatbot Model
autores: M. R. Putri; A. Y. Husodo; B. Irmawati
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Communication, Networks and Satellite (COMNETSAT)
abstract: In the current digital era, interaction through chatbots has become commonplace due to their ability to serve multiple users simultaneously. One of the widely used types of chatbots today is the Question Answering Chatbot (QAC). In this study, a QAC model is built using a Large Language Model (LLM) and the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework. Compared to conventional generation models, RAG offers several advantages, such as strong scalability, easy data acquisition, and low training costs. The RAG process involves Indexing and Retrieval Generation stages. This research focuses on simplifying the embedding process in the indexing stage for efficient context management and response quality. This study utilizes GPT-3.5-Turbo as the LLM. The results obtained using GPT-3.5-Turbo indicate that the use of the Answer Only dataset and Prompt 2 provides the best response quality, with consecutive Faithfulness and Answer Relevancy metric values of 0.9167 and 0.9512, respectively. Subsequently, an experiment is conducted using the latest LLM, namely GPT-4o (omni), with Prompt 2 and the Question Only dataset to compare the two models. GPT-4o produces the best response quality with a Faithfulness metric value of $\mathbf{0 . 9 5 5 1}$. Meanwhile, the best Answer Relevancy score is achieved by GPT-3.5-Turbo with a value of 0.9512.

titulo: Construction and Evaluation of a Large Language Model for the Energy Domain Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: R. Wang; Q. Wang; Y. Nan; H. Ye; P. He
venue: 2025 7th International Conference on Frontier Technologies of Information and Computer (ICFTIC)
abstract: Knowledge in the energy sector is characterized by its multi-source heterogeneity, strong specialization, and rapid evolution, posing significant challenges to traditional information retrieval and question-answering systems. To address this, this study constructs a regulatory Q&A large language model. By adopting Retrieval-Augmented Generation technology, we collected and built an energy knowledge base, constructed a retriever and a generator, and implemented a vertical-domain LLM Q&A system. An experimental dataset was created for evaluation, resulting in scores of 0.93 for answer similarity, 0.79 for answer relevance, and 0.63 for answer correctness. The proposed model outperformed the base model by 0.04, 0.02, and 0.05 points, respectively. It effectively mitigates issues of the base model in vertical domains, such as inadequate semantic understanding, unhelpful responses, and factual hallucinations, thereby providing an effective technical pathway for intelligent knowledge services in the energy field.

titulo: Learning Hadith through Chatbot Using Large Language Model and Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: A. A. Razali; A. M. Ali; W. A. Latif; E. A. Kamaru-Zaman; F. S. M. Rashid; N. H. A. Hamid
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
abstract: Hadith is the concept of recorded action or sayings of Prophet Muhammad throughout his lifetime. The digitalization of Islamic knowledge has improved accessibility toward Hadith literature. However, many users often encounter problems like static keyword searching that relies on specific keyword or Arabic terms usage. They also face the process of search result skimming that is time consuming and mentally taxing when combined with the actual learning process. To resolve these issues, the development of Hadith chatbot using LLM is proposed. The objectives of this project are to: (1) identify Hadith texts and themes for Sahih Muslim, (2) design an LLM framework for these texts, and (3) develop a web-based chatbot prototype. The research methodology consists of preliminary studies, knowledge acquisition, data collection and preprocessing, system design, system development, testing and refinement, and documentation. The resulting web-based Hadith chatbot displayed the ability to retrieve relevant Hadith accurately while adhering to the context given. Users are now able to learn Hadith knowledge using their day-to-day conversational language as a medium of interaction. Identified future work includes the knowledge base expansion and multilingual support implementation into the system. In addition to the Sahih Muslim and Syarah Sahih Muslim, other major Hadith collections, Quranic verses, and their interpretations should be integrated to make the system more comprehensive for Islamic knowledge as a whole. Multilingual support could also be considered to expand the chatbot to a more diverse group of users. Overall, this project has demonstrated the effectiveness of Hadith chatbot using LLM in enhancing accessibility and understanding of Hadith knowledge by removing the process of static keyword searches and search results skimming.

titulo: Confidence Aware Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation for Robust Question Answering
autores: Z. Zhao; Y. Si
venue: 2026 International Conference on Large Models and Intelligent Agent Technologies (LMIAT)
abstract: Multimodal retrieval augmented generation improves evidence-grounded question answering by providing multimodal large language models with images, text, tables, and optical-character-recognition content. Existing pipelines commonly apply a fixed retrieval procedure despite query-level variation in evidence quality. This paper proposes CAMRAG, a confidence aware framework that combines calibrated retrieval scores, score margins, cross-modal agreement, and modality coverage. Low-confidence questions trigger one rewrite and supplementary retrieval; a cumulative-confidence rule then constructs a compact context. CAMRAG achieves 44.8 EM, 54.9 F1, and 76.5 evidence recall on WebQA, and 55.2 EM, 64.7 F1, and 81.8 evidence recall on MultiModalQA. Only 38.6% of questions trigger supplementary retrieval at the selected threshold. These results demonstrate consistent gains under the evaluated benchmarks while avoiding repeated retrieval for most queries.

titulo: High-Precision Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enhanced Question Answering Systems
autores: Z. Dai
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Signal Processing (ICSP)
abstract: Intelligent question answering (QA) systems based on large language models (LLMs) have seen increasing application, especially with the integration of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques. These systems have proven valuable in areas such as intelligent customer service and virtual assistants. However, traditional chunking methods often fail to capture the semantic and structural relationships within documents, resulting in fragmented context. This paper proposes HRAG-QA, a novel high-precision retrieval-augmented generation approach that leverages structured document storage to enhance retrieval and response performance. Simulation-based evaluations demonstrate that HRAG-QA outperforms existing techniques in retrieval recall, mean reciprocal rank, and answer accuracy, highlighting the potential for improved QA system performance and scalability. The implementation code and datasets used in this study are available at https://github.com/Thedaizheng/rag_system.

titulo: Automated Smart City Planning through Personalized Large Language Model with Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: N. Alamsyah; M. Amirul Haq; C. Oktomy Noto Susanto
venue: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The rapid urbanization and the need for sustainable city management have driven the demand for intelligent and efficient smart city planning solutions. In light of the dangers of cyberattacks and the inherent risks associated with using foreign-run services, our approach provides a secure and autonomous solution for urban development planning.

titulo: B-RAG: A Retrieval Augmented Generation Based AI System for Educational Question Answering from Bangla Textbook in Bangla
autores: M. S. A. Khan; M. S. A. Khan
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Bangladesh’s education system heavily relies on National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) resources, which serve as the primary knowledge base for millions of students across the country. However, digital tools for interactive learning in Bangla remain limited, particularly in supporting direct question answering from these textbooks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances educational chatbots by improving accuracy and contextual relevance while mitigating hallucinations in large language models. Although RAG systems have been applied globally in language learning, programming, health, and legal education, no system currently addresses Bangla textbook question answering. To address this, we propose B-RAG, a RAGpowered chatbot that retrieves and generates accurate Bangla responses from NCTB content. The system indexes textbook content into a vector database, performs semantic retrieval, and generates responses via a large language model, deployed through a Streamlit interface with FastAPI. Evaluation using MultiClassification, Token-Similarity, and Token-Level F1 metrics shows high retrieval accuracy, strong linguistic alignment, and precise answer generation, demonstrating B-RAG’s potential for context-aware educational support in Bangla.

titulo: A Lightweight MLLM-Driven Multimodal RAG Framework for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
autores: Z. Zhao; Y. Si
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Machine Learning and Intelligent Systems Engineering (MLISE)
abstract: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves evidence-grounded question answering, but many existing systems still rely mainly on textual retrieval and weakly handle visual, OCR, table, and metadata evidence. This paper proposes a lightweight MLLM-driven multimodal RAG framework following an “Input-Retrieve-Fuse-Reason-Output” pipeline. Given a query, visual, textual, and OCR-based retrievers collect modality-specific candidates. A lightweight evidence fusion module then normalizes retrieval scores, considers query relevance and cross-modal alignment, penalizes redundancy, and selects a compact multimodal context for MLLM reasoning. Experiments on WebQA and MultiModalQA show consistent improvements over direct MLLM answering, text-only RAG, multimodal retrieval without fusion, score-normalized multimodal RAG, and cross-modal reranking multimodal RAG. The framework achieves 60.7/62.5/68.9/83.4 on WebQA and 69.2/71.4/79.3/89.6 on MultiModalQA in terms of EM/Acc./F1/ER, showing improved answer quality and evidence reliability.

titulo: Intelligent Laptop Assistance Chatbot using Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: V. R; Manasa; P. G; R. S. G; S. K. N
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
abstract: The growth of e-commerce has led to an increasing demand for smart and scalable customer support systems. Traditional chatbots remain less effective since they are more prone to giving incorrect responses due to poor contextual understanding and brittle rule-based reasoning. This paper proposes the use of a Retrieval-Augmented-Generation based laptop assistance chatbot that effectively combines semantic search with large language models powers to provide smart, context-sensitive responses to troubleshoot laptops of top few brands . Product guides and support documents are chunked, processed, and stored in a vector database to enable real-time retrieval. Given a customer's query, the chatbot retrieves the most relevant chunks of documents and leverages a large language model to generate human-like answers. Moreover, the system supports smart recommendations of YouTube videos relevant to the user's question, which enhances guidance over troubleshooting and product usage. The proposed model was evaluated with the RAGAS metric, achieving a faithfulness of 0.81, answer relevance of 0.76, and context precision and recall of 0.74, to show strong factual grounding and contextual reliability. Overall, the system greatly improves response accuracy, reduces human-agent load, and enhances customer experience in resolving laptop related issues.

titulo: Localized Open-Source LLM Aware Retrieval Augmented Generation of Legal Documents: A Case Study on Indian Constitution and Penal Code
autores: P. Phukon; Y. Lokhar; P. P. Ray
venue: 2024 International BIT Conference (BITCON)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are advanced artificial intelligence systems which are designed to generate human-like language based on their training data. Retrieval- Augmented Generation (RAG) is a framework that enhances the response of LLM by incorporating external information sources, leading to more accurate, context-relevant responses. However, LLMs commonly struggle with contextual relevance, especially in particular fields such as legal documentation, where specific local laws are crucial. Furthermore, there is limited research on the use of RAG technology in the legal area, particularly for producing and analyzing legal documents. This study develops a chatbot using RAG to answer questions on the Indian Constitution (IC) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC), with a Streamlit-based interface to display legal queries and their generated responses. This study analyzes the evaluation of various LLMs integrated with RAG including (including (i) Llama3 8b, (ii) Mistral 7b, (iii) Gemma2 7b, (iv) Phi3 3.8b, and (v) Qwen2 7b and it evaluates their performance in terms of relevance, faithfulness, context recall, and context precision.

titulo: A Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Border Inspection Legal Question Answering
autores: Y. Zhang; D. Li; G. Peng; S. Guo; Y. Dou; R. Yi
venue: 2024 International Conference on Asian Language Processing (IALP)
abstract: Border inspection legal question answering (LQA) is designed for specific legal scenarios, aiming to address legal questions related to border inspections and provide accurate and practical legal guidance to the public and border inspection departments. Current research requires a retrieval process regardless of whether the necessary knowledge already exists, and does not evaluate the legal information in the generated responses, leading to errors and low-quality content. we propose the Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework for Border Inspection LQA (DRAG-BILQA), which generates responses first and then dynamically controls retrieval based on confidence scores. In this framework, we innovatively introduce a legal factor recognition module to ensure the legal accuracy of generated answers and improve the quality of the generation. We also present the BorderLegal-QA dataset, filling the gap in border inspection legal datasets. We conducted extensive experiments on both the BorderLegal-QA and the general LQA dataset JEC-QA. Experimental results show that DRAG-BILQA outperforms Sota models in terms of legal factor recognition accuracy and retrieval performance, achieving a METEOR score of 39.5 and improving generation quality. Case analysis also demonstrate that DRAG-BILQA effectively Augmented the legal accuracy of the generated content.

titulo: A KBQA Method Based on Mixed Retrieval Augmented Generation Technology
autores: J. Luo; L. Wang; F. Liu
venue: 2025 IEEE 6th International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Information Technology (AINIT)
abstract: Retrieval augmented generation technology has made it significantly convenient to utilize large language models for knowledge base question answering on local document data, and it has become one of the prominent research hotspots in the field of LLM. However, existing RAG frameworks for knowledge bases still face several challenges, including the inability to extract key information, incomplete answers, and inaccuracies, which may lead to fragmented answers and low-quality responses. To address these issues, this paper proposes a mixed RAG method that combines VectorRAG and GraphRAG to improve the accuracy and contextual relevance of knowledge base question answering. Additionally, to tackle the problem where user queries may lack specific entities, causing GraphRAG to fail to extract key information, we introduce a dual-retrieval paradigm. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing the model's question-answering abilities.

titulo: Robust Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Retrieval Augmented Generation in Power Grid Dispatching Regulations
autores: Y. Zou; Y. Liu; S. Zhang; B. Song; X. Liang
venue: 2025 International Conference on New Power System Technology (PowerCon)
abstract: This paper presents an retrieval-augmented based question-answering model tailored for power grid dispatch regulations. titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Large Language Model For Educational Chatbot
autores: L. Danuarta; V. C. Mawardi; V. Lee
venue: 2024 Ninth International Conference on Informatics and Computing (ICIC)
abstract: In the digital age, educational chatbots are increasingly essential for providing personalized learning experience. This study explores the potential of the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) method to enhanced the performance of educational chatbots. By integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with real-time data retrieval from external sources, the RAG approach improves the accuracy, relevance, and safety of chatbot responses. The findings underscore the effectiveness of RAG advancing educational chatbot performance.

titulo: KG2QA: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Communication Standards Question Answering
autores: Z. Luo; W. Wan; T. Zhang; D. Wang; X. Tang
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: The rapid evolution of communication technologies has led to an explosion of standards, rendering traditional expert-dependent consultation methods inefficient and slow. To address this challenge, we propose KG2QA, a question answering (QA) framework for communication standards that integrates fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) with a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) via a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. We construct a high-quality dataset of 6,587 QA pairs from ITU-T recommendations and fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, achieving significant performance gains: BLEU-4 increases from 18.86 to 66.90, outperforming both the base model and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. A structured KG containing 13,906 entities and 13,524 relations is built using LLM-assisted triple extraction based on a custom ontology. In our KG-RAG pipeline, the fine-tuned LLMs first retrieves relevant knowledge from KG, enabling more accurate and factually grounded responses. Evaluated by DeepSeek-V3 as a judge, the KG-enhanced system improves performance across five dimensions, with an average score increase of 2.26%, demonstrating superior factual accuracy and relevance. Integrated with Web platform and API, KG2QA delivers an efficient and interactive user experience. Our code and data have been open-sourced1

titulo: Using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation Technique to Improve the Performance of GPT-4 in Answering Quran Questions
autores: S. Alnefaie; E. Atwell; M. A. Alsalka
venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing (ICNLP)
abstract: One of the challenges in natural text processing concerns answering questions, and studies have tended to use large language models for this task. However, these models often generate misleading and incorrect answers. Answering religious questions is a delicate and sensitive topic. Therefore, the contribution of this paper is to use the retrieval-augmented generation technique to improve the performance of large language modules in Arabic. In this experiment, we compared the answers of standard GPT-4 and GPT-4 using the retrieval-augmented generation technique for the same questions on the Quranic Question–Answer Pair dataset. The results showed that retrieval-augmented generation technique improved the answers to different types of questions. It also improved the text parts of answers, reaching a 0.266 exact match (EM) and 0.772 F1. In addition, it improved the parts of answers regarding Quranic verses, achieving 0.333 F1@1, 0.25 EM, 0.53 F1, and 0.266 partial average precision.

titulo: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Question Answering over Product Manuals
autores: W. Zhang; W. Zhou
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Computer Information Science and Application Technology (CISAT)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing tasks. However, in intelligent question-answering (QA) applications within vertical domains, they are highly prone to hallucinations due to a lack of domain-specific knowledge. Retrieval-Augmented Generation effectively mitigates this issue by integrating external knowledge bases. In this paper, we propose a RAG framework tailored for product manual QA. First, we utilize LLMs to convert illustrations within the manuals into natural language descriptions, and perform hierarchical chunking on the manual content based on Markdown heading structures to construct a knowledge base dedicated to product documents. Subsequently, a hierarchical document routing method is employed to identify the specific product manual targeted by the user's query, thereby narrowing the retrieval scope. Building upon this, a hybrid retrieval approach—combining keyword retrieval and semantic vector retrieval—is applied to extract the top-K relevant chunks. Finally, LLM generates a comprehensive response containing both textual explanations and relevant illustrations based on the retrieved results. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to baseline methods, our proposed approach improves the final score from 0.7286 to 0.7943, validating the effectiveness of this framework in product manual QA scenarios.

titulo: Development of an RAG-Based LLM Chatbot for Enhancing Technical Support Service
autores: H. -C. Lee; K. Hung; G. M. -T. Man; R. Ho; M. Leung
venue: TENCON 2024 - 2024 IEEE Region 10 Conference (TENCON)
abstract: The global shortage of manpower for technical support is a critical issue in the digital transformation era. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have made significant strides in natural language processing, leading to the development of AI chatbots to address this problem. However, LLMs have notable limitations in handling domain-specific information, often generating incorrect responses when queries go beyond the coverage of the training data or require the most up-to-date information. A promising solution is the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach, which incorporates domain-specific data retrieval into the generative process. Our team has developed a domain-specific and RAG-based LLM chatbot to enhance the software house technical support of an IT consultant in Canada. The chatbot was implemented and evaluated in real-world production environments. Preliminary results show that the system has achieved high scores of 38%, 188%, and 40% in the ROUGE-I, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L measures, respectively, compared to using only a general LLM model. End-user feedback also reflected that the enhanced system produced more accurate and efficient replies, thereby enhancing overall customer satisfaction.

titulo: A Hallucination-Resistant Document-Centric Conversational Framework Using Fusion Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: M. Sambasivarao; R. Ramesh; M. S. S. Sai
venue: 2026 International Conference on Secure IoT and Cybersecurity (ICOSICS)
abstract: Large Language Models have achieved very good results in conversational question answering. However, their efficiency over technical and research documents remains limited due to certain hallucinations, a lack of source grounding, and scarce explainability. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates some of these issues due to its incorporation of external knowledge, but most existing RAG systems employ fixed strategies, with little transparency about how retrieved evidence supports generated responses. These limitations reduce trust and usability within high-stakes technical domains. This paper presents an explainable RAG based conversational system, put forward for question answering over technical research documents. The proposed system introduces a query-intent-aware adaptive retrieval mechanism that dynamically adjusts retrieval parameters based on the inferred intent of the user query, allowing for more precise and contextually relevant document retrieval. To ensure answer verifiability, proposed technique leverages citation-grounded response generation explicitly linking the generated outputs to their supporting document segments. An explainability layer is integrated that exposes evidence retrieved and generation rationale for reductions of unsupported claims and improvements in user trust. The system is implemented using an open-source large language model, sentence-level semantic embeddings, and a vector-based similarity search framework-ensuring reproducibility and practical deployment. We conduct experiments with proposed techniques on a dataset of technical research papers, with comparisons against a vanilla LLM model as well as a traditional RAG model. The experimental findings underline that our proposed model performs better w.r.t relevance, citation, and hallucinated answers, and the latency is acceptable, hence emphasizing the effectiveness of adaptive retrieval as well as explanation techniques incorporated in our proposed model, which make proposed a viable answer for technical documents leveraging the benefits of RAG-based conversational systems.

abstract: Improve the accuracy of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Large Language Model (LLM), this paper proposes a document layout detection and description network model (Doc-LDNet) for RAG. Applying Doc-LDNet as a document parsing tool in RAG can effectively enrich the results of document parsing. The experimental results show that applying the Doc-LDNet in RAG can effectively improve the accuracy of LLM in professional domain knowledge question-answering.

titulo: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Query-Driven Video Content Grounding
autores: K. V. S. Akash; P. Abhinav; P. A. Kruti; D. Rajeev
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications (ICIMIA)
abstract: Video Question Answering (Video-QA) requires answers grounded in visual events, temporal context, and spoken or written evidence. Conventional large language models can generate plausible but unsupported responses when long videos are compressed into incomplete prompts. This paper presents a lightweight Video-RAG framework that retrieves relevant video segments before generation. Videos are divided into fixed 8 -second chunks; CLIP embeddings are extracted from representative frames, BERT/T5 embeddings are extracted from ASR transcripts or subtitles, and both streams are indexed with FAISS. At inference, a hybrid visual-textual similarity score retrieves timestamped evidence that is provided to a multimodal LLM. The framework is validated on standard Video-QA settings, including MSR-VTT-QA, TVQA, and ActivityNet-QA, using retrieval quality, answer accuracy, memory, and runtime metrics. Results show that dual visual-textual retrieval improves grounding over text-only, visual-only, Standard LLM, CLIP, and Video-LLaMA baselines while remaining practical on commodity GPU and Apple Silicon hardware. The work demonstrates that explicit retrieval is an effective and deployable mechanism for factual, explainable Video-QA.

abstract: This work describes the design and the implementation of an AI document search chatbot using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture that combines generative modelling with information retrieval to provide an accurate and verifiable responses. The system supports PDF, DOCX, CSV, and TXT uploads, which are automatically processed, segmented, and indexed in a vector database for semantic search. Owing to its modular design, the architecture is scalable, maintainable, and easily extensible for enterprise and academic knowledge-management applications.

titulo: Leveraging Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Synergies for Intelligent Fault Analysis in Urban Rail Transit Signaling Systems
autores: T. Su; C. Ma; X. Chen; X. Wang
venue: 2025 4th Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (FASTA)
abstract: To address the challenges of insufficient text data utilization and low manual diagnosis efficiency in urban rail transit signaling system fault analysis, particularly the difficulty in handling novel faults under unmanned train operations, this study proposes a dual-engine framework integrating Knowledge Graph (KG) and Large Language Model (LLM). Based on preprocessed fault diagnosis logs from Nanjing Metro's signaling system, a multi-dimensionally annotated dataset was constructed. The CasRel joint extraction model was employed to overcome the limitations of traditional pipeline methods in recognizing nested terms and mitigating error propagation, building a high-density domain-specific KG. Subsequently, a three-tiered question-answering paradigm (fact query, enumeration verification, causal verification) and multi-granularity intent classification system were innovatively integrated to enable semantic retrieval and dynamic reasoning over the KG. To tackle data dependence and logical hallucinations in vertical domain LLMs, a domain-adapted LLM was developed using QLoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning technology, complemented by a zero-shot autonomous reasoning mechanism based on prompt engineering. By deconstructing signal transmission logic, cross-system association rules, and device temporal relationships, causal chain prompts, analogical inference templates, and dynamic temporal context cues were generated to guide the LLM in performing root cause deduction along domain knowledge-constrained pathways without historical data. Concurrently, the reasoning logic underwent real-time verification leveraging the KG's security protocol rule library to filter domain-violating hypotheses. Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) technology further embedded KG retrieval results and dynamic prompts into the LLM's input, forming a closed-loop “knowledge anchoring, prompt guidance, verification and generation” decision process. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework significantly enhances novel fault diagnosis accuracy and reliability, achieving security-compliant root cause localization in zero-shot scenarios while outperforming traditional methods. It autonomously transforms new fault resolutions into KG nodes, triggering LLM incremental learning to enable continuous evolution of the knowledge system. This research provides an interpretable and scalable diagnostic decision-support paradigm for intelligent rail transit operations, offering technical substantiation for deploying industrial LLMs in safety-critical systems.

abstract: Conventional RAG approaches, though effective for general tasks, often fail to retrieve precise information for complex questions involving multiple entities, which is called Multi-Entity question answering (QA), such as “How are all IEEE Fellows distributed across distinct research domains by 2024?”. Most students have given a positive response, saying that their motivation to keep learning and their confidence in their abilities have increased. titulo: ActiveParam: Selective Parameterization for Efficient and Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: S. Li; X. Liu; P. Peng; S. Liu
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by incorporating external knowledge. However, parametric RAG (PRAG) methods often suffer from redundancy and noise sensitivity, leading to inefficiency and degraded robustness. We propose ActiveParam, a framework for selective knowledge parameterization. ActiveParam introduces a Knowledge Probing stage, where the LLM computes an ignorance score to identify knowledge gaps for each document. Only documents with high scores, indicating novel information, are parameterized through lightweight adapters. Experiments on four question-answering benchmarks and three LLMs show that ActiveParam consistently improves F1 scores by 2-5 points over baselines like Naive Combine, while simultaneously reducing the number of required parameter adapters. This work thus establishes that selective parameterization, guided by our novel ignorance score, offers a more efficient and robust path for knowledge augmentation.

venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Social Network Systems (AISNS)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face significant challenges in knowledge-intensive tasks, including knowledge solidification, insufficient timeliness, and hallucination generation. The approach constructs a dynamic multi-granularity knowledge indexing system and integrates an intelligent dual-path routing decision mechanism to achieve efficient collaboration between knowledge retrieval and generation processes. titulo: Context Awareness Gate for Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: M. H. Heydari; A. Hemmat; E. Naman; A. Fatemi
venue: 2024 15th International Conference on Information and Knowledge Technology (IKT)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a widely adopted approach to mitigate the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in answering domain-specific questions. Previous research has predominantly focused on improving the accuracy and quality of retrieved data chunks to enhance the overall performance of the generation pipeline. However, despite ongoing advancements, the critical issue of retrieving irrelevant information-which can impair a model's ability to utilize its internal knowledge effectively-has received minimal attention. In this work, we investigate the impact of retrieving irrelevant information in open-domain question answering, highlighting its significant detrimental effect on the quality of LLM outputs. To address this challenge, we propose the Context Awareness Gate (CAG) architecture, a novel mechanism that dynamically adjusts the LLM's input prompt based on whether the user query necessitates external context retrieval. Additionally, we introduce the Vector Candidates method, a core mathematical component of CAG that is statistical, LLM-independent, and highly scalable. We further examine the distributions of relationships between contexts and questions, presenting a statistical analysis of these distributions. This analysis can be leveraged to enhance the context retrieval process in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

venue: IEEE Transactions on Reliability
abstract: Large language model-based question answering has the potential to improve access to technical knowledge, but hallucinated responses remain a severe reliability risk when answers are generated without sufficient evidential support. In this article, we propose RC-RAG, a reliability-centered retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for PHM question answering that explicitly incorporates evidence evaluation and verification into the retrieval and generation pipeline. RC-RAG augments PHM literature with document-level meta-knowledge, performs hierarchical document-content retrieval, and applies relevance and evidence assessment with verification-aware answer generation to ensure that answers are produced only when sufficient and consistent evidence is available. To evaluate the framework, we construct a curated PHM data challenge question-answering benchmark derived from a series of PHM conferences and data challenge competitions, including those organized by the IEEE Reliability Society and the PHM research community. Experimental results show that RC-RAG achieves significantly higher accuracy and precision compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

titulo: An Evidence-Grounded Multi-Stage Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Multimodal Medical Question Answering
autores: K. Sharma; S. Srivastava; S. Sahrawat; A. Singhal
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI Engineering and Innovations (AIEI)
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based medical question answering systems often produce fluent answers, but they lack clear grounding, source traceability, and verification, which limits their reliability for clinical exploration of knowledge and medical education. By conditioning responses on external evidence, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates these constraints. However, most current medical RAG techniques rely on shallow pipelines and single-source retrieval, leave them susceptible to topic drift, noisy context, and unsupported generation. This paper proposes a multi-stage, evidence-grounded RAG framework that explicitly models retrieval quality, evidence sufficiency, and grounding verification through a five-stage orchestrated pipeline consisting of multi-source retrieval from PubMed and NCBI Bookshelf, cross-encoder reranking, sentence-level evidence distillation, gated follow-up retrieval, grounded answer generation using a locally deployed LLM (Ollama), and post-generation grounding verification with safe regeneration. To facilitate multimodal reasoning and guarantee that all medical explanations are produced solely by the text-based RAG pipeline, the framework further allows clinical documents provided by the user and vision-derived summaries. ResNet-18 models trained and assessed on common MedMNIST benchmarks are used to create vision components, which are only merged after independent validation. titulo: A Systematic Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Techniques for Mitigating Hallucinations in Chatbot Systems
autores: S. M. Hatim; A. A. K. Nizam; N. Shamsudin; N. A. M. Zamani; Z. Ahmad
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly deployed in education, health care, and decision-support settings, yet their reliability is limited by hallucination: fluent responses that are factually incorrect, weakly grounded, or inconsistent with supplied evidence. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this limitation by conditioning generation on external knowledge retrieved at inference time. This paper presents a systematic review of RAG techniques for hallucination mitigation in chatbot systems. Following the PRISMA 2020 process, studies published from 2020 to 2026 were searched in Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. After duplicate removal, screening, and full-text eligibility assessment, 23 studies were synthesized qualitatively. The review analyzes RAG architectures, retrieval strategies, evidence-integration mechanisms, and evaluation practices. Findings show that advanced and modular RAG architectures generally improve factuality and faithfulness over purely parametric LLMs, especially when retrieval is paired with re-ranking, evidence filtering, verification, or citation-aware generation. However, mitigation remains constrained by retrieval noise, latency, limited benchmark standardization, and weak integration between hallucination detection and correction. The paper concludes with research directions for trustworthy, efficient, and explainable RAG-based chatbot systems.

abstract: Documentation in real-time is time consuming and a tiring process to do manually. This chatbot is not dependent on any other external APIs and uses Streamlit. Thus, the proposed paper provides a cost-efficient RAG system by using a LLM called Mistral from Ollama.

titulo: Pathfinder: MCTS and LLM Feedback-Based Path Selection for Multi-Hop Question Answering
autores: D. P. Maram; K. Gunaratna; V. Srinivasan; H. Jeelani; S. Chappidi
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Multi-hop question answering is a challenging task in which language models must reason over multiple steps to reach the correct answer. With the help of Large Language Models and their reasoning capabilities, existing systems are able to think and decompose an input question over multiple steps to analyze, retrieve, and reason. However, training-based approaches for this problem still suffer from LLM hallucinations and incorrect reasoning paths that hinder performance. Hence, we propose PATHFINDER, an approach that: (i) uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to generate training path traces, (ii) improves training data quality by filtering erroneous and lengthy traces using sub-answer recall and LLM-as-a-judge verification, and (iii) reformulates sub-queries to handle failed retrieval cases. By following these steps, we demonstrate that PATHFINDER improves the performance of multi-hop QA over public benchmark datasets.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising solutions for various downstream tasks. A notable application of RAG is in open-domain question answering, which can be implemented in multiple languages, including Bahasa Indonesia. titulo: Intellicore – A Framework for Building Personalized AI Agents using Retrieval- Augmented Generation
autores: A. Singh; P. Lal; Amrita
venue: 2026 International Conference on Sustainable Engineering and Technology Innovations (ICSETI)
abstract: The rapid advancement in large language models (LLMs) has demonstrated their significant potential to function as intelligent assistants across diverse application domains. Despite their impressive reasoning capabilities, most existing LLM-based systems are designed as generic models and exhibit limited ability to adapt the specific knowledge requirements, preferences, and communication styles of individual users. This limitation reduces their effectiveness in domain where personalization is essential, such as education, healthcare, professional consulting, and personal productivity. To address this challenge, this paper proposes Intellicore, a novel framework for developing personalized AI assistants using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach. This proposed framework integrates both user-specific and domain-specific data sources with optimized retrieval processes. It enables the generation of responses that are contextually relevant, accurate and tailored to individual users. Intellicore emphasizes a modular architecture by incorporating document embedding, semantic search, and adaptive prompt engineering, and efficient fine-tuning techniques, thereby ensuring scalability across multiple users and applications. Unlike conventional chatbot platforms, Intellicore ensures response consistency by grounding generation in authoritative external knowledge sources while simultaneously adapting to the user context. The paper further details the implementation of the proposed framework, including use of vector databases, orchestration layers, and metrics for evaluating personalization quality. The initial empirical results indicate that Intellicore significantly improves accuracy and user satisfaction when compared to standard LLM-based chatbots. Overall, this study presents a practical and extensible framework for building next-generation AI assistants that effectively balance general intelligence with user-specific personalization, laying the groundwork for future applications in interactive intelligent systems.

titulo: Path-Retriever: Precise and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning with GNN-Assisted Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: R. Tang; F. Wu
venue: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) empowers Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding them in external knowledge. Knowledge graphs (KGs), which capture vast amounts of facts in a structured format, offer a reliable source for RAG. However, existing methods struggle with complex, multi-hop questions, often either over-relying on the LLM’s fallible sequential reasoning or failing to generate verifiable, structured evidence from KGs. In this paper, we propose Path-Retriever, a novel two-stage framework that decouples contextual representation learning from explicit, verifiable reasoning. In the first stage, we train an instruction-guided Graph Neural Network (GNN) not as a direct answer predictor, but as a powerful feature extractor. This pre-trained GNN learns to produce structure-aware, reasoning-oriented embeddings for entities and relations tailored to a specific question context. In the second stage, we introduce an LLM-Guided Interactive Beam Search (IGBS) algorithm. This algorithm performs an explicit path exploration on the KG, using the rich embeddings from our pre-trained GNN as a powerful heuristic scoring function. Crucially, after each expansion step, the most promising candidate paths are evaluated by LLM, which acts as a reasoning "strategist" to dynamically prune the search space and identify correct answers early. This interactive process synergizes the structural awareness of the GNN with the logical inference capabilities of the LLM. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in two widely used KGQA benchmarks (WebQSP and CWQ). Our results validate the efficacy of combining deep contextual graph representations with LLM-guided interactive search for solving complex, multi-hop questions.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a key tool to strengthen maternal health through predictive models, remote monitoring, and decision-support systems. titulo: KRPKI-RAG: Knowledge Refinement and Potential Knowledge Integration for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve strong results on knowledge-intensive tasks but remain prone to hallucinations in domain-specific question-answering tasks. To address these challenges, we propose KRPKIRAG, a novel question answering framework that integrates Knowledge Refinement and Potential Knowledge Integration for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. The system first employs a knowledge refinement module to filter noisy passages while retaining high-value content. Subsequently, it applies potential knowledge integration to re-examine passages initially deemed noisy or ambiguous to determine whether they should be retained. Experiments on multiple question-answering datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in F1 and Exact Match (EM) scores, highlighting the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed method.

titulo: DynaRAG: Bridging Static and Dynamic Knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: P. Liang; M. Yuan; J. Liu; J. Yang; X. Li; W. Yan; Y. Wu
venue: 2026 9th International Symposium on Big Data and Applied Statistics (ISBDAS)
abstract: We present DynaRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework designed to handle both static and time-sensitive information needs through dynamic knowledge integration. Unlike traditional RAG pipelines that rely solely on static corpora, DynaRAG selectively invokes external APIs when retrieved documents are insufficient for answering a query. The system employs an LLM-based reranker to assess document relevance, a sufficiency classifier to determine when fallback is necessary, and Gorilla v2—a state-of-the-art API calling model—for accurate tool invocation. We further enhance robustness by incorporating schema filtering via FAISS to guide API selection. Evaluations on the CRAG benchmark demonstrate that DynaRAG significantly improves accuracy on dynamic questions, while also reducing hallucinations. Our results highlight the importance of dynamic-aware routing and selective tool use in building reliable, real-world question-answering systems.

titulo: AdaptiRAG: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Co-Trained Domain-Specific Fine-Tuned LLMs for Question Answering
autores: V. Venganti; S. R. Rayarao
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies (ICAISET)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for grounding large language model (LLM) outputs in external knowledge, yet existing approaches suffer from two compounding limitations: (1) static retrieval policies that incur unnecessary latency for queries answerable from parametric memory, and (2) independently optimized retrieval and generation components that fail to leverage cross-component learning signals. We present AdaptiRAG, a co-trained framework that integrates a lightweight context classifier for adaptive retrieval gating, a hybrid dense–sparse retrieval pipeline with cross-encoder reranking, and a LoRA-adapted domain-specific LLM whose fine-tuning objective incorporates retrieval quality signals. Evaluated on BioASQ and CUAD benchmarks, AdaptiRAG achieves F1 scores of 73.8% and 71.4% respectively, representing improvements of +12.7 and +13.2 percentage points over naive RAG baselines. The adaptive gating mechanism reduces P95 retrieval latency by 43% and GPU memory consumption is reduced by 48% through QLoRA 4-bit quantization compared to full fine-tuning, while throughput improves by 2.1× under concurrent query loads. Ablation studies confirm that each component contributes independently and that co-training provides a statistically significant improvement over modular assembly. Our results demonstrate that adaptive retrieval gating combined with co-trained generation is a practical and reproducible path toward high-accuracy, inference-efficient domain QA systems.

titulo: From Similarity to Answerability: Reliable Medical Retrieval via LLM-Driven Utility Distillation

abstract: Medical RAG often underperforms because retrievers optimize semantic similarity instead of whether evidence can actually answer a clinical question. titulo: Research and Implementation of Large Language Model Retrieval-Augmented Generation Technology
autores: X. Wang; X. Li; H. Wang
venue: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Electronics and Computer Technology (ICCECT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising technique to enhance their capabilities. This paper delves into the foundational principles and framework of RAG, examining the retrieval-generation process and key modules such as loading, indexing, storage, querying, and evaluation. It also discusses critical technologies underpinning RAG systems, including data partitioning, retrieval algorithms, and generation processes, while presenting several typical implementation frameworks. Finally, we explore potential applications of RAG across various domains and outline future research directions, such as enhancing retrieval efficiency, enabling dynamic knowledge updates, optimizing performance in low-resource environments, and more. Overall, as technology continues to advance, RAG is poised to play an increasingly significant role in practical applications.

titulo: IRG-RAG: An Iterative Reflective Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation Method for Chinese Medicine
autores: J. Zhang; L. Ma; H. Liu; B. An; Q. Sun
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold significant potential in the medical domain but are hindered by the “hallucination” phenomenon, where generated content may be plausible but factually incorrect. Retrieval-Augmented Generation has emerged as an effective paradigm to mitigate this by integrating external knowledge, and gradually migrates to storing and retrieving relevant information within graph structure. Currently, most Graph RAG methods in medical domain face critical limitations such as semantic poverty of the graph and the fragility of the retrieval process. We propose IRG-RAG, an Iterative Reflective Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework tailored for Chinese medical question-answering, focuses on addressing these two key challenges. Our framework introduces a knowledge-enhanced graph construction method, enriching edges with contextual descriptions to endow the graph with richer semantic information. Additionally, we propose an iterative reflective retrieval strategy, which dynamically travels on the graph to retrieve relevant information, backtracks from ineffective paths to reduce noise, and incorporates negative feedback to guide subsequent explorations, mimicking humanlike problem-solving. Experiments on CMExam and CMB-Exam datasets demonstrate that our method significantly enhances the reliability of the model's answer, offering a robust solution to hallucination in domain-specific applications. Codes and data will be available at https://github.com/Damon1Zhang/IRG-RAG.

titulo: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Document-Based Question Answering

titulo: AI-Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Medical Question-Answering Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: A. R. Faridi; Keshvi; F. Masood
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Multimedia, Signal Processing and Communication Technologies (IMPACT)
abstract: Precise medical question-and-answer (QA) systems are essential for clinical decision-making, medical education, and patient care because they provide quick and precise medical information. With immense progress made, high accuracy in medical QA continues to be challenging due to biomedical information complexity and specialty. To solve these issues, this study systematically investigates other state-of-the-art Large Language Model (LLM) prompting strategies as well as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods. The main objective of this paper is to thoroughly investigate and contrast the performance of several methods on the MedMCQA dataset-a well-known medical QA benchmark having about $\mathbf{4, 1 0 0}$ multiple-choice questions on diverse medical topics-such as zero-shot prompting, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, TF-IDF with XGBoost baseline, fine-tuned PubMed-BERT, and three RAG variants (Naive RAG, Query Expansion, and Answer Expansion). Our results show significant performance differences between methods. The standard TF-IDF+XGBoost baseline achieved low accuracy $(32.07 \%)$, while fine-tuned PubMedBERT boosted to $\mathbf{4 4. 0 \%}$. LLM-based prompting yielded significant improvements, particularly for OpenAI's GPT-4 in a zero-shot setup $(80.13 \%)$. But RAG methods significantly surpassed all other methodology, Answer Expansion-based RAG achieving the highest accuracy of about 85%. This research highlights the high promise of retrieval-enhanced methods in medical QA, calling for broader adoption and continued research on RAG frameworks, specifically those incorporating Answer Expansion, in clinical informatics applications.

titulo: A Concise GNN-LLM Alignment Framework for Knowledge-Enhanced Medical Question Answering
autores: C. Song; X. Chen; H. Zhang; R. Hu; W. Liang
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Knowledge Graph based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) technology is an effective method to improve the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in medical question answering tasks. However, there is an inherent difference between structured knowledge graphs and sequential LLMs. The existing method of converting triples of knowledge graph into text through predefined templates leads to loss of structural information and excessive context length, resulting in alignment difficulties between the two. In this paper, we propose a GNN-LLM Aligned Medical knowledge QuestionAnswering model (GLAM-QA). The model first pretrains a GNN to extract structural information from the knowledge graph, realizes the interactive fusion of graph representations and LLM vocabulary embeddings through a cross attention layer, and then generates graph tokens via a projector for input to the LLM. It can retain graph structural information without finetuning the LLM and provide accurate and concise answers. Experiments on three public datasets show that compared with five comparative algorithms, the proposed GLAM-QA achieves better performance in BertScore, F1-Score, and BLEU-1 metrics. This research provides an effective solution to the alignment problem between knowledge graphs and LLMs, and improves the accuracy and practicality of medical question answering systems.

titulo: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Intelligent Question Answering of Enterprise Rules and Regulations
autores: G. Chen
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Computer Network, Electronic and Automation (ICCNEA)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of large volume and frequent updates of enterprise rules and regulations documents, low efficiency of traditional static document retrieval, and susceptibility to misunderstanding, an intelligent question answering system for rules and regulations based on large language models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology is designed. The core contribution lies in the optimization of the retrieval stage: a clause-number-aware adaptive two-level chunking strategy is proposed to ensure semantic integrity; a dual-path hybrid retrieval architecture combining BM25 keyword search and BGE vector retrieval is designed; and a query-type-driven weighted reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) algorithm is introduced for adaptive fusion of retrieval results. For multi-turn dialogue scenarios, a query completion mechanism combining rule-based routing and LLM-based rewriting is designed. The system is built on the LangChain framework for document processing and workflow orchestration, uses Ollama for local deployment of the Qwen3.5:2B model for answer generation, employs Redis cache for response speed optimization, and uses Streamlit to build a visual interactive interface. A test set containing 120 questions covering five types of policy scenarios (attendance, performance, reimbursement, etc.) is constructed. Experimental results show that hybrid retrieval achieves a hit rate of 95.0% under standard queries and 85.0% under colloquial queries. Compared with single-path FAISS retrieval, it improves by 2.5 percentage points under standard queries and decreases by 7.5 percentage points under colloquial queries. Notably, in colloquial scenarios, Whoosh returns low-relevance but non-empty results that interfere with the fused ranking, causing the hybrid hit rate (85.0%) to fall below that of FAISS alone (92.5%); this is a known limitation and a key direction for future optimization, although the first-hit rate remains above 70%). The question answering accuracy reaches 87.5%, and the response time after cache hit is below 0.1 seconds. The system verifies the effectiveness of the hybrid retrieval RAG architecture in enterprise rules and regulations QA scenarios, providing a feasible path for transforming enterprise document management from static storage to intelligent services.

autores: Y. Yao; X. Lyu

abstract: Open-domain table question answering (OD-TQA) aims to retrieve relevant evidence tables from a large-scale table corpus based on a given question and subsequently generate accurate answers. However, semantically similar queries often result in highly redundant retrieval outputs, and the conventional two stage pipeline: retrieval followed by answer generation, tends to suffer from error propagation, ultimately degrading both retrieval precision and answer quality. To address these challenges, we propose a Multi-Agent Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for OD-TQA. Specifically, we design a Refiner Agent to augment the semantic diversity of the input question by generating varied paraphrases, thereby enriching the informative of the question. To overcome the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in encoding structured table data, we transform tables into textual descriptions to better align with LLM embeddings. Furthermore, we introduce a Filter Agent and a Solver Agent to mitigate error accumulation by filtering irrelevant tables and performing fine-grained reasoning over the retained evidence. These three agents operate in a sequential and collaborative manner, forming a robust pipeline for the OD-TQA task. Experimental results on two OD-TQA benchmarks demonstrate that our method substantially improves answer accuracy, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

titulo: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Document Link Structure for Multi-Hop Web Question Answering
autores: S. Mazaheri; A. Dadashzadeh; A. N. Alankesh; R. Dividino
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Collaborative Advances in Software and COmputiNg (CASCON)
abstract: The Web is a vast and intricate network of interconnected information sources. While traditional Web search engines have long enabled users to search through billions of linked pages using keyword matching, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) marks a fundamental shift in how we search for and process online information. Organizations are increasingly adopting LLM-based solutions, particularly retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), to automate information extraction from Web documents, going beyond simple keyword matching to understand semantic relationships between content. However, while RAG excels at reasoning within a single context window, it faces significant challenges in multi-hop inference, particularly in Web search scenarios where information must be gathered and processed from different sources. Graph-augmented RAGs address these limitations by leveraging graph-structured data to capture relationships between documents and enable more context-aware responses. This work investigates whether LLMs, enhanced with Web document-level graph-augmented RAG, can better automate the process of navigating and synthesizing information from complex Web documents. Our approach exploits both the textual content of Web documents and their hyperlink structure to create a comprehensive framework for Web-based information navigation and synthesis. We evaluate our approach on benchmark a multi-hop question-answering datasets, and demonstrate measurable improvements in the retrieval performance of information synthesis when compared to baseline approaches. The code and prompt templates are available at https://github.com/mehrshaad/Multi-hop-WebRAG.

titulo: Document Embeddings Enhance Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well in many NLP tasks but frequently generate inaccurate information in the biomedical domain, due to hallucination issues. However, naive RAG encounters challenges in effectively utilizing retrieved content, particularly in specialized domains like biomedicine. LLMs often struggle to integrate retrieved content as irrelevant information can interfere with the model’s judgment. Even if relevant documents are retrieved, the model may be unable to accurately comprehend and utilize the domain-specific features due to its inherent knowledge limitations. DEEB-RAG uses MedCPT to generate document embeddings and these embeddings are then aligned with the LLM’s semantic space using a two-stage training process on a simple projector. Experimental results on biomedical QA datasets show that DEEB-RAG improves accuracy, with an average performance increase of 2.3% over naive RAG. This demonstrates DEEB-RAG’s ability to mitigate the challenges of utilizing complex biomedical information, thereby enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of LLMs in biomedical domain.

titulo: MuaLLM: A Multimodal Large Language Model Agent for Circuit Design Assistance with Hybrid Contextual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: P. Abbineni; S. Aldowaish; C. Liechty; S. Noorzad; A. G. Ghalati; M. Fayazi
venue: 2026 31st Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASP-DAC)
abstract: Conducting a comprehensive literature review is crucial for advancing circuit design methodologies. However, the rapid influx of state-of-the-art research, inconsistent data representation, and the complexity of optimizing circuit design objectives (e.g. power consumption) make this task significantly challenging. Traditional manual search methods are inefficient, time-consuming, and lack the reasoning capabilities required for synthesizing complex circuits. In this paper, we propose MuaLLM, an open-source multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) agent for circuit design assistance that integrates a hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework with an adaptive vector database of circuit design research papers. Unlike conventional LLMs, the MuaLLM agent employs a Reason + Act (ReAct) workflow for iterative reasoning, goal-setting, and multi-step information retrieval. It functions as a question-answering design assistant, capable of interpreting complex queries and providing reasoned responses grounded in circuit literature. Its multimodal capabilities enable processing of both textual and visual data, facilitating more efficient and comprehensive analysis. The system dynamically adapts using intelligent search tools, automated document retrieval from the internet, and real-time database updates. Unlike conventional approaches constrained by model context limits, MuaLLM decouples retrieval from inference, enabling scalable reasoning over arbitrarily large corpora. At the maximum context length supported by standard LLMs, MuaLLM remains up to 10x less costly and 1.6x faster while maintaining the same accuracy. This allows rapid, no-human-in-the-loop database generation, overcoming the bottleneck of simulation-based dataset creation for circuits. To evaluate MuaLLM, we introduce two custom benchmarks: RAG-250, targeting retrieval and citation performance, and Reasoning-100 (Reas-100), focused on multistep reasoning in circuit design. MuaLLM achieves $\mathbf{9 0. 1 \%}$ recall on RAG-250, highlighting strong multimodal retrieval and citation accuracy. On Reas-100, it reaches 86.8% accuracy, demonstrating robust reasoning capabilities on complex design queries.

venue: 2026 41st Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) analysis is a critical methodology for risk assessment in the chemical process industry. However, the valuable engineering knowledge generated from these analyses often resides in static, semi-structured documents, hindering effective retrieval and reuse. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches struggle in this domain due to semantic mismatches during retrieval and the lack of structured reasoning in generation. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel framework for intelligent question answering on HAZOP reports, named the Domain-Adaptive and Reranking-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (DR-RAG) framework. The framework features three key innovations: a domain-adaptive retriever fine-tuned via contrastive learning with hard negatives to enhance semantic discrimination; a dual-path retrieval strategy combined with cross-encoder reranking to ensure high precision across heterogeneous data; and a JSON Schema-constrained generation module that mandates the Large Language Model to produce structured outputs aligned with HAZOP causal logic. Experimental results on a real-world industrial dataset demonstrate that DR-RAG significantly outperforms baselines, improving context precision from 65.0 percent to 96.7 percent and elevating end-to-end answer accuracy from 1.25 to 1.90 on a 0 to 2 scale. This work offers a robust and scalable solution for automating knowledge engineering in industrial safety.

autores: R. Alsayyed; S. Khelfa; A. Hawash
venue: 2026 ASU International Conference in Emerging Technologies for Sustainability and Intelligent Systems (ICETSIS)
abstract: Hallucinations continue to significantly restrict large language models (LLMs), particularly in fact-finding and knowledge-intensive tasks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which bases model outputs on external knowledge sources, addresses this problem. This study examines the impact of integrating structured knowledge from Wikidata into an LLM-based question-answering pipeline to reduce hallucinated material. The proposed Wikidata-based RAG technique injects this structured context into the LLM prompt before response synthesis by first extracting entities from the input question and then gathering candidate entities and verified attributes from Wikidata. Both the prompt-only baseline models and the Wikidata-grounded RAG system were used to evaluate 80 multi-hop compositional problems. The proposed RAG model is evaluated using four hallucination evaluation methods. The model is evaluated against three prompt-only baselines: the AimonLabs hallucination-detection model, the Vectara HHEM, and an LLM-as-a-Judge rubric. Retrieved-Context Faithfulness (RAGTruth-style evaluation) is assessed using the last evaluation method. (Vectara HHEM: 77.5% vs 38.75% factual replies; AIMON: 60% vs 32.5% factual responses; LLM-as-a-Judge: 75% vs 38.75% factual responses) RAG consistently surpasses the baseline across all four evaluators. 54 of 79 assessed examples had a retrieved-context fidelity of 68.35%. This suggests that the observed frequency of hallucinations is influenced by the evaluation approach used. These results show how fact accuracy may be greatly increased by basing LLMs on structured knowledge from Wikidata. They also show how important it is to have several assessors when studying hallucinations.

titulo: How to Discover Knowledge for FutureG: Contextual RAG and LLM Prompting for O-RAN
autores: N. Conger; N. Scollar; K. Davaslioglu; Y. E. Sagduyu; S. Kompella
venue: 2026 IEEE 23rd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
abstract: We present a retrieval-augmented question answering framework for 5G/6G networks, where the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) has become central to disaggregated, virtualized, and AI-driven wireless systems. While O-RAN enables multi-vendor interoperability and cloud-native deployments, its fast-changing specifications and interfaces pose major challenges for researchers and practitioners. Manual navigation of these complex documents is labor-intensive and error-prone, slowing system design, integration, and deployment. To address this challenge, we adopt Contextual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Contextual RAG), a strategy in which candidate answer choices guide document retrieval and chunk-specific context to improve large language model (LLM) performance. This improvement over traditional RAG achieves more targeted and context-aware retrieval, which improves the relevance of documents passed to the LLM, particularly when the query alone lacks sufficient context for accurate grounding. Our framework is designed for dynamic domains where data evolves rapidly and models must be continuously updated or redeployed, all without requiring LLM fine-tuning. We evaluate this framework using the ORAN-Benchmark-13K dataset, and compare three LLMs, namely, Llama3.2, Qwen2.5-7B, and Qwen3.0-4B, across both Direct Question Answering (Direct Q&A) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies. We show that Contextual RAG consistently improves accuracy over standard RAG and base prompting, while maintaining competitive runtime and CO2 emissions. These results highlight the potential of Contextual RAG to serve as a scalable and effective solution for domain-specific Q&A in O-RAN and broader 5G/6G environments, enabling more accurate interpretation of evolving standards while preserving efficiency and sustainability.

titulo: Speech Retrieval-Augmented Generation without Automatic Speech Recognition
autores: D. J. Min; K. Mundnich; A. Lapastora; E. Soltanmohammadi; S. Ronanki; K. Han
venue: ICASSP 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: One common approach for question answering over speech data is to first transcribe speech using automatic speech recognition (ASR) and then employ text-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on the transcriptions. While this cascaded pipeline has proven effective in many practical settings, ASR errors can propagate to the retrieval and generation steps. To overcome this limitation, we introduce SpeechRAG, a novel framework designed for open-question answering over spoken data. Our proposed approach fine-tunes a pre-trained speech encoder into a speech adapter fed into a frozen large language model (LLM)–based retrieval model. By aligning the embedding spaces of text and speech, our speech retriever directly retrieves audio passages from text-based queries, leveraging the retrieval capacity of the frozen text retriever. Our retrieval experiments on spoken question answering datasets show that direct speech retrieval does not degrade over the text-based baseline, and outperforms the cascaded systems using ASR. For generation, we use a speech language model (SLM) as a generator, conditioned on audio passages rather than transcripts. Without fine-tuning of the SLM, this approach outperforms cascaded text-based models when there is high WER in the transcripts.

titulo: ClauseRouteRAG: A Clause-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for 3GPP Telecommunications Standards
autores: S. Lu; X. Wang; Z. Shao; J. Bai; Z. Xiao; Y. Zhang
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) produces technical specifications with long documents, hierarchical clause structures, and many tables, which makes automated question answering difficult. While Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has improved robustness for knowledge intensive tasks, existing systems can still miss the right clauses in long specifications and may retrieve incomplete evidence for standards questions. This paper presents ClauseRouteRAG, a RAG framework for multiple choice question answering over 3GPP specifications. ClauseRouteRAG first selects a small set of relevant clauses by aggregating evidence from an initial retrieval pass. It then retrieves passages within these clauses using dense retrieval and BM25 with rank fusion. Finally, it reranks the candidate passages using overlap of technical identifiers extracted from the question and the retrieved passages, and it prompts the language model to answer using only the provided evidence. Experiments on TeleQnA Release 17 and Release 18 show that ClauseRouteRAG consistently improves over LLM only baselines and a naive RAG pipeline, reaching an overall accuracy of 0.849 on TeleQnA under the default setting.

titulo: Towards Developing a Multimodal Chat Assistant for University Stakeholders: RAG-Based Approach
autores: M. A. Hanif Shaikh; A. Al Shafi
venue: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: University stakeholders often face difficulties in accessing timely and reliable information, especially in developing countries, where there are very few intelligent support systems. Existing rule-based chatbots are unable to handle complex, domain-specific queries and are not well-equipped to adapt to evolving institutional policies. As a fill-in-the-gap solution, we present the multimodal university chatbot with retrieval-augmented generation. The system combines the large language model with semantic retrieval to produce context-based responses from institution-centric resources, such as the university handbook. The system accepts text and image queries through the vision-language model and applies quantized inference for rapid deployment on constrained hardware. A scalable backend built with FastAPI, adjoined with a responsive frontend developed with Next.js, ensures real-time usability. Our multimodal evaluation demonstrates that the system maintains strong satisfaction scores across both text and image queries, despite increased response time for visual inputs. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation shows that hallucination is reduced from 31.7% to 6.6% in our proposed RAG-based system, confirming the effectiveness of retrieval grounding.

titulo: CRAG-VQA: Context Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Hallucination-Resistant Knowledge based Visual Question Answering
autores: T. G; S. P
venue: 2026 Fourth International Conference on Secure Cyber Computing and Communications (ICSCCC)
abstract: Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering (KB- VQA) extends beyond visual perception by requiring external knowledge and reasoning, making it particularly susceptible to hallucinations in Large Language Model (LLM)–driven systems. These hallucinated responses that may be logically inconsistent, primarily due to the absence of explicit answer validation mechanisms and lack of contextual prompting methods. CRAG- VQA, a Contextual RAG framework for KB-VQA with Hallucination Mitigation is proposed to resolve the above issues. This work handles knowledge-intensive visual queries that require reasoning beyond directly observable image features. CRAG-VQA dynamically retrieves and integrates multimodal and knowledge- grounded context—including visual evidence, semantic attributes, and external knowledge sources—conditioned on the input image and query. The proposed framework employs contextual prompting to explicitly ground LLM reasoning in retrieved evidence, while a consistency-based verification mechanism aligns generated answers with both visual cues and knowledge context. By decoupling knowledge retrieval from answer generation and enforcing contextual alignment, CRAG-VQA effectively reduces unsupported inferences and factual drift. The proposed system minimizes Hallucination using Consistency Checking to emphasize visually supported information while minimizing reasoning errors and dependence on unconstrained parametric knowledge. Experimental evaluation on standard VQA benchmarks confirms notable gains in accuracy for multimodal reasoning in KB-VQA.

venue: 2025 IEEE 6th International Conference on Computer, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: The article discusses how the Knowledge Graphs(KGs) technology can be applied to Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle Advanced Persistent Threats (APT) in cybersecurity. APT-ArgusQA employs First and Second-Order RAG Enhancement strategies, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of LLMs in the APT domain by integrating APT Knowledge Graph nodes, neighboring nodes, and relational information. It also demonstrates how to fine-tune pre-trained models provided by OpenAI to suit tasks in APT knowledge-based question answering. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated through a series of experiments. The discussion revolved around the potential of KGs in continuously learning and adapting to new threats, as well as their prospects in improving the interpretability of decision-making in cybersecurity.
