abstract: Large language model (LLM)–based conversational systems are constrained by fixed context windows, limiting their ability to retain and retrieve information from extended dialogue histories. titulo: Quality Outweighs Quantity: Advancing Medical Question Answering with RAG-MCP Muti-Agent LLM Framework and Curated Knowledge Databases

abstract: Medical multiple-choice question (MCQ) answering requires specialized domain knowledge, multi-step clinical reasoning, and ability to discriminate among closely related distractor options. The proposed architecture employs an administrator agent that performs domain-specific task routing and coordinates five specialized medical agents-Physiology, Pathology, Clinical Medicine, Treatment and Pharmacology, and Public Health-integrating their outputs through weighted consensus for final answer selection. Critically, this study demonstrates that knowledge database quality significantly outweighs quantity in RAG systems: curating high-quality question subsets from knowledge data yields substantially greater performance gains than utilizing entire unfiltered knowledge datasets. Evaluated on MedMCQA and MedQA-USMLE benchmarks using GPT-oss 21B and LLaMA 4Scout 17B base models without fine-tuning, the MCP-based multiagent framework achieves approximately 5% accuracy improvement (71-75%) over single-agent baselines (66-70%). Furthermore, employing only top-500 highest-quality curated questions in RAG knowledge database boosts accuracy to nearly 80%, representing $\boldsymbol{\sim} \mathbf{1 0 \%}$ overall improvement. Ablation studies confirm multi-agent consensus mechanisms provide 1.0-2.4% additional gains beyond retrieval augmentation alone, while scaling analysis reveals optimal performance at 11-13% curated knowledge data. These findings establish that domain specialization, structured agent collaboration, and strategic data curation collectively enhance both accuracy and interpretability in medical reasoning systems, offering practical pathway for deploying reliable clinical decision support without computationally expensive model fine-tuning.

We start from openly available models and resources, adapt and finetune them to our target - Romanian question answering with information retrieval - and then release our solutions publicly at https://github.com/Andrei481/RomanianChatbot.

titulo: TenderGraphRAG: An Enhancement Framework for Question Answering Systems Based on a Tendering and Bidding Knowledge Graph
autores: R. Chu; C. Zheng; L. Xu; H. He; J. Li
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Applications (ICCIA)
abstract: In specialized domains such as public tendering and bidding, Large Language Models (LLMs) often suffer from factual ‘hallucinations’ and knowledge limitations, hindering their reliability in question-answering systems. To address this, we introduce TenderGraphRAG, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework built upon a high-fidelity, domain-specific knowledge graph. The cornerstone of our framework is the Human-in-the-Loop Collaborative Relation Ontology Evolution (HLC-ROE) paradigm. This novel approach synergizes LLM-driven schema discovery with expert validation in a closed loop, enabling the rapid and accurate construction of the domain knowledge graph. At query time, TenderGraphRAG employs a hybrid retrieval strategy, fusing structured graph path traversal, sparse keyword (BM25) search, and dense vector search. Experimental results on our self-constructed tendering and bidding QA dataset show that TenderGraphRAG substantially outperforms a spectrum of baselines, from traditional keyword-based (BM25-RAG) and standard vector-based (NaiveRAG) systems to advanced graph-enhanced frameworks. Notably, compared to the graph-enhanced LightRAG system, our framework achieves an 11.4 percent higher accuracy (0.824 vs. 0.740) and a 17.0 percent higher completeness score (0.908 vs. 0.776). These results demonstrate that deep domain specialization, anchored by a high-fidelity knowledge graph, is a highly effective strategy for enhancing the reasoning and factual grounding of RAG systems in complex professional fields.

titulo: Addressing LLM Challenges: A Hybrid Framework for Duplicate Question Detection
autores: H. -H. Hsu; N. -F. Huang
venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Detecting similar or duplicate texts or questions is a critical subtask in information retrieval. Despite the remarkable advancements achieved by large language models (LLMs) in the question answering (QA) domain in recent years, challenges such as unreliable responses caused by LLM hallucinations and outdated information have highlighted the continued importance of information retrieval techniques. The integration of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with LLMs has mitigated some of these limitations, enhancing the reliability of applying LLMs to domain-specific knowledge. This paper uses Chinese educational questions as a case study and introduces an innovative framework for duplicate question detection, termed the Balanced Duplicate Question Detector (BDQD). The BDQD incorporates multiple extensible detectors and a machine learning-based balancer. Experimental results reveal that detecting duplicate questions involves an inherent trade-off between precision and recall. Logistic regression proves effective in balancing thresholds across different detectors, establishing a more stable and reliable standard for duplicate question determination. Finally, we propose a hybrid QA framework that considers both cost and efficiency, integrating the lightweight question retrieval architecture developed in this study with RAG and LLMs. This framework offers practical recommendations for building robust and efficient QA systems.

titulo: Cost-Aware Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Evidence Selection for Source-Grounded Healthcare LLM QA
autores: R. Balamurugan; K. T. A. Sekar; P. Nanjundan
venue: 2026 International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies (TQCEBT)
abstract: Evidence-grounded question answering (QA) is critical in healthcare, where responses must be traceable to trusted sources and produced in a verifiable format. This paper presents a local, evidence-grounded healthcare QA pipeline built on the MedQuAD dataset, a collection of question-answer pairs curated from National Institutes of Health (NIH) resources. The pipeline retrieves a top- $\boldsymbol{k}$ candidate pool using a hybrid scoring function that combines lexical relevance (BM25) and latent semantic similarity (LSA), then selects a compact evidence subset of size mfor downstream generation. The main contribution is a costaware evidence subset selection method formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) objective that maximizes summed relevance while penalizing redundancy and a token-based cost proxy. Three selection strategies are compared: (i) a ranking baseline (Top- $m$), (ii) a relevance-diversity QUBO selector $(\gamma=0)$, and (iii) a cost-aware QUBO selector $(\gamma>0)$. A locally hosted LLM generates answers constrained to a strict JSON schema, enabling deterministic validation of output structure and evidence identifiers. Experimental results on representative healthcare queries show that the cost-aware QUBO reduces mean evidence cost and redundancy relative to Top- $\boldsymbol{m}$ while maintaining comparable relevance and full schema compliance. A trade-off analysis further highlights how optimization-based selection improves evidence efficiency with minimal impact on end-to-end latency, supporting practical local deployment of grounded healthcare QA systems.

titulo: Query-Aware Adaptive Chunking for RAG in Mental Health and Well-Being Policy Question Answering
autores: P. Kondapalli; M. Z. R. Saimon; S. Das Polok; G. S. Chakraborty; M. A. Abrar; S. Batra
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Practices in Technology and Management (ICIPTM)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an effective approach for question answering over domain-specific documents by grounding large language model outputs in external knowledge sources. However, most existing RAG pipelines rely on fixed-size document chunking during retrieval, which may not be optimal for diverse query types commonly encountered in policy documents. In particular, questions related to mental health and well-being policies range from factual definitions to procedural and role-based inquiries, each requiring different levels of contextual information. In this paper, we propose a query-aware adaptive chunking strategy for RAG that dynamically selects chunk sizes based on the inferred query intent. Instead of modifying or fine-tuning the underlying language model, the proposed approach introduces a lightweight retrieval-time adaptation mechanism that aligns retrieved context with the informational needs of different query types. The method is evaluated on mental health and wellbeing policy documents published by the World Health Organization, focusing on workplace-related guidelines and recommendations. Evaluation is conducted at both the retrieval and generation levels. Retrieval performance is assessed using Hit@5 and answer coverage metrics, while generation quality is evaluated through manual human assessment using a 3-point Likert scale measuring relevancy, faithfulness, and completeness. Experimental results show that while fixed and adaptive RAG approaches achieve comparable retrieval performance, the adaptive strategy consistently improves generation quality, particularly for procedural and role-based policy questions. These findings demonstrate that query-aware adaptive chunking can enhance the effectiveness of RAG systems in healthcare policy question answering without requiring additional model training.

titulo: RAGRouter: A Retrieval-Augmented Routing Strategy Model for Large Language Model
autores: J. He
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Data Mining (ICDM)
abstract: To address the critical challenge of balancing computational cost and response quality in large language model (LLM) deployments, this paper introduces RAGRouter, an innovative routing strategy model based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The widespread application of LLMs in natural language generation, dialogue systems, and question-answering faces a fundamental trade-off: larger models yield higher quality but incur prohibitive costs, while smaller models often prove inadequate for complex queries. Existing routing strategies, though aiming to optimize resource efficiency via dynamic model selection, frequently suffer from misallocated resources and a mismatch between model capabilities and task demands, further limited by insufficient semantic understanding and underutilized syntactic features. Our proposed RAGRouter framework tackles these limitations by achieving accurate query difficulty assessment and efficient model selection through sophisticated feature fusion and knowledge enhancement. Specifically, the model extracts deep contextual semantic features and constructs syntactic representations from dependency parse trees. A cross-modal attention mechanism subsequently fuses these semantic and syntactic elements into a holistic query representation. Furthermore, the integration of RAG technology builds a vector knowledge base, which uses K-Nearest Neighbors retrieval to find historically similar queries and their routing labels, thereby generating context-enhanced prompts for fine-tuning the QWEN-7B model. To bolster generalization and address data imbalance, we also propose a data augmentation technique using semantic and structural transformations, complemented by a perplexity-based dynamic sampling strategy that employs weighted and oversampling methods to improve robustness on complex tasks. Experimental results on public benchmarks demonstrate that RAGRouter significantly enhances the accuracy and stability of routing decisions, substantially reducing the invocation rate of powerful models like GPT-4 while maintaining high response quality. The model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, showing superior adaptability and generalization in mathematical reasoning and knowledge-intensive question-answering, thus providing a scalable and effective technical pathway for optimizing resource efficiency in practical LLM applications. titulo: Trigger as Entity: Backdoor Attacks to Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
autores: Z. Zheng; Y. -J. Choi; C. Huang; H. Cao; S. Tian; T. Pei
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
abstract: Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has achieved remarkable success in refining the outputs of Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling them to integrate relational and multi-hop knowledge into context-aware responses by constructing a knowledge graph from an external database. In this paper, we focus on the underexplored security risks arising from the external database, and propose the first backdoor attacks against the graph-based RAG of LLMs. Specifically, attackers insert the backdoor into the knowledge graph as entities by poisoning a carefully crafted corpus into the external database, thereby causing LLMs to output attacker-desired answers for trigger-containing queries while preserving correct answers for others. The attacks are formulated as a minimax problem, whose solution is a poison corpus. Powered by the chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities of LLMs, we propose a new strategy to solve the minimax problem. We craft retrieval text to insert triggers into the knowledge graph as entities, exploit hijacking text to redirect LLMs’ attention toward attacker-desired answers, and finally link the hijacking text to the triggers so that it serves as context only for trigger-containing queries. In addition, our attacks involve three types of triggers, including word-level, topic-level, and semantic-level, with progressively increasing stealthiness. Empirical results across multiple knowledge databases and language models indicate that the proposed attacks achieve the desired attack performance. Our findings highlight the substantial risks in LLM applications (e.g., chatbots and agents) built on graph-based RAG systems.

titulo: Analysis of Methods for Evaluating Responses of LLMs in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: K. Traykov; Y. Kolova
venue: 2025 International Conference on Big Data, Knowledge and Control Systems Engineering (BdKCSE)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly employed to provide domain-specific, context-aware answers by combining large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge sources. In this paper, we investigate methods for assessing changes in RAG-generated answers before and after an update of the underlying knowledge base. We report experimental results across different models, highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and biases in automated comparative evaluation. The findings provide insights into practical approaches for response quality assessment in evolving RAG systems, offering a foundation for more robust and scalable evaluation pipelines in real-world applications.

titulo: PopRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Using Consistent LandScan Population Data for Humanitarian Crisis Response
autores: C. Stipek; N. Nukavarapu; V. Lebakula; S. Walters; S. Basford; A. Faxon; C. Silva; M. Urban; G. Lakshmanan; S. Srinivasan; A. Sadovnik; S. Swaminathan

abstract: Understanding and characterizing populations at a global scale is critical to many tasks such as humanitarian response, disease modeling, among others. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have enabled the use of large language models (LLMs) to provide advanced capabilities to assist in data acquisition tasks as the volume of data has been increasing. However, LLMs can become outdated due to the date at which the model was trained. To address this, attention has turned to the development of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to improve upon traditional LLM chatbots for domain-specific tasks. While there are various domains in which LLMs and RAGs have revolutionized, geospatial data acquisition, particularly for population information, has remained under-studied. titulo: Traceability-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering for Fuzzy Queries in Engineering O&M
autores: X. Zhou; D. Song; Y. Zheng; T. Xiao; Y. Cao; J. Wu
venue: 2026 6th International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science (ISCTIS)
abstract: Engineering operation-and-maintenance (O&M) workflows accumulate large volumes of technical knowledge, including equipment manuals, technical standards, defect cases, maintenance records, and troubleshooting experience. However, these assets are often scattered across personal computers, paper archives, and heterogeneous business systems, making knowledge access slow and reuse inefficient. In practice, field engineers frequently issue fuzzy queries by describing symptoms, scenarios, or incomplete device names rather than using standardized technical terminology. To this end, we propose TraceRAG, a traceability-aware retrieval-augmented question answering framework for fuzzy-query answering over engineering knowledge bases. The framework integrates Query Alignment, hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder reranking, and evidence-grounded generation with per-stage trace logging. Query Alignment combines intent-oriented template expansion and LLM-based rewriting while preserving the original query to reduce semantic drift. Retrieved candidates are then fused and reranked before answer generation, and supporting evidence is explicitly exposed to improve answer transparency and reduce hallucination risk. We evaluate the method on a 1,131-item electrical engineering knowledge benchmark together with 678 synthetic fuzzy queries. The results show that cross-encoder reranking improves canonical-query MRR@10 by +0.082 absolute over hybrid retrieval, while Query Alignment with reranking achieves the best fuzzy-query MRR@10 of 0.660. These results indicate that TraceRAG improves fuzzy-query knowledge access on the reported benchmark and has potential relevance for O&Moriented technical knowledge retrieval and reuse.

venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Large-language model optimization for a particular application is crucial and challenging in natural language processing. titulo: Comparative Analysis of RAG Frameworks for Better Private Question Answering
autores: S. K. Sah; P. Gupta; G. R; G. M
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abstract: In the present paper, the comparative analysis of current Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks is provided with the main emphasis on effectiveness and safety of these tools in the context of the question-answer task in a private setting. RAG is a solution to the core problem of factual error in Large Language Models (LLMs) in order to base their responses on external, updated knowledge bases. Nevertheless, the fact that it can apply to sensitive, proprietary data raises a new, more serious issue: the very mechanism that makes RAG effective, the access to an outside knowledge base, introduces new security vulnerabilities. In this regard, we perform a thorough literature review of more than 20 recent scholarly articles, describing basic and state-of-the-art RAG structures. We suggest a multi-layered assessment framework including the usual performance-based measures (latency, throughput, accuracy) and the retrieval and generation quality-specific measures (Precision at k, Faithfulness, Hallucination scores). We critically evaluate the notable RAG systems, such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack, in terms of architectural design, scalability, and the compatibility with privacy-sensitive deployments. We conduct a thorough evaluation of major privacy-protective methods, such as Differential Privacy (DP), Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC), and Homomorphic Encryption (HE) and measure privacy-utility trade-offs they present. The analysis points out that, although the specialized architectures such as DPSparseVoteRAG provide promising solutions, the enforcement of strong privacy guarantees can be very costly in terms of performance. It is a useful resource to developers and researchers interested in designing secure and performant RAG systems to support sensitive applications, giving a best practices overview and defining essential future research directions in privacy-preserving AI. The current work includes a comparative analysis of three popular RAG models, namely, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack based on their architectural appropriateness to private question answering and not on controlled experimental benchmarking. The scope of evaluation focuses on performance features, deployment, and privacy-sensitive integration features. The key results include a definite privacy-utility trade-off in which strict privacy assurances by mechanisms like Differential Privacy, Secure Multi-Party Computation and Homomorphic Encryption lead to quantifiable losses in latency, throughput or accuracy of the answers.

abstract: This paper presents a retrieval-augmented generation–based framework aimed at achieving efficient and accurate knowledge acquisition and question answering within private knowledge base environments. titulo: slAIces: an LLM Chatbot for Simplifying Experiments with the SLICES-RI
autores: D. Kefalas; S. Christakis; S. Fdida; N. Makris; I. Syrigos; V. Passas; T. Korakis
venue: 2024 IFIP Networking Conference (IFIP Networking)
abstract: SLICES-RI is the outcome of several years of evolution of the concept of a networking test platform, that has recently transformed into a scientific instrument for the assessment of new research challenges in the Digital Infrastructures domain. Making large-scale scientific instruments easily accessible has always been challenging, often hindered by the complexity of the underlying platforms, the size and diversity of resources and the low-level settings that experimenters need to configure. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence(AI) have ignited a wave of innovation, inspiring companies, professionals, and researchers to incorporate chatbot assistants into their projects. titulo: MedLTRAG: Co-Augmentation of Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models for Long-tail Medical Question Answering
autores: M. Wu; X. Wang; J. Sun; B. Wei
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Despite the remarkable success of large language models (LLMs), their ability to effectively incorporate long-tail domain knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. In specialized domains such as medicine, reliable question answering requires structured and precise knowledge that is often poorly captured by purely parametric representations. We observe that the key limitation of existing LLM-based approaches to long-tail medical QA lies in a misalignment between how specialized knowledge is represented and how it is accessed during inference. To address this limitation, we propose MedLTRAG, a framework that tightly integrates LLMs with knowledge graphs (KGs) to enable grounded medical reasoning. MedLTRAG follows an offline-to-online paradigm: domain-specific KGs are first constructed from medical literature to encode specialized expertise, and are then selectively retrieved at inference time to support reasoning through a multi-stage beam search mechanism. By externalizing long-tail knowledge into structured representations and explicitly incorporating them into the inference process, MedLTRAG reduces the brittleness of purely parametric reasoning. Extensive experiments on multiple disease-centric medical QA benchmarks demonstrate that MedLTRAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Beyond empirical improvements, this work outlines a generalizable paradigm for integrating structured knowledge with LLMs, offering a principled pathway toward robust reasoning in knowledge-intensive, long-tail domains.

abstract: Maintenance of medium voltage switchgears is a complex task that requires extensive expertise. abstract: Recent advances in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) have allowed large language models (LLMs) to consult external knowledge bases to overcome their parameterized knowledge limitations. To address this issue, we propose STAR (Self-Knowledge and Targeted Augmented Retrieval), a simplified two-branch retrieval-augmented question-answering framework composed of two main components: a Self-Knowledge Branch and an optimized Passage Retrieval Branch. In our design, the system first checks whether the question can be answered using the LLM’s existing knowledge. If not, it retrieves passages and then ranks smaller segments of those passages based on their relevance. This approach reduces the query’s reliance on extraneous content, lowers computational costs, and offers a more direct route to accurate solutions. Empirical results on benchmarks such as Natural Questions and TriviaQA show that our simplified approach matches or exceeds the accuracy of multi-module counterparts while operating at a fraction of the complexity.

abstract: We present knowledge-aware iterative retrieval (KAIR), an innovative framework for LLM agents driven by large language models (LLMs) that iteratively refines user queries and filters contextual evidence using dynamically evolving knowledge to facilitate better systems. A key feature of this system is its separation of external information sources from an internal knowledge cache, which is continuously updated to guide query formulation and evidence selection. This design reduces the risk of biased feedback loops and facilitates dynamic, trackable exploration of search paths, balancing the exploration of diverse information with precision through autonomous agent decision-making. abstract: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering (KB-VQA) necessitates retrieving external knowledge to answer questions about images. titulo: ReRead: Retrieval-Guided Efficient Reading for Long-Context Question Answering
autores: J. Ling; W. Bao; Z. Zhong; T. Zhou; J. Wang
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA)
abstract: Long-context question-answering tasks require models to locate a small amount of scattered evidence within lengthy, sparse, and noisy inputs, and to integrate information across multiple fragments during reading. Existing recurrent reading and memory-updating methods provide an effective paradigm for handling ultra-long contexts by processing the context chunk by chunk while continuously maintaining an intermediate memory. However, these methods typically adopt a complete sequential reading strategy, in which all chunks are treated equally and fed into the memory-updating process. As the context length increases, this strategy leads to rapidly growing large language model (LLM) invocations, token consumption, and inference time, while also increasing the risk that irrelevant information contaminates the memory state. To better balance answer quality and inference cost, we propose ReRead, a retrieval-guided selective reading method for long-context question-answering. ReRead first divides the long context into ordered reading units and performs question-aware hybrid retrieval using BM25 and a dense retriever, then merges and deduplicates the retrieved candidates, and reorganizes them into a selective reading sequence according to their original order in the context. Finally, the model progressively updates its natural-language memory along this sequence and generates the final answer based on the resulting memory state. Experiments on RULER-HQA and various long-context generalization tasks demonstrate that ReRead maintains answer quality comparable to complete sequential recurrent reading, while effectively reducing LLM invocations, token consumption, and end-to-end inference time, achieving a superior efficiency-performance trade-off.

abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) exhibit strong reasoning abilities, but their reliance on parametric knowledge limits factual accuracy. Specifically, we first leverage a LRM to generate deliberate thinking, then select an action from a predefined action space (Search andFinish). Further analysis highlights its strong reflective ability to recognize errors and revise its reasoning trajectory. Our study enhances LRMs’ factuality while effectively integrating robust reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

titulo: Efficient Multi-Hop Question Answering Over Knowledge Graphs via LLM Planning and Embedding-Guided Search
autores: M. Shrestha; E. Kim
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs remains computationally challenging due to the combinatorial explosion of possible reasoning paths. Recent approaches rely on expensive Large Language Model (LLM) inference for both entity linking and path ranking, limiting their practical deployment. Additionally, LLM-generated answers often lack verifiable grounding in structured knowledge. We present two complementary hybrid algorithms that address both efficiency and verifiability: (1) LLM-Guided Planning that uses a single LLM call to predict relation sequences executed via breadthfirst search, achieving near-perfect accuracy (micro-F1 $>0.90$) while ensuring all answers are grounded in the knowledge graph, and (2) Embedding-Guided Neural Search that eliminates LLM calls entirely by fusing text and graph embeddings through a lightweight 6.7M-parameter edge scorer, achieving over $100 \times$ speedup with competitive accuracy. Through knowledge distillation, we compress planning capability into a 4B-parameter model that matches large-model performance at zero API cost. Evaluation on MetaQA demonstrates that grounded reasoning consistently outperforms ungrounded generation, with structured planning proving more transferable than direct answer generation. Our results show that verifiable multi-hop reasoning does not require massive models at inference time, but rather the right architectural inductive biases combining symbolic structure with learned representations.

abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong general capabilities and achieved great success in areas such as image understanding and reasoning. abstract: Power-system technical standards provide the engineering basis for substation design, equipment acceptance, operation and maintenance, relay protection, and grid security control. titulo: Conflict-Aware RAG Routing: Balancing Cost and Accuracy via Context Contradiction
autores: D. P. Nam; T. H. Tuan; D. D. Long; C. Van Mai
venue: 2026 IEEE 13th International Conference on Intelligent Systems (IS)
abstract: Adaptive model routing can reduce the cost of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), but the routing signal must identify when a small language model (SLM) is likely to fail. We study context conflict, the contradiction among retrieved passages, as one such signal. A five-feature Random Forest combines conflict with query length, retrieved-context length, chunk overlap, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) confidence. We evaluate the pipeline on 3,000 multi-hop questions from MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and 2WikiMultiHopQA using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct locally and DeepSeek-V4-Flash through an API. Nested five-fold calibration selects budget cutoffs from inner out-of-fold rather than in-sample training scores. At an approximately 65% LLM-call rate, the hybrid router saves about 35% of API calls while retaining 83.2–92.2% of the Always-LLM F1. Its advantage over RRF alone is dataset-dependent: at the 50% budget it changes F1 by −1.08, −0.03, and +1.48 points on MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and 2Wiki, respectively; only the 2Wiki interval excludes zero. At 30%, it offers no consistent advantage. An exploratory high-RRF/high-conflict subgroup analysis finds larger hybrid-versus-RRF gains on HotpotQA and 2Wiki. However, a direct additive conflict override at +2/5/10 usage points does not outperform equal-cost random escalation. Thus, contradiction can be complementary on some retrieval distributions, but a simple conflict override is not generally justified.

titulo: SAGE: A Framework of Precise Retrieval for RAG
autores: J. Zhang; G. Li; J. Su
venue: 2025 IEEE 41st International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE)
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has demonstrated significant proficiency in conducting question-answering (QA) tasks within a specified corpus. Nonetheless, numerous failure instances of RAG in QA still exist. These failures are not solely attributable to the limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs); instead, they predominantly arise from the retrieval of inaccurate information for LLMs due to two limitations: (1) Current RAG methods segment the corpus without considering semantics, making it difficult to find relevant context due to impaired correlation between questions and the segments. (2) There's a trade-off between missing essential context with fewer context retrieved and getting irrelevant context with more context retrieved. It is hard to make an ideal balance. In this paper, we introduce a RAG framework, named SAGE, designed to overcome these limitations. First, to address the issue of segmentation without considering semantics, we propose to train a semantic segmentation model. This model is trained to segment the corpus into semantically complete chunks. Second, to ensure that only the most relevant chunks are retrieved while the irrelevant ones are ignored, we design a chunk selection algorithm to dynamically select chunks based on the decreasing speed of the relevance score of chunks, leading to a more relevant selection. Third, to further ensure the precision of the retrieved chunks, we propose letting LLMs assess whether retrieved chunks are excessive or lacking and then adjust the amount of context accordingly. Experimental results show that SAGE outperforms baselines by 61.25% in the quality of QA on average. Moreover, by avoiding retrieving noisy context, SAGE lowers the cost of the tokens consumed in LLM inference and achieves a 49.41% enhancement in cost efficiency on average. Additionally, our work offers valuable insights for boosting RAG, contributing to the development of more effective RAG systems.

titulo: HiTS: A Multimodal Framework for Time Series Analysis via Hierarchical Injection and Visual-Grounded Reasoning
autores: Y. Yin; L. Yan; Q. Liao
venue: 2026 Cross Strait Radio Science and Wireless Technology Conference (CSRSWTC)
abstract: Applying large language models (LLMs) to time series question answering (TSQA) requires effective fusion of continuous temporal data with discrete language representations. titulo: Knowledge-Augmented Planning and Pruning for Multi-Hop Question Answering
autores: X. Meng; B. Peng; X. Ma; B. Liu; Z. Dong
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Big Data & Artificial Intelligence & Software Engineering (ICBASE)
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) excel at language understanding and generation, their application to multi-hop knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) faces challenges from structural and semantic mismatches. Current approaches primarily adopt an agent-based paradigm involving planning (decomposing queries), exploration (searching subgraphs), and reflection. However, previous methods suffer from two limitations: For planning, agent-based paradigms heavily rely on LLMs to decompose questions without continuous grounding in KG structures, leading to unanchored subgoal hallucinationsfactually inconsistent reasoning steps; For KG exploration, previous retrieval strategies prioritise isolated entity matching over contextualised relational triplets, resulting in semantically fragmented retrieval that propagates redundant subgraph exploration and semantic drift. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel KAPP (Knowledge-Augmented Planning and Pruning) framework that synergizes dynamic knowledge grounding with semantic-aware subgraph optimisation. Specifically, KAPP introduces two innovations: a dynamic knowledge-guided planner that interleaves LLM-driven subgoal generation with KG-validated path correction, eliminating hallucinated steps through iterative verification, and a triple-level semantic pruner that evaluates relational relevance via joint question-triplet encoding, preserving contextual coherence while reducing redundant retrievals. Extensive experiments on CWQ and WebQSP benchmarks demonstrate KAPP’s effectiveness, achieving 5.6-7% accuracy gains over existing KG-augmented methods and reducing LLM API calls by $\mathbf{3 2. 4 \%}$.

abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence, especially in large language models (LLMs), has significantly impacted various domains, including healthcare. This article presents M4CXR, a multimodal LLM designed to enhance CXR interpretation. The model is trained on a visual instruction-following dataset that integrates various task-specific datasets in a conversational format. As a result, the model supports multiple tasks such as medical report generation (MRG), visual grounding, and visual question answering (VQA). M4CXR achieves state-of-the-art clinical accuracy in MRG by employing a chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting strategy, in which it identifies findings in CXR images and subsequently generates corresponding reports. The model is adaptable to various MRG scenarios depending on the available inputs, such as single-image, multiimage, and multistudy contexts. In addition to MRG, M4CXR performs visual grounding at a level comparable to specialized models and demonstrates outstanding performance in VQA. Both quantitative and qualitative assessments reveal M4CXR’s versatility in MRG, visual grounding, and VQA, while consistently maintaining clinical accuracy.

autores: P. L. Elkin; A. N. Elkin; G. Mehta; F. LeHouillier; J. R. Nebeker; N. Saquib; S. H. Brown
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether semantic clinical knowledge augmentation through Semantic Clinical Artificial Intelligence (SCAI) improves medical question answering across commercial and open large language models, and to examine how a reasoning distilled model performs on the same benchmark. Materials and Methods: We evaluated Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Meta Llama 3 70B, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B on official text only United States Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE) sample questions from Step 1 (n = 87), Step 2 CK (n = 103), and Step 3 (n = 123), with and without SCAI. SCAI comprised HD-NLP parsing, graph and knowledge graph embeddings, a trained SCAI LLM semantic knowledge reasoner, and a semantic knowledge base; the current implementation contained 33,023,902 triples across 246 relation labels. Responses were scored against the answer key with secondary human verification. All models produced a response to every text only item, so incorrect responses were counted as confabulations. Results: Across 313 items, accuracy increased from 90.7% to 97.1% for Gemini, 82.4% to 92.0% for Llama 3 70B, and 55.3% to 81.8% for DeepSeek-R1-Distill; Copilot changed from 93.6% to 94.2%. Within model gains were statistically significant for Gemini, Llama 3 70B, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill on all three steps, but not for Copilot. The best single model result was Llama 3 70B plus SCAI on Step 3 (121/123, 98.4%). Gemini plus SCAI was the numerically strongest commercial system. Conclusions: SCAI was associated with materially better accuracy and lower confabulation (False Positive Results) across several heterogeneous LLMs, supporting a semantically grounded pipeline in which a dedicated SCAI LLM generates clinical context for a host LLM while suggesting that strong general reasoning performance does not automatically translate into healthcare readiness.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across edge and cloud platforms for real-time question-answering (QA) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). abstract: Robustness is a critical consideration when integrating artificial intelligence (AI) systems into decision-making processes. Even if digital mental health chatbots seem like a good solution, many of the ones that are currently available use static mappings between intentions and responses or designs based on rules, which makes the interactions shallow, the emotional sensitivity low, the personalization weak, and the contextual memory bad. Further issues with approaches based on Large Language Model (LLM) include hallucinations, poor explainability, and insufficient detection of high-risk events needing expert intervention. This research suggests an Adaptive Agentic Artificial Intelligence-driven mental health chatbot combining multi-agent systems, knowledge graph reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), reinforcement learning, and memory-based personalization to improve dependability and user participation. The structure combines graphstructured domain knowledge using FalkorDB, vector-based retrieval with ChromaDB, a strong safety and escalation system, intent and emotion detection, condition-specific agents (ADHD, OCD, anxiety, and general wellbeing), and graph-structured domain knowledge using FalkorDB. titulo: Noise, Distraction, and Mitigation: An Analysis of RAG Failure Modes in Medical Question Answering
autores: M. T. I. Rahat; R. Safowan; M. Abir; R. M. Rahman
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is an idea to give Large Language Models (LLMs) a much needed boost by tapping into external knowledge sources. However, there is still much to learn about how well it works in the field of medicine. At present, we do not have enough information to say for certain. In this research, we take a top-of-the-line medical LLM called MMed-Llama-3-8B and test on a 500 question challenge called the PubMedQA benchmark. We found a significant performance degradation when integrating RAG system to the model. When the RAG model provides additional documents, the baseline accuracy of 68.8 % has been dropped to as low as 17.6 %. To investigate the source of error, we analyzed 165 cases in detail where the performance was degraded by RAG system. The primary issues we found were that RAG retrieved some documents that diverted the model from the context in 41.8 % of cases, whereas in 37.6 % cases the retrieved documents contradicted knowledge. To mitigate this, we devised a better way to prompt the model that could improve the performance of the RAG setup to 59.6 % a 186 % boost over just using RAG as it is. Our research reveals the fact that within domains such as medicine, the mere application of RAG is inadequate and the models should be able to manage noise that are inherent in data from external sources.

abstract: Enterprises increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge-driven applications such as clinical question answering, technical support, and legal analysis. This paper presents GalaxyRAG, a privacy-preserving and resourceefficient hybrid GraphRAG framework designed for secure and scalable enterprise reasoning. A step-wise reasoning loop enables LLMs to perform multi-hop reasoning without fine-tuning, while a two-stage hybrid evaluation protocol ensures stable and semantically robust performance measurement. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks and enterprise datasets, GalaxyRAG achieves up to 15-point accuracy gains, while our hybrid evaluation reduces the standard deviation of evaluation scores by over 50%.

titulo: MatKV: Trading Compute for Flash Storage in LLM Inference
autores: K. -W. Shin; J. H. Park; M. Oh; Y. Jo; J. Do; S. -W. Lee
venue: 2026 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE)
abstract: We observe two major trends in LLM-based generative AI: (1) inference is becoming the dominant factor in terms of cost and power consumption, surpassing training, and (2) retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is becoming prevalent. When processing long inputs in RAG, the prefill phase of computing the key-value vectors of input text is energy-intensive and time-consuming even with high-end GPUs. Thus, it is crucial to make the prefill phase in RAG inference efficient. To address this issue, we propose MatKV, a scheme that precomputes the key-value vectors (KVs) of RAG objects (e.g., documents), materializes them in inexpensive but fast and power-efficient flash storage, and reuses them at inference time instead of recomputing the KVs using costly and power-inefficient GPU.11https://github.com/kunwooshin/MatKV Experimental results using Hugging Face's Transformers library across stateof-the-art GPUs and flash memory SSDs confirm that, compared to full KV computation on GPUs, MatKV reduces both inference time and power consumption by half for RAG workloads, without severely impacting accuracy in the question-answering task. Furthermore, we demonstrate that MatKV enables additional optimizations in two ways. First, a GPU can decode text while simultaneously loading the materialized KVs for the next instance, reducing load latency. Second, since decoding speed is less sensitive to GPU performance than KV computation, lowend GPUs can be leveraged for decoding without significantly compromising speed once the materialized KVs are loaded into GPU memory. These findings underscore MatKV's potential to make large-scale generative AI applications more cost-effective, power-efficient, and accessible across a wider range of tasks and hardware environments.

abstract: This study introduces an agentic multi-persona orchestration framework that leverages a structured intent inference technique along with parallel role-grounded reasoning and centralised supervisory synthesis. titulo: KEDA: Knowledge-Graph-Enhanced Reasoning for Cross-Artifact Change-Impact Analysis and Question Answering in Electronic Design Automation
autores: S. Ahir
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: Semiconductor design workflows produce tightly coupled artifacts, including RTL source code, timing constraints (SDC), formal assertions (SVA), testbenches, and version-control history, whose semantic dependencies are typically analyzed in isolation by existing electronic design automation tools. Consequently, a change to one artifact may silently affect others, while engineers lack a unified representation for tracing relationships and reasoning about transitive impacts. This paper presents KEDA, a framework that automatically constructs a multi-artifact knowledge graph from hardware design repositories using open-source tools, including Yosys and Git. KEDA applies graph-traversal algorithms for change-impact analysis and graph-grounded retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) for engineering question answering. Its knowledge-graph schema comprises 10 node types and 17 edge relations that unify RTL structure, timing constraints, formal assertions, testbenches, and commit history within a single queryable representation. Evaluation on five open-source designs comprising 38 modules and 207 controlled changes across seven change categories shows that weighted breadth-first search achieves an average recall of 0.94 for change-impact analysis, compared with 0.02 for a structural baseline, and improves F1 by 0.32 to 0.51 across the evaluated designs. For engineering question answering, evaluation on 81 questions across three designs shows that KEDA-QA achieves an evidence recall of 0.826 and evidence precision of 0.893. In comparison, the LLM-only approach retrieves no supporting evidence, while vector-based RAG achieves an evidence recall of 0.605 and precision of 0.409. These results indicate that structured cross-artifact knowledge graphs substantially improve change-impact traceability and evidence-grounded reasoning in hardware design workflows.

abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has achieved significant progress in the medical question answering (MQA) domain. abstract: The fusion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with traditional knowledge systems presents a promising direction for preserving and expanding access to India's rich medicinal plant heritage. Agentic AI, defined by autonomous reasoning, iterative planning, and adaptive problem solving, serves as a powerful tool for digitizing, analyzing, and sharing indigenous knowledge related to medicinal plants. This survey investigates the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), Large Language Models (LLM), Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and Question Answering (QA) techniques in the development of intelligent systems for Indian medicinal plant knowledge. Current frameworks and successful applications in healthcare and ethnobotany are reviewed, alongside the integration challenges posed by diverse data sources and traditional wisdom. Evaluation of a single RAG based agent demonstrated high effectiveness, achieving a precision of 88.48%, recall of 88.64%, and $F 1$ score of 88.56%. In comparison, a standalone LLM achieved a precision of 80.41%, recall of 85.56%, and F1 score of 82.90%. These results reflect the potential of agentic AI to bridge ancient practices and modern science, offering actionable and context aware insights to support sustainable healthcare and biodiversity management.

titulo: Cloud-Edge Retrieval-Augmented Agent Tutor for Trustworthy Personalized Learning in Resource-Constrained Higher Education
autores: H. Wei; Y. Chai; S. You; Y. Jia; W. Lu; M. Sok
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology (AIoTC)
abstract: Generative AI tutors are attractive for universities that lack enough human tutoring capacity, but unbounded cloud chatbots are difficult to audit, costly to operate, and risky when advice is not grounded. This paper presents a cloud-edge retrieval-augmented agent tutor for trustworthy personalized learning in resource-constrained higher education. The workflow combines early-risk learning analytics, local evidence retrieval, policy checking, route-aware cloud escalation, and an explicit run record. On the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), the executed pipeline processed 32,593 student-course records, produced 8,149 test predictions, audited 160 high-risk feedback cases, and generated a full-test routing audit. Logistic regression achieved Macro-F1=0.757, AUC=0.838, and at-risk recall $=0.693$ from first-28-day activity; across five split seeds, Macro-F1 was $0.757 \pm 0.002$. Feature ablation, query ablation, and route-policy stress tests identify which design choices matter. The contribution is a reproducible AIoTC-style architecture and evidence package, bounded to offline public-data evaluation rather than classroom learning gains or hardware latency benchmarking.

titulo: Leveraging Fine-Tuned Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Long-Context Support: For 3GPP Standards
autores: O. Erak; N. Alabbasi; O. Alhussein; I. Lotfi; A. Hussein; S. Muhaidat; M. Debbah
venue: 2024 IEEE Globecom Workshops (GC Wkshps)
abstract: Recent studies show that large language models (LLMs) struggle with technical standards in telecommunications. We propose a fine-tuned retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system based on the Phi-2 small language model (SLM) to serve as an oracle for communication networks. Our developed system leverages forward-looking semantic chunking to adaptively determine parsing breakpoints based on embedding similarity, enabling effective processing of diverse document formats. To handle the challenge of multiple similar contexts in technical standards, we employ a re-ranking algorithm to prioritize the most relevant retrieved chunks. Recognizing the limitations of Phi-2’s small context window, we implemented a recent technique, namely SelfExtend, to expand the context window during inference, which not only boosts performance but also accommodates a wider range of user queries and design requirements from customers to specialized technicians. For fine-tuning, we utilize the low-rank adaptation (LoRA) technique to enhance computational efficiency during training and enable effective fine-tuning on small datasets. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over existing question-answering approaches in the telecom domain, achieving performance that exceeds larger language models such as GPT-4 (which is about 880 times larger in size). This work presents a novel approach to leveraging SLMs for communication networks, offering a balance of efficiency and performance. This work can serve as a foundation towards agentic language models for networks.

titulo: Tool Context Adaptation for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
autores: H. Li; J. Jin
venue: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become an effective paradigm for knowledge-intensive question answering. Agentic RAG further enhances this paradigm by incorporating autonomous agents to perform iterative reasoning and dynamic tool calling. However, existing systems often struggle with effective tool selection and usage, mainly because agents rely on static, generic context when calling tools. We propose TCA-RAG, a framework that improves tool calling through context adaptation. TCA-RAG accumulates tool-related experience at two layers: trajectory-layer experience that reflects how tools perform under specific query scenarios, and tool-layer experience that summarizes generalizable knowledge about each tool. During inference, the system retrieves relevant trajectory and tool experiences and integrates them into the agent’s context to guide efficient tool selection and usage. Experiments on multi-hop QA benchmarks show that TCA-RAG significantly improves answer accuracy and tool-calling efficiency compared with existing RAG and agentic baselines. The code is available in https://github.com/zirconiumnmlee/TCA.

The approach integrates text-to-SQL over an in-memory SQLite database, enabling fast, explainable retrieval and summarization. Reusable components are available in a public GitHub repository to facilitate future research at the intersection of knowledge graphs and RAG.

titulo: LLM-Based Conversational Bots for Support and Question Answering in Higher Education: A Systematic Literature Review
autores: L. R. Albano Santos; A. D. de Souza; B. G. Batista
venue: 2026 17th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed conversational agents into powerful tools for higher education, yet their use for student support and question answering remains fragmented. Institutions lack a unified view of effectiveness, architectures, and challenges such as accuracy, privacy, bias, and costs. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) that identifies, analyzes, and synthesizes studies on LLM-powered conversational bots in higher education. A systematic search in Scopus yielded 14 primary studies, analyzed through qualitative synthesis and descriptive statistics. Findings show predominant applications in FAQs, academic advising, and administrative support, with GPT-family models most common. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is the leading architecture for reducing hallucinations, while fine-tuning supports domain specialization. A cross-mapping of challenges and mitigation strategies reveals paired architectural and governance trade-offs. Reported effectiveness was positive, though challenges with accuracy, privacy, and costs persist. The study maps an emerging field, identifies research gaps, and proposes directions for longitudinal, cost-benefit, and ethical investigations to guide responsible chatbot integration in higher education.

abstract: The scarcity of Arabic-language educational tools tailored for university students, particularly in specialized fields like law and humanities, limits academic engagement and learning effectiveness. titulo: Automated Single-Turn Solution Recommendation System for Software IT Support Tickets
autores: P. T. Isaza; M. Nidd; N. Zheutlin; J. -W. Ahn; C. A. Bhatt; Y. Deng; R. Mahindru; M. Franz; H. Florian; S. Roukos
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Clients wishing to implement generative AI in the domain of IT Support and AIOps face several critical issues: lengthy, vague, and insufficient customer input; model domain coverage; and hallucination. Customers often submit lengthy or incomplete support tickets not suitable for downstream tasks such as retrieval and question-answering in their raw form. For solution recommendation generation itself, clients might choose not to use larger proprietary models such as GPT-4 due to cost and privacy concerns and so are limited to smaller models with potentially less domain coverage that do not generalize to the client's specific technical domain. Retrieval augmented generation is a common solution that addresses both of these issues: a retrieval system first retrieves the necessary domain knowledge which a smaller generative model leverages as context for generation. We present a system developed for a client in the IT Support domain for support case solution recommendation that combines 1) an encoder-only model for classification 2) a generative large language model for query generation 3) retrieval augmented generation (RAG) for answer generation and 4) ensemble generative large language model and k-precision for evaluating the answer groundedness to combat hallucination. The paper describes architecture details, data collection and annotation, development journey and preliminary validations, deployment evaluation, and finally lessons learned.

titulo: Evidence-First Structured Generation: A Two-Stage "Extract-Generate" Minimization Framework for Power Regulation Question Answering
autores: Y. Cen; M. Hou; J. Fan; H. Qiu; W. Chen; J. Chen; M. Gao
venue: 2025 7th International Academic Exchange Conference on Science and Technology Innovation (IAECST)
abstract: The auditability and reproducibility of answers are vital for safety and compliance in power regulation question answering. However, current approaches often lack evidence traceability, involve high costs in fine-tuning and deploying large models, and exhibit poor format adaptability. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an Evidence-First, two-stage extract-generate framework. Its first stage employs a dual-track retrieval strategy combining BM25 and vector retrieval to obtain candidate clauses, from which a fine-tuned model extracts key evidence snippets. These extracted snippets, along with associated metadata including clause numbers, versions, source URLs and confidence scores, are passed to the second stage. The second stage uses predefined templates to integrate this evidence with metadata for structured answer generation. Utilizing LORA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, the framework updates only a minimal fraction of parameters, creating a stable retrieve-extract-generate loop. Experiments on 1069 power regulations and a DuReader-robust subset show our method achieves 88.7% evidence completeness and 89.3% format consistency under comparable resources, outperforming baselines like standard RAG and Direct LLM-RAG, while reducing risks of format collapse and citation omission. This work delivers a low-cost, high-trust technical solution for industry regulation QA with significant engineering application value.

abstract: The recent Artificial intelligence development, proven by the progress in Large Language models (LLMs) and generative systems, has triggered a broad surge in AI adoption in various sectors and domains, especially in the Education Sector. titulo: EarthGPT: A Universal Multimodal Large Language Model for Multisensor Image Comprehension in Remote Sensing Domain
autores: W. Zhang; M. Cai; T. Zhang; Y. Zhuang; X. Mao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success in vision and visual-language tasks within the natural image domain. Owing to the significant domain gap between natural and remote sensing (RS) images, the development of MLLMs in the RS domain is still in the infant stage. To fill the gap, a pioneer MLLM named EarthGPT integrating various multisensor RS interpretation tasks uniformly is proposed in this article for universal RS image comprehension. First, a visual-enhanced perception mechanism is constructed to refine and incorporate coarse-scale semantic perception information and fine-scale detailed perception information. Second, a cross-modal mutual comprehension approach is proposed, aiming at enhancing the interplay between visual perception and language comprehension and deepening the comprehension of both visual and language content. Finally, a unified instruction tuning method for multisensor multitasking in the RS domain is proposed to unify a wide range of tasks including scene classification, image captioning, region-level captioning, visual question answering (VQA), visual grounding, and object detection. More importantly, a dataset named MMRS-1M featuring large-scale multisensor multimodal RS instruction-following is constructed, comprising over 1M image-text pairs based on 34 existing diverse RS datasets and including multisensor images such as optical, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and infrared. The MMRS-1M dataset addresses the drawback of MLLMs on RS expert knowledge and stimulates the development of MLLMs in the RS domain. Extensive experiments are conducted, demonstrating the EarthGPT’s superior performance in various RS visual interpretation tasks compared with the other specialist models and MLLMs, proving the effectiveness of the proposed EarthGPT and offering a versatile paradigm for open-set reasoning tasks. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/wivizhang/EarthGPT.

titulo: Multilingual Speech-to-Text and Automated Meeting Summarization Using NLP and Machine Learning
autores: P. G. Krishna; T. Thilagam
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Manually preparing minutes of a meeting is time-consuming and error-prone, especially in the multilingual case, such as that in India, where the same meeting can use Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada and English languages. In this paper we propose a pipeline to automate the preparation of meeting minutes by utilizing multilingual automatic speech recognition (Whisper Large-v3), GPU-based speaker diarization (Pyannote 3.1), large language model summarization and sentiment analysis (LLaMA-3.3-70B), two stage rule plus LLM based action item extractor, and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) based on FAISS for meeting question answering. In contrast to previous work which addressed transcription and summarization separately, our system integrates all stages through a single Flask/Angular web application and provides engineering metrics such as accuracy scores, latencies, GPU usage and costs which were mostly missing from earlier work on multilingual meeting summarization. On an evaluation with three recordings, our system delivers a WER of 5.34%, diarization accuracy of 91.3%, summarization BERTScore-F1 of 0.891, action item F1 of 0.877, RAG factual accuracy of 84.7% while taking less than 90 seconds for a 30 minute meeting on a single NVIDIA T4 GPU.

titulo: CD-RAG: A Chain-of-Thought and Dynamic Completion Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented QA System for Component Manufacturing Processes
autores: X. Tang; L. Guo; S. Jing
venue: 2025 7th International Conference on Internet of Things, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (IoTAAI)
abstract: This paper proposes CD-RAG (Chain-of-Thought and Dynamic-completion enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a graph-enhanced generative question answering system tailored for component-level process knowledge in industrial settings. Designed to improve semantic understanding and knowledge coverage in complex domain-specific tasks, CD-RAG integrates structured graph retrieval with large language model (LLM)-based generation into a hybrid QA framework. To address performance bottlenecks in conventional RAG systems under conditions of sparse entity-relation representation and incomplete knowledge graphs, CD-RAG introduces two key innovations: (1) a reasoning module guided by chain-of-thought prompting, which enhances multi-hop inference and causal response generation; and (2) a dynamic knowledge completion mechanism, which automatically triggers external web-based search upon retrieval failure, enabling knowledge re-ingestion and semantic closure. The system constructs a multi-dimensional knowledge graph from heterogeneous process-related texts, including technical manuals and industrial e-books, capturing information on workflows, operational standards, and part attributes. Experimental results demonstrate that CD-RAG consistently outperforms baseline systems across all evaluated dimensions. This work offers a generalizable framework and engineering pathway for deploying generative QA systems in real-world industrial knowledge environments.

titulo: Zero Trust Framework for Detecting and Preventing Prompt Injection Attacks in Enterprise AI Chatbots
autores: G. Anbazhagan; P. S; D. J. S
venue: 2026 International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Management (ICSTEM)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into enterprise applications but remain vulnerable to direct and indirect prompt injection attacks. Existing defense mechanisms often rely on static filtering and lack continuous verification. This paper proposes AdaptiveTrustGuard, a Zero Trust framework that integrates prompt validation, semantic similarity detection, retrieval verification, context isolation, adaptive trust scoring, temporal attack analysis, and policy enforcement, continuously verifying each interaction before it reaches the LLM. Initial evaluation on a manually labelled set achieved 60% recall, but testing on the independent deepset/prompt-injections benchmark exposed poor generalization (8.3% recall). Replacing fixed thresholds with a classifier trained on prompt embeddings and calibrated via a validation split recovered strong performance (78.3% recall, 92.2% precision, ROC-AUC 0.943 on deepset), exceeding an external baseline detector, while achieving 61.7% recall on the larger, more realistic PromptShield benchmark. These findings demonstrate the applicability of Zero Trust principles to LLM security while highlighting the necessity of multi-benchmark validation

abstract: [Introduction] The study addresses the challenge of transferring research knowledge to the industry, with a particular focus on small businesses and startups, which often lack access to empirical insights. titulo: Design of a Graph Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Model for the ATT&CK Knowledge Graph
autores: X. Wei; J. Ma
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: With the increasing sophistication of cyber attacks, traditional passive defense systems struggle to cope with stealthy offensive techniques. Although the MITRE ATT&CK framework provides a comprehensive knowledge base of adversarial behaviors, its structured and specialized nature limits its accessibility for average security practitioners. Large language models (LLMs) excel in natural language processing tasks but suffer from hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and data privacy concerns in specialized domains. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) based question-answering model that integrates the ATT&CK knowledge graph with LLMs to accurately answer multi-hop reasoning questions in cybersecurity. The method constructs a knowledge graph integrating multiple sources such as ATT&CK, CVE, and CWE, and leverages LLMs for entity recognition, relation pruning, and path reasoning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms baseline models in F1-score, validating its effectiveness in cybersecurity knowledge question-answering.

titulo: Improving Groundedness in Policy Document Question Answering Using Hybrid RAG with Structure-Based Topic Chunking : A DTNN 2030 Case Study
autores: N. F. Abdul Ghani; M. Ibrahim; M. S. Sulaiman; M. Fauzi Haris; S. N. Hamdan
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
abstract: This paper presents a Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for question answering on long-form policy documents. Dense-only retrieval, a common baseline in RAG pipelines, may struggle with exact lexical matching for structured information such as technical terminology, acronyms, and domain-specific entities commonly found in policy documents. To address this limitation, this study proposes a structure-based topic chunking method that enriches retrieval signals using three information layers: a keyword layer for exact lexical matching, a contextual summary layer for preserving higher-level document meaning, and a content layer containing the original raw text. The proposed retrieval pipeline combines FAISS dense retrieval, BM25 sparse retrieval, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), and cross-encoder reranking to improve retrieval quality and contextual relevance. During answer generation, only the original content layer is forwarded to the Large Language Model (LLM), allowing the effect of retrieval quality on response groundedness to be evaluated independently. The framework was evaluated on the Dasar Teknologi Nuklear Negara (DTNN) 2030, a Malaysian national policy document on nuclear technology development, using 32 manually constructed questions across five question categories. Experimental results show that the Hybrid + Reranker approach achieved an overall score of 126/192 (65.6%) compared to 71/192 (37.0%) for dense-only retrieval, representing an improvement of 28.6 percentage points. The largest improvement was observed in groundedness, where ungrounded responses were reduced from 53.1% to 3.1%. These findings suggest that, in this case study, the retrieval strategy was the main factor behind the improved groundedness on DTNN 2030.

titulo: DocMind: Conversational PDF QA with RAG
autores: B. J. Rakshitha; R. Dharuni; L. M; S. Lakshmi; V. Ravi Kumar
venue: 2026 1st International Electronics & Packaging Technologies Conference: Bridging Skills & Innovation for India’s Industry (EPT India)
abstract: Traditional keyword searches offer no understa–nding of the semantics of the documents being searched, and Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinations, making the extraction of relevant information from large PDF documents problematic. In this paper, we present DocMind, which is a framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for conversational question answering on PDF documents. The system combines semantic document parsing with token-based chunking, sentence-transformer embeddings, and HNSW-indexed vector retrieval. To find the relevant context for a document chunk, a user query is embedded in the same vector space, and the document chunk is provided to an LLM for generating a cohesive answer. DocMind, unlike standard RAG systems, has multi-turn conversational memory and a transparency feature that indicates when an answer is not justified by the document the user uploaded. Our experiments show DocMind outperforms BM25 and TF-IDF by a large margin in the BERT F1 score, ROUGE-L, and the faithfulness metric. DocMind, by semantic retrieval, combines controlled generation to enhance information accessibility and reduce hallucinations while providing reliable, transparent, and domain-agnostic question answering.

titulo: Medical Image Intelligence: Large Model-Enhanced Medical Multi-Image Difference Visual Question Answering System
autores: J. Wang; W. Lu; J. Yin; F. Lu; J. Xie; S. Liu
venue: 2025 4th International Joint Conference on Information and Communication Engineering (JCICE)
abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence has precipitated the gradual implementation of visual question answering (VQA) in the domain of medical imaging. However, extant models are deficient in terms of the specialisation and temporal reasoning capabilities that are prerequisites for the medical field. The proposed framework is a multimodal visual question answering framework based on medical knowledge graphs and large language models, termed MediLKG-VQA(Medical LLM-Knowledge-Grounded VQA). This framework integrates a medical knowledge graph, constructed utilising the MIMIC-CXR-JPG dataset, with a multirelationship graph neural network, with the objective of enhancing semantic reasoning capabilities. The model’s capacity to analyse variations in medical images across different time points is facilitated by dual-graph input, thereby enabling the inference of lesion progression. Furthermore, the incorporation of the Qwen-3 large language model facilitates bilingual (Chinese-English) question-answering and structured explanations, thereby enhancing the system’s interactivity and clinical adaptability. Experimental findings demonstrate that the system exhibits superior performance in terms of accuracy, interpretability, and clinical adaptability when compared with existing methods. This provides a novel solution for intelligent diagnosis and medical decision-making.

titulo: An AI-Assisted Framework for Dynamics and Control Laboratory with Chatbot-Supported Multiple Representations of Learning
autores: D. Kanala; R. Montgomery; A. Tekes; T. Utschig; C. Tekes
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: Engineering laboratory courses in dynamics and control require students to integrate theoretical modeling, simulation, and physical experimentation while interpreting system behavior and troubleshooting implementation challenges. Providing timely and scalable instructional support in such settings remains difficult. This paper presents the design and preliminary evaluation of an AI-powered chatbot developed to support learning in a dynamics and control laboratory through instructionally guided assistance. The proposed system integrates a LLaMA-based language model with a retrieval-augmented generation framework grounded in laboratory manuals, experimental documentation, and course-specific materials. The chatbot is deployed on a private GPU server behind institutional network controls and accessed through a cloud-hosted interface, enabling secure and scalable student interaction. The system is designed to provide conceptual clarification and procedural guidance while avoiding direct solution generation. A rubric-based evaluation was conducted on 112 student-issued queries collected during the pilot deployment of a pendulum laboratory activity. Results indicate strong alignment with student intent and laboratory context, acceptable response latency for real-time use, and stable, grounded behavior under typical laboratory conditions.

titulo: Facilitating Aboriginal Perinatal Mental Health Information Access with a Retrieval-Augmented LLM-based Chatbot
autores: M. S. M. Utami; W. H. Kwok; J. Kotz; R. Walker; G. Wang; R. Marriott
venue: 2025 47th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
abstract: Aboriginal pregnant women and new mothers face an increased risk of mental health issues, often stemming from historical trauma, including violence and discrimination. These challenges could contribute to complex trauma and adverse perinatal outcomes, highlighting the need for culturally sensitive care. However, non-Aboriginal clinicians often face barriers due to limited cultural knowledge, exacerbated by other factors such as time constraints for training and reliance on one-time training. Large Language Models (LLMs)-based chatbots offer the potential to support self-directed learning and enhance clinicians’ self-efficacy through interactive question and answer. However, LLMs also pose challenges, including hallucinatory responses, outdated knowledge, fictitious information, unverifiable references, and difficulty handling domain-specific queries. In this study, we aim to mitigate these challenges by developing a specialized chatbot for improving Aboriginal perinatal mental health question-answering. The chatbot integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a semantic search engine, enabling it to retrieve verified external knowledge and provide more accurate, contextually relevant responses without frequent retraining. We evaluate its performance against a baseline GPT-3.5-turbo model and compare LLMs integrated with different RAG techniques to assess improvements in accuracy and reliability.Clinical Relevance— This study shows the potential of the specialized RAG LLM-based chatbot to improve domain-specific, clinically relevant, and on-demand question-answering support for clinicians. By providing accurate, verified information through interactive responses, it may help bridge knowledge gaps, support self-directed learning, and complement existing training.

titulo: SAOG: Spatial-Attribute-Aware 3D Object Grounding via Visual Question Answering-Enhanced Reasoning
autores: T. Jin; J. Xu; S. Yuan; J. Li; T. -M. Nguyen; L. Xie
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: 3D object grounding aims to identify the target object referred to by natural language instructions in the presence of multiple distractors. The task is inherently challenging, as it demands joint consideration of spatial relations and intrinsic object attributes to disambiguate the referred target from distractors. Conventional supervised learning methods often exhibit limited generalization due to the complexity of the problem and the scarcity of annotated data, and offer little interpretability of grounding decisions. Recent zero-shot LLM-based approaches have demonstrated promising results for this task, yet they tend to focus either on tool-based spatial verification or on visual reasoning over images, without jointly accounting for spatial relations and intrinsic attributes. To bridge this gap, we propose SAOG, a zero-shot spatial-attribute-aware 3D object grounding pipeline, in which context-aware visual question answering (VQA) enhances the tool-based reasoning process by synergistically exploiting visual attributes and complementary spatial cues. Experiments on the Nr3D dataset show an accuracy improvement of 7.0 percentage points over state-of-the-art zero-shot methods. We further demonstrate its applicability in robotic navigation, and the code will be made publicly available to facilitate future research.
