titulo: Retrieval Augmented Thought Process for Private Data Handling in Healthcare
autores: T. Pouplin; H. Sun; S. Holt; M. van der Schaar
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated the strong potential to assist both clinicians and the general public with their extensive medical knowledge. However, their application in healthcare is constrained due to concerns about the privacy of data used in training, which prevents the integration of private and personal information because of security and ethical issues. Moreover, if their capabilities can be enhanced with information retrieval to access up-to-date knowledge, the current integration of LLMs with Information retrieval lacks robustness to imperfect retrieval, which can hinder their effectiveness and even reduce overall performance. In this work, we address this challenge by introducing the Retrieval-Augmented Thought Process (RATP). Given access to external knowledge, RATP formulates the thought generation of LLMs as a multiple-step decision process. To optimise such a thought process, RATP leverages Monte-Carlo Tree Search and learns a proxy reward function that permits cost-efficient inference. On a private dataset of electronic medical records, deliberately excluded from any LLM training set, RATP achieves 35% additional accuracy compared to in-context retrieval-augmented generation for the question-answering task.

titulo: Domain Adaptive Document Reranking for Retrieval Augmented Generation
autores: Y. Rachidy; Y. Hmamouche; F. Sehbaoui; A. E. F. Seghrouchni
venue: 2025 IEEE 37th International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI)
abstract: Current AI-driven Question-Answering (QA) systems face significant challenges in delivering accurate, domainspecific responses across diverse fields. While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at text generation, they often face difficulties in producing precise answers without access to external knowledge sources. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this limitation by connecting LLMs to external information sources. However, RAG systems often struggle to maintain the relevance and reliability of the retrieved information. Finetuning rerankers on domain-specific data could improve the selection of relevant text chunks before generation, but adapting them for multi-domain RAG settings remains challenging. Additionally, the cost of fine-tuning becomes significant, particularly when dealing with large models and extensive datasets. To address this limitation, we propose Domain Adaptive Document Reranking for Retrieval Augmented Generation. This new approach leverages the Mixture of Experts (MoE) paradigm when finetuning rerankers within RAG systems. Our framework employs a routing mechanism that dynamically directs queries to domainspecific experts, improving performance without sacrificing crossdomain generalization. Experimental results in the agricultural and medical domains demonstrate that our framework outperforms baselines, underscoring the critical role of domain expertise in refining retrieved information for accurate LLM-based QA in multi-domain settings.

titulo: Vision-Language Transformers for Medical Report Synthesis: A Multimodal Approach
autores: K. Suram; H. A J; A. Kurian; K. Augustine; R. Majeed A
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
abstract: The efficacy of large language models has revolutionized the healthcare domain by improving medical records documentation, report generation, question answering, and retrieval-augmented generation. Traditional models are equipped to process text-based input, limiting their effectiveness in the presence of multimodal data such as healthcare images, unstructured reports, and prompts. This research proposes a multimodal large language model augmented using RAG for automated report generation in healthcare. A BLIP model integrated with the LoRA fine-tuned T5 transformer has been developed to interpret user-driven prompts and X-ray images to synthesize accurate, and context-aware clinical reports. The model shows high report generation accuracy using various evaluation metrics (Bleu - 0.11, Meteor - 0.39, Rouge-L - 0.58). By leveraging visionlanguage models and transformer architectures,the proposed MLLM integrates textual, and visual data to enhance diagnostic accuracy and reduce physician workload.

titulo: Visual-Grounded Hierarchical Perception for Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
autores: Z. Zhang; L. Li; X. Liu; L. Jiao; F. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Remote sensing visual question answering (RSVQA) leverages vision and natural language for intelligent Earth observation. While multimodal large language models (LLMs) demonstrate broad potential in remote sensing (RS) multitask frameworks, their heavy reliance on textual priors from extensive conversational pretraining and neglect of the hierarchical nature of RS scenes limit their performance. To address these limitations, this article proposes a visual-grounded hierarchical perception (VGHP) framework that activates a pretrained LLM’s open-world knowledge under the joint guidance of visual evidence and linguistic semantics for reliable answer generation. Specifically, a visual-grounded language encoder (VGLE) dynamically binds question semantics to the visual context via cross-modal attention at every encoding layer, effectively mitigating the language prior bias by enforcing vision-conditioned reasoning. Concurrently, a hierarchical vision perceiver (HVP) is designed to capture multigranular visual information, routing local details and global semantics across feature hierarchies in a vision tower, thereby addressing multiscale perception challenges in RS images. Extensive experiments on three RSVQA benchmarks showcase the superiority of the proposed VGHP, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency.

titulo: Implementing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy in Chatbots to Reduce Students’ Exam Stress using ChatGPT
autores: M. M. A. H. Indumini; K. A. S. H. Kulathilake; D. K. Hettiarachchi
venue: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Undergraduate students frequently encounter academic stress, highlighting the need for accessible and effective coping mechanisms. This study develops an AI chatbot grounded in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) principles to meet the mental health needs of these students. The primary goal is to devise and assess a chatbot that delivers personalized support for managing academic stress. The chatbot engages students in meaningful conversations, identifies cognitive distortions in their thought processes, and provides customized coping strategies. It leverages OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 turbo LLM for generating lifelike interactions and uses a vector database to store domain-specific knowledge. Responses are preprocessed with OpenAI embeddings for intent classification. Support Vector Machines (SVM), Multinomial Logistic Regression, and Random Forest models are used for classifying cognitive distortions, with SVM achieving the highest accuracy of $85.94 \%$. Intent classification is refined using cosine similarity, enhancing the chatbot’s conversational accuracy. Although SVM outperforms other models, ongoing challenges call for further research to refine the chatbot’s functionality and improve its impact on student well-being.

titulo: Reason-Align-Respond: Aligning LLM Reasoning With Knowledge Graphs for KGQA
autores: X. Shen; F. Wang; Z. Yang; B. Wang; W. Du; C. Zong; R. Xia
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex reasoning tasks, yet they often suffer from hallucinations and lack reliable factual grounding. Meanwhile, knowledge graphs (KGs) provide structured factual knowledge, but lack the flexible reasoning abilities of LLMs. In this paper, we present Reason-Align-Respond (RAR), a novel framework that systematically integrates LLM reasoning with knowledge graphs for knowledge graph question answering (KGQA). Our approach consists of three key components: a Reasoner that generates human-like natural language reasoning chains, an Aligner that maps these chains to valid KG paths, and a Responser that synthesizes the final answer. We formulate this process as a latent variable mixture model and optimize it using the Expectation-Maximization algorithm, which iteratively refines the reasoning chains and knowledge paths. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of RAR, achieving state-of-the-art performance with Hit scores of 93.3% and 91.0% on WebQSP and CWQ respectively. Human evaluation confirms that RAR generates high-quality, interpretable reasoning chains well-aligned with KG paths while maintaining computational efficiency during inference.

titulo: ATU-Tutor: A RAG-Based Socratic Tutoring System with Agentic AI Adaptive Assessment
autores: M. S. Sayeed; S. Wajiha; R. Ghosh; M. A. S. Siddique; S. Bhandari
venue: 2026 IEEE World AI IoT Congress (AIIoT)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential for educational tutoring, but hallucinations, poor curriculum alignment, and limited access to domain specific knowledge limit their application in academic settings. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is one way to overcome these shortcomings by anchoring model outputs to external sources. Still, most educational RAG systems are limited to single turn question answering and offer little pedagogical assistance. The paper will provide the design and assessment of the RAG enhanced LLM chatbot in Socratic tutoring and adaptive quiz generation at Arkansas Tech University (ATU). The system employs a hybrid retrieval pipeline with FAISS, BM25, and cross encoder re ranking on a knowledge base of 2,328 chunks from 17 open educational resources textbooks, as well as a retriever fine tuned on 929 domain specific query passage pairs. The Qwen3 8B model supports both tutoring and assessment. In tutoring mode, the system generates grounded explanations and Socratic follow up questions; in assessment mode, it generates curriculum aligned multiple choice and short answer questions with immediate feedback. The assessment of 14 questions demonstrated strong results in relevance, conciseness, contextual grounding, and resistance to hallucinations, with overall heuristic and LLM scores of 4.00/5. Lower scores in empathy and Socratic scaffolding indicate areas for future improvement. The findings show the potential of retrieval based tutoring and self adaptive assessment in a university specific curriculum.

titulo: A Curriculum-Grounded AI Tutoring System
autores: S. Đurović; S. Kovačević; M. Lasica; B. Uskoković; A. Softić; A. Džuho; A. Badnjević
venue: 2026 30th International Conference on Information Technology (IT)
abstract: This paper presents TutorMe, an AI-assisted elearning chatbot platform designed to support students with lesson explanations, question answering, quiz generation, and learning-material navigation using curriculum-aligned, digitized resources. TutorMe is implemented as a modular web application integrated with a domain-restricted knowledge base built from structured PDF learning materials. The contribution is engineering-focused: we describe a reproducible design for a knowledge-base-grounded tutoring assistant, document key configuration choices (prompting strategy, retrieval behavior, and platform settings), and report a pilot offline evaluation using a rubric for manual assessment of correctness and groundedness. In an internal test set of 120 questions spanning biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics at three difficulty levels, manual review showed that 80.0 % of answers were fully correct. Biology exhibited the lowest accuracy (60%) due to terminology imprecisions, while mathematics achieved 93.3%. titulo: Introducing Axlerod: An LLM-Based Chatbot for Assisting Independent Insurance Agents
autores: A. Bradley; J. Hastings; K. M. Ahmed
venue: 2025 Cyber Awareness and Research Symposium (CARS)
abstract: The insurance industry is undergoing a paradigm shift through the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly in the realm of intelligent conversational agents. Chatbots have evolved into sophisticated AI-driven systems capable of automating complex workflows, including policy recommendation and claims triage, while simultaneously enabling dynamic, context-aware user engagement. This paper presents the design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of Axlerod, an AI-powered conversational interface designed to improve the operational efficiency of independent insurance agents. titulo: Dynamic Retrieval-Reasoning Framework on Hypergraphs for Complex Question Answering
autores: Y. Hou; C. Zheng
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with knowledge graphs improves factual grounding in large language models (LLMs) but remains limited by two critical bottlenecks. First, conventional graph-based RAG models knowledge as binary triples, which fragments higher-order semantic structures and fails to preserve the integrity of n-ary relational facts. Second, non-adaptive, query-agnostic retrieval introduces redundant information that interferes with the LLM’s intrinsic reasoning. To overcome these challenges, we propose G-RAGent, a dynamic reasoning framework that unifies hypergraph-based knowledge representation with an adaptive retrieval agent. G-RAGent encodes multi-entity facts as hyperedges and employs a ReAct-style iterative reasoning process in which the LLM decomposes questions, predicts relevant semantic topics, selectively retrieves sub-hypergraphs, and halts retrieval when internal knowledge suffices. Our evaluation demonstrates G-RAGent outperforms the SOTA model Graph-CoT by 21.5 absolute points—a relative improvement of 60.9%, and reduces end-to-end latency by over 28%, demonstrating G-RAGent’s effectiveness and superiority on retrieval and reasoning.

titulo: A multimodal Question Answering system using Language Models for accessing disaster related queries of Assam
autores: P. J. Baruah; V. S. Snehal; T. Borah; A. Paul; M. Bhattacharya; T. D. Singha
venue: 2026 IEEE Guwahati Subsection Conference (GCON)
abstract: This paper evaluates the feasibility of deploying lightweight multimodal retrieval-augmented generation systems on resource-constrained edge devices for autonomous post-disaster analysis. We construct a specialized multimodal knowledge base from government reports and field imagery to benchmark 5 efficient open-sourced architectures: InternVL-3.5-8B, Gemma-3-4B-IT, Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2-VL-2B, and a ViLT+RoBERTa baseline. The models are evaluated using a set a question that includes both factoid and descriptive type of questions. The experimental results reveal that modern small language models significantly outperform traditional disjoint pipelines the task. The Gemma-3-4B-IT, a light-weight small language model emerged as the optimal architecture, achieving the best balance between high-resolution visual understanding and low-latency inference. It achieved an F1-score of 90.34%, and BLEU, ROUGE-L, BERT Score, SAS and average-latency of 0.34, 0.88, 0.97, 0.17 and 2.24 sec respectively.

titulo: An Accessible Real-Time Document Question Answering Extension for People with Visual Impairment
autores: A. V; K. S. Kuppusamy
venue: 2025 1st International Conference on Data Science and Intelligent Network Computing (ICDSINC)
abstract: Visually impaired users face challenges in retrieving specific information from digital documents due to the linear design of traditional screen readers and limited contextual support. titulo: Local RAG-based learning assistant in educational applications
autores: K. Horváth; C. Hajdu
venue: 2026 IEEE 30th International Conference on Intelligent Engineering Systems (INES)
abstract: In recent years, an increasing number of AI-powered tools have been created, most of which operate as cloud-based services. The vast majority of such services upload personal notes, recordings, and documents to external servers, raising data protection and ethical concerns. The aim of the research is to design, implement and evaluate a locally executable AI-powered learning assistant capable of processing documents, images, and audio files. The system can generate answers and summaries as well as provide spoken responses through an integrated text-to-speech module. Since everything runs locally, the tool can be used completely offline. The system is built on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline in which all source documents, the vector database, and metadata remain on the user’s machine. Several quantized LLM models were tested to find the optimal balance between accuracy and resource use on consumer hardware. The evaluation shows that a well-tuned retrieval pipeline matters more for output quality than model size alone, and that RAG significantly reduces hallucination on domain-specific Hungarian queries.

titulo: LLM Integrated AI Assistant For Educational Institutions
autores: S. Rajendran; R. S. Pillai; U. Abhijith; J. Swathy; A. Radhakrishnan
venue: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Solutions for Sustainable Smart Cities: Challenges and Opportunities (ADSSSC)
abstract: Through manual inquiry methods like phone calls, emails, and face-to-face visits, organizations face the problems of delayed responses, inconsistent information, limited staff members’ access and greater workload. To counter these limitations modern inquiry automation systems were developed and empowered by AI chatbots that are built with RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG) [8]. The organization uses this method to collect all its knowledge which gets transformed into a vector database for permanent storage. The system uses this system design to access needed data with high speed. The system validates answers through trustworthy data sources. The system achieves better accuracy through vector search which identifies contextually relevant data. The knowledge which has been collected after a user makes a request helps a small language model to produce highly accurate and steady responses. The systems operate continuously to handle multiple users while delivering dependable and current information. The system provides an AI-assisted inquiry automation solution which achieves both maximum scalability and complete future readiness.

titulo: RAG-Based Knowledge Retrieval Architecture for Medical Web Platforms
autores: B. Fedallah; Ö. İnik
venue: 2026 2nd International Symposium on AI-Driven Engineering Systems (ISADES)
abstract: Medical web platforms often serve users as static content repositories, unable to respond to specific health-related queries in real time. This study presents a RAG-Based (RetrievalAugmented Generation) knowledge retrieval architecture designed for integration into medical web platforms. The proposed system combines a Laravel 11 backend, ChromaDB vector database, and Llama 3.3 (70B) language model via Groq API to transform a static medical platform into an intelligent, sourcegrounded question-answering system. Medical content is chunked into 200 -word segments with 30 -word overlap, resulting in 56 chunks, embedded using all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and stored in ChromaDB for semantic retrieval. A React-based frontend component (useRAG hook) communicates with the backend API to deliver real-time responses. The system is evaluated using the RAGAS framework with the Faithfulness metric, measuring whether generated answers are grounded in the retrieved context. Results demonstrate that open-source, low-cost RAG pipelines can effectively reduce hallucination and improve information accuracy in medical web contexts.

titulo: Optimizing Vertical Domain RAG: Domain-Adaptive Data Processing and RLAIF Synergy
autores: X. Zhang; Y. Zhou; Z. Wei
venue: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Ethics (ICAIDE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) in question answering systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has significantly improved LLM performance on knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating external knowledge sources. However, due to incomplete data processing pipelines and domain-specific information biases in LLMs, conventional RAG frameworks often perform poorly in vertical domain question answering scenarios. Focusing on the domain of food safety standards, this study proposes an enhanced RAG framework. The approach improves the efficiency of the retrieval module through customized data processing strategies and incorporates reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) to infuse the generation module with domain knowledge and high-quality response preferences using a self-constructed dataset. This framework effectively mitigates issues of value misalignment and factual inaccuracy commonly encountered in LLM applications within vertical domains. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RAG framework outperforms conventional RAG in terms of response accuracy and domain adaptability, validating its effectiveness. This work offers new insights and methodologies for building verticaldomain QA systems and enhances the applicability of LLMs in specialized fields.

titulo: Venn Diagram Prompting: Accelerating Comprehension with Scaffolding Effect
autores: S. Mahendru; T. Pandit
venue: 2024 6th World Symposium on Artificial Intelligence (WSAI)
abstract: We introduce Venn Diagram (VD) Prompting, an innovative prompting technique which allows Large Language Models (LLMs) to combine and synthesize information across complex, diverse and long-context documents in knowledge-intensive question-answering tasks. Generating answers from multiple documents involves numerous steps to extract relevant and unique information and amalgamate it into a cohesive response. To improve the quality of the final answer, multiple LLM calls or pretrained models are used to perform different tasks such as summarization, reorganization and customization. The approach covered in the paper focuses on replacing the multi-step strategy via a single LLM call using VD prompting. Our proposed technique also aims to eliminate the inherent position bias in the LLMs, enhancing consistency in answers by removing sensitivity to the sequence of input information. It overcomes the challenge of inconsistency traditionally associated with varying input sequences. We also explore the practical applications of the VD prompt based on our examination of the prompt's outcomes. In the experiments performed on four public benchmark question-answering datasets, VD prompting continually matches or surpasses the performance of a meticulously crafted instruction prompt which adheres to optimal guidelines and practices.

motivo: revisão ou survey
titulo: LLM-based Evidence Verification in Cyber Threat Intelligence: A Systematic Review of Retrieval-Augmented Approaches and Entailment-based Attribution Verification
autores: J. K. Shriwas; P. Karmore
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed for cyber threat intelligence (CTI) purposes, including attack investigations and threat actor attribution. Hallucinations, i.e., fluent but unsupported claims, present a challenge to this application, as the wrong attribution might mislead an incident response team or waste the investigative efforts. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), one of the most popular approaches to combatting hallucination by LLMs, validates the claims against the knowledge from the outside sources such as the MITRE Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge (ATT&CK) framework. The paper offers a systematic review of recent publications about RAG use in CTI question answering, retrieval-augmented systems, entailment-based claim verification in other domains, and the reliability of agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI). Throughout this literature, a persistent gap is identified: whereas the correctness and relevance of the retrieval is evaluated, none of the papers verify whether the claim is indeed entailed by the retrieved information. Notably, the analysis of one of the existing retrieval-augmented CTI tools, RAGIntel, shows that threat-actor attribution is the task where this kind of system performs the poorest, with a context precision of 0.091 compared to 0.790 for the technique classification. Moreover, even the correct threat attribution can be marked as incorrect due to the existence of aliases for threat-actor groups, e.g., "APT34" versus "OilRig". Thus, to date, among the systems identified in this review, no retrieval-augmented system has attempted to verify the attribution claims via entailment of the retrieved MITRE ATT&CK group-technique relations, taking into account possible aliases of the groups. The paper proposes to solve this gap with an alias-aware entailment-based verification layer producing an explicit statement about the relation between the claim and the evidence.

titulo: Expert-Knowledge-Enhanced Question Answering and Training Assistance System for Simulation Training Scenarios
autores: Z. Xu; Z. Wang; H. Wang; Y. Zhou; M. Sun
venue: 2026 7th International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Information Technology (AINIT)
abstract: This paper presents an expert-knowledge-enhanced question answering and training assistance system for simulation training scenarios, where knowledge is dispersed, procedural constraints are strict, and response reliability is critical. The proposed method first organizes concept, rule, case, and procedural knowledge into a unified multi-source knowledge base. It then introduces a multi-evidence-constrained question answering mechanism that jointly leverages rule, procedural, and case evidence to guide large language model generation, improving answer accuracy and procedural correctness. In addition, a trustworthy output mechanism is designed through evidence consistency checking, rule conflict detection, and low-confidence control, enhancing the verifiability and traceability of generated responses. Based on these designs, a prototype system is implemented to support training preparation, in-process assistance, and post-training review. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively improves the accuracy, procedural consistency, and trustworthiness of professional training question answering.

titulo: Design and Evaluation of Agentic RAG Systems: Native, Self-RAG, and Adaptive RAG
autores: Y. Chinnam; S. Gogineni; G. Suryanarayana; V. Botsa; N. B. Kuduthuru; A. Pimpalshende
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Networking Systems (ICC-CNS)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant paradigm for grounding large language model (LLM) outputs in factual, externally retrieved evidence. However, different RAG architectures impose fundamentally different retrieval philosophies: Native RAG retrieves unconditionally at every inference step, Self-RAG retrieves on-demand and self-critiques its own outputs using special reflection tokens, and Adaptive RAG dynamically routes each query through the simplest sufficient retrieval strategy based on query complexity. Despite the practical significance of this distinction, a controlled, multi-model empirical comparison of these three paradigms under a unified orchestration framework has not been reported. In this work, we implement all three RAG variants using LangChain and LangGraph as the orchestration backbone, with GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Claude 3 Sonnet as the generator models, and evaluate them on the HotpotQA multi-hop question answering benchmark available on Hugging Face. Each pipeline is coupled with a FAISS-based dense retriever using text-embedding-3-small embeddings. Experiments are conducted on 1,000 randomly sampled distractor-setting questions from the validation split. Results show that Adaptive RAG consistently achieves the strongest balance across token F1, ROUGE-L, and RAGAS Faithfulness, while Self-RAG yields higher faithfulness scores at the cost of increased latency. Native RAG offers the lowest latency but the weakest faithfulness. Among generator models, GPT-4o outperforms Gemini 1.5 Pro and Claude 3 Sonnet on all three metrics, though the gap narrows under the Self-RAG protocol. These findings provide the first direct, framework-unified comparison of the three RAG paradigms across multiple frontier LLMs on a challenging multi-hop benchmark.

titulo: Exploring Knowledge Filtering for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
autores: M. Qiang; Z. Wang; S. Li; G. Zhou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation significantly enhances the performance of Large Language Models on knowledge-intensive tasks by incorporating external knowledge. To address this, we propose a novel two-stage framework. First, we establish an annotation strategy to label the harmfulness of a document based on its impact on downstream task performance. Subsequently, our Knowledge Filtering module utilizes this annotated data to learn to identify and eliminate harmful knowledge. For this module, we develop and evaluate four distinct strategies, ranging from methods that leverage LLM self-evaluation and lightweight proxy models to those based on preference alignment. Experiments conducted on three diverse question answering datasets demonstrate that our approach effectively purges harmful knowledge, leading to more reliable and accurate responses.

titulo: A Hybrid SQL-RAG-LLM Question Answering System for Plastic Waste Management
autores: D. Sivan; Y. -L. Wei; K. S. Kumar; Y. -J. Chen; R. Jose
venue: 2025 7th International Conference on Interdisciplinary Computer Science and Engineering (ICICSE)
abstract: Plastic waste management is a critical global challenge, demanding rapid synthesis of large and heterogeneous research outputs. Here, a hybrid question answering framework is presented, that integrates structured SQL querying with large language model (LLM) based generation to deliver both accuracy and coverage. A validator LLM selects or merges outputs, followed by a fact-checking pass to ensure alignment with evidence. User feedback drives an interactive fine - tuning loop, logging rejected and accepted answers for supervised model updates. Preliminary results indicate the SQL pathway delivers high precision for structured questions, while the hybrid route improves coverage for broader queries. This approach offers a scalable solution for decision support in environmental policy, recycling optimization and scientific discovery in plastic waste management.

abstract: We introduce EgoTextVQA, a novel and rigorously constructed benchmark for egocentric QA assistance involving scene text. titulo: Tekna AI: An Experimental Evaluation of BERTurk, Hybrid RAG and Semantic Caching for Telecommunications and Data-Center Customer Interaction
autores: B. Yılmaz
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Computer Science and Engineering (UBMK)
abstract: In telecommunications and data-center services, customer messages carry different purposes such as information requests, sales intents and technical fault reports; they are often short, noisy and contain several intents at once. Routing such messages to the correct workflow, without pushing all traffic to expensive large-language-model (LLM) calls, is a critical and difficult step. We evaluate Tekna AI, a customer-interaction platform developed at Teknotel, through the lens of its architecture. The platform is layered: an incoming message is first resolved locally by a BERTurk-based classifier that also distinguishes composite intents; the suitable workflow is then selected among question answering, sales and troubleshooting. Retrieval is carried out by a hybrid layer combining HNSW dense search with BM25 lexical matching; for recurring questions, a context-aware semantic cache prevents the answer from being regenerated. The novel aspects are (i) local classification that resolves composite intents in a single decision layer, (ii) a context-aware semantic cache, and (iii) a design that constrains agent behaviour through controlled tool calls. We measure classification accuracy, retrieval and answer quality, and the effect of caching on computational load. The results show that moving routing onto a local model and constraining agents through tools reduces unnecessary LLM calls while preserving answer quality.

titulo: Hybrid Layered Retrieval and Task-Aware Embeddings for Efficient Persian RAG Systems
autores: T. Zoughi; E. Arianyan; M. Mahmoudi; M. Aghdamifard; M. Nikoogoftar
venue: Journal of Web Engineering
abstract: This study introduces task-injected layered hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (TILHR-RAG), a framework specifically designed for Persian to address the scarcity of native-language resources and the limitations of English-centric approaches. The architecture combines task-aware query augmentation, a layered retrieval strategy, and a hybrid semantic-lexical retriever, all supported by a multi-stage pipeline that includes preprocessing, document chunking, question generation, and embedding. A novel mechanism for injecting task-specific vectors directs retrieval toward domain intent while preserving comparability across documents. The layered design operates in three stages: per-task frequently asked questions (FAQ) retrieval, hybrid document search using FAISS semantic similarity combined with BM25 keyword matching, and a fallback response generated by a large language model (LLM). This structure ensures both precision and robustness. Comprehensive experiments across five progressively refined configurations demonstrate that TILHR-RAG achieves the best balance among accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, reaching 89.67% semantic accuracy with moderate latency and memory consumption on NVIDIA A100 hardware. Further evaluations on low-resource graphics processing units (GPUs) confirm that accuracy remains stable under hardware constraints, although latency increases significantly. Moreover, multilingual E5 embedding models substantially improve retrieval and generation quality for Persian – outperforming ParsBERT and Sentence-BERT (SBERT) – by mitigating challenges such as orthographic variation and complex compound word structures. Taken together, these findings establish task-injected layered hybrid retrieval-augmented generation as a practical, reproducible, and resource-efficient blueprint for Persian question answering, advancing retrieval-augmented generation for low-resource languages without requiring costly large language model fine-tuning, while also offering adaptable strategies for broader multilingual applications.

titulo: Answer is not Enough: RAG-Based Video Question Answering with Timestamp Localization
autores: N. Hosmani; A. Rajput; K. Bhavikatti; K. Mallibhat
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging in Computing Technologies (INCECT)
abstract: Video-based instruction has emerged as a predominant course delivery mode in technology-enabled learning systems; still, the issue of long, unstructured lecture recordings remains a concern for students. While recent methods incorporate keyword matching and manual forwarding, they fall short in terms of precision. In this paper, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant is designed for use in multi-video lecture settings. Whisper is used to convert lecture videos into audio files and time-stamped transcripts. These transcripts are broken into focused segments and indexed through a compact local model served via Ollama. A grounding-aware LLM is used to provide timely and reliable explanations, tying in exactly to the relevant time frames. Questions are posted in a shared embedding space, where the best matches are identified using cosine similarity. A local language model then generates an answer while filtering out unsupported information. The model is evaluated using twenty lecture questions; the assistant retrieved the correct top answer about 90% of the time, and every correct answer appeared within its top three or top five suggestions. The system uses three strategies for extracting information: (i) if the topic is located in one place, it retrieves that segment from the corresponding video; (ii) if the topic appears in more than one lecture, it retrieves segments from multiple videos; and (iii) if the topic is not present in the material, the model reports “Not covered,” which prevents misleading learning. This study presents a RAG-based teaching assistant that is both efficient and reliable, and that serves as a practical navigation tool for educational video repositories. The proposed RAG-based Teaching Assistant is practical and reproducible, and it significantly improves student productivity while supporting more precise revision.

titulo: A Summarization Framework with Self-Improvement for RAG Retrieval in the Legal Domain
autores: Y. Perezhohin; F. Riedlinger; V. Costa; M. Castelli
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly used for legal question answering, but their effectiveness depends critically on the quality of the representations indexed during retrieval. Documents are segmented into fixed-size chunks and summarized using a lightweight language model. A second model, acting as a synthetic evaluator based on the G-EVAL methodology, assesses the semantic adequacy of each summary and triggers refinement when necessary. Only validated summaries are admitted into the vector database. The acceptance criterion governing this process is analyzed through a sensitivity study that characterizes the trade-off between retrieval effectiveness and computational overhead. Experiments on the LEGALBENCH-RAG benchmark demonstrate that quality-controlled summaries yield substantial gains over untreated indexing. In a direct comparison using the same model, pairing text-ada-large-3 with our validated summaries increases accuracy at k = 8 from 36.63% to 72.70%. Because retrieval operates on compact, semantically verified representations rather than raw long chunks, the approach improves computational efficiency and narrows the performance gap between proprietary and lightweight models: MultiQA with validated summaries reaches 64.24% accuracy, outperforming the closed-source text-adalarge-3 baseline without quality control.

titulo: External Retrievals or Internal Priors? From RAG to Epitome-Augmented Generation by Fuzzy Selection
autores: K. He; J. Xu; Q. Lin; W. Wang; Z. Gao; J. Wu; Y. Huang; M. Feng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offers a promising solution to the limitations of static knowledge and hallucinations in large language models (LLMs). While prior research has introduced numerous enhancements to RAG systems, a significant challenge remains underexplored: the potential conflict between external retrievals and LLMs’ internal priors, which can undermine the quality of generated outputs. To tackle this issue, we present the epitome-augmented generation (EAG) framework, which strategically aligns queries, external retrievals, and internal priors to produce high-quality LLM generations by selecting fuzzy inputs. EAG employs two novel lightweight modules, criticism and distillation, allowing traditional RAGs to be upgraded to EAGs without the need for specialized training data. Extensive experiments on five datasets across general and medical domains, including both open-ended and closed-ended tasks, validate the effectiveness of EAG. Our framework achieves substantial F1 score improvements: 7.03%, 23.35%, and 21.58% over baseline RAGs in medical question answering tasks, 11.80% in law domain, 7.95% in finance domain, and 4.13% and 5.16% in general domain. Beyond performance gains, our study delves into the interplay between LLMs’ internal priors and external retrievals, uncovering key principles that govern generation quality and providing valuable insights for future retrieval-augmented frameworks.

titulo: QEC-LLM: Training Query-focused Extractive Compression Model with LLM-guiding for Open Domain QA
autores: S. Wang; J. Duan; X. Li; H. Wen; Y. Zhang; C. Liu; Z. Yi
venue: 2025 32nd Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference (APSEC)
abstract: The current Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG) pipeline incorporates retrieved contexts as external knowledge to reduce hallucinations, but the large and redundant context makes it difficult for the model to identify key information. In Question-Answering (QA) tasks, large language models (LLMs) can identify query-focused information through extractive compression, simplify redundant long texts and improve the accuracy, but they are resource-intensive and less efficient. To ensure the accuracy of extractive compression and improve its efficiency, we propose a framework for query-focused extractive compression (QEC-LLM) that leverages the LLM’s knowledge and a queryguided mechanism to construct sample sets, effectively training a smaller student model. The student model sorts and scales paragraph sentences based on similarity scores for compression and performance optimization. In addition, since LLM may generate some information that is missing from the student model during the extraction process, our framework will add this supplementary information to the QA prompt and combine it with the extracted information to achieve generative augmentation. We conduct extensive experiments on QA datasets with different compression ratios. The results demonstrate that QECLLM significantly improves end-to-end QA performance and inference efficiency, while demonstrating strong generalization across different retrieval strategies.

titulo: When AI Meets the Web: Prompt Injection Risks in Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugins
autores: Y. Kaya; A. Landerer; S. Pletinckx; M. Zimmermann; C. Kruegel; G. Vigna
venue: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
abstract: Prompt injection attacks pose a critical threat to large language models (LLMs), with prior work focusing on cutting-edge LLM applications like personal copilots. In contrast, simpler LLM applications, such as customer service chatbots, are widespread on the web, yet their security posture and exposure to such attacks remain poorly understood. These applications often rely on third-party chatbot plugins that act as intermediaries to commercial LLM APIs, offering non-expert website builders intuitive ways to customize chatbot behaviors. To bridge this gap, we present the first large-scale study of 17 third-party chatbot plugins used by over $\mathbf{1 0, 0 0 0}$ public websites, uncovering previously unknown prompt injection risks in practice. First, 8 of these plugins (used by 8,000 websites) fail to enforce the integrity of the conversation history transmitted in network requests between the website visitor and the chatbot. This oversight amplifies the impact of direct prompt injection attacks by allowing adversaries to forge conversation histories (including fake system messages), boosting their ability to elicit unintended behavior (e.g., code generation) by $\mathbf{3}-\mathbf{8} \times$. Second, 15 plugins offer tools, such as web-scraping, to enrich the chatbot's context with website-specific content. However, these tools do not distinguish the website's trusted content (e.g., product descriptions) from untrusted, third-party content (e.g., customer reviews), introducing a risk of indirect prompt injection. Notably, we found that $\sim \mathbf{1 3 \%}$ of e-commerce websites have already exposed their chatbots to third-party content. We systematically evaluate both vulnerabilities through controlled experiments grounded in real-world observations, focusing on factors such as system prompt design and the underlying LLM. Our findings show that many plugins adopt insecure practices that undermine the built-in LLM safeguards.

autores: Y. Chen; C. Zhao; Z. Gao; X. Zhang; Q. Fang; Y. Yang; K. Cai
venue: 2026 14th International Conference on Traffic and Logistics Engineering (ICTLE)
abstract: Aeronautical Information Publication (AIP) documents provide authoritative operational information for flight planning, airport operations, and air traffic management. However, their hybrid table–text layouts make reliable knowledge retrieval difficult, particularly when operational questions require field-level table interpretation, cross-section evidence aggregation, or verification of safety-critical constraints. Existing large language model (LLM) based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods usually treat AIP documents as plain text, which can destroy row–column semantics and weaken the traceability of generated answers. To address this problem, this paper proposes a structure-aware RAG framework for AIP knowledge retrieval in intelligent air traffic management. The framework uses separate Schema and Cell retrieval channels to locate field definitions and concrete values, constructs a compact virtual DataFrame from retrieved evidence, and employs a ReAct-based code execution agent for deterministic reasoning. Experiments on a real-world AIP question-answering benchmark covering 11 major civil airports and 500 operational queries show that the proposed framework improves both answer accuracy and traceability compared with unstructured retrieval baselines. Additional analyses of retrieval fusion, model choice, ablation settings, and error types show that preserving table structure is important for aviation-oriented transportation information services.

titulo: Design Process for Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
autores: X. Xu; D. Zhang; W. Zhang; Q. Lu; L. Zhu
venue: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Conference on Software Architecture Companion (ICSA-C)
abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) refers to artificial intelligence systems capable of developing and creating new content such as text, images, audio, or videos based on learned patterns from existing data. Integrating GenAI deeply into more complex software systems poses challenges such as hallucination, out-dated knowledge, non-removable knowledge, and non-traceable reasoning process. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising solution for enabling GenAI systems to incorporate knowledge from external sources. However, there is a lack of systematic guidance on designing a RAG system and identifying critical decision points. This paper presents a design process for a RAG system, including a suitability analysis based on the requirements of specific scenarios and the inherent characteristics of RAG. It outlines the key steps to design a RAG system and discusses critical design decisions. Insights are provided on the impact of design alternatives on the quality attributes of GenAI systems and their tradeoffs. Finally, a feasibility study examines an LLM-based chatbot designed for Q&A in taxation scenarios.

titulo: ElecKG-RAG: an electric knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation framework for power system defect diagnosis
autores: Y. Gu; Y. Yan; B. Guo; Y. Zhou; L. Qi; D. Qi
venue: 5th Energy Conversion and Economics Annual Forum (ECE 2025)
abstract: Defect diagnosis in electrical equipment is critical for effective grid management. titulo: Privacy Risks in Retrieval Augmented and Multi-Agent LLM Architectures Handling PHI
autores: S. K. A. Koduri
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The rapid integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and multi-agent Large Language Models (LLM) is reshaping the healthcare sector, enhancing clinical decision support and patient triage. While these systems enhance reasoning through dynamic knowledge retrieval and agent collaboration, they introduce significant privacy vulnerabilities regarding Protected Health Information (PHI). This paper presents a systematic review and architectural risk analysis of centralized RAG, on-device RAG, and distributed multi-agent structures published between 2023 and 2025. Unlike prior surveys that focus primarily on single-agent chatbots, this work explores how agent cooperation, memory retention, and multi-hop retrieval create emergent PHI leakage vectors. We introduce a formal mathematical risk propagation model to quantify these vulnerabilities and instantiate it through a synthetic Monte Carlo simulation that characterizes how exposure scales across architectures, governance weightings, and multi-hop propagation paths. We further contextualize the model against recently published empirical benchmarks of multi-agent privacy leakage, showing that its qualitative prediction-that inter-agent channels are a substantial source of exposure-is consistent with directly measured leakage rates in independent studies. We conclude by proposing specific benchmarking metrics and privacy-by-architecture principles to support HIPAA-compliant agentic AI deployments.

titulo: GNLM: A Graph-Native Language Model With Road Name Address-Based Spatial Reasoning for Geographic Question Answering
autores: C. -S. Lee; D. -S. Park; J. -M. Choi; H. -J. Chang
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Geographic question answering (QA) requires factually accurate responses grounded in structured spatial knowledge. However, existing approaches based on large language models (LLMs) suffer from factual hallucination, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lacks structural reasoning capabilities. We propose GNLM (Graph-Native Language Model), a novel architecture that restructures the traditional LLM pipeline by performing all reasoning through knowledge graph traversal and restricting the role of LLMs to natural language generation. The knowledge graph is constructed exclusively from government public data sources (building registry, road name addresses) and expert-curated domain knowledge, ensuring factual reliability without LLM-generated content. GNLM introduces four key contributions: 1) a Graph-First, LLM-Last architecture with fact validation that structurally prevents fabrication (all observed errors stem from knowledge gaps, not false generation); 2) an extended Resource Description Framework (RDF) triple attribute model that represents entity properties as independent graph nodes connected by semantic edges, enabling property-level querying and meta-reasoning; 3) coordinate-free spatial reasoning that leverages the Korean road numbering standard (20 m interval,  $k = 10$  m per unit) for proximity ranking without Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates; and 4) a 14-strategy reasoning router that classifies queries into specialized graph traversal algorithms. Evaluated on a real-world dataset of Daejeon, South Korea ( $58{,}882$  nodes,  $80{,}088$  edges from  $58{,}408$  buildings and 711 roads), GNLM achieves 88.4% accuracy on 250 diverse queries with a hallucination rate (HR) of only 5.7% on 35 fact-verification queries, compared to 60.0% for pure LLM, 25.7% for Dense RAG, and 17.1% for GraphRAG—demonstrating a consistent improvement as structural grounding increases. Cross-model validation with llama3.1:8b confirms LLM-agnostic generalizability. Multi-region validation on Sejong City ( $17{,}008$  buildings) with identical methodology confirms cross-region generalizability (Yuseong-gu avg  $\rho = 0.976$ , Sejong avg  $\rho = 0.973$ , both over 10 roads). Road-number-based proximity ranking achieves Spearman  $\rho = 0.9878$  and Precision@ $10= 96.0\%$  against GPS ground truth, with short-range (<500 m) Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of only 31.9 m, demonstrating that structured address numbers alone can effectively preserve spatial ordering without any coordinate data. Cross-road queries, supported via a graph-native intersection topology with 34 annotated intersections, achieve a 90% resolution rate with Spearman  $\rho = 0.701$ —substantially lower than same-road accuracy, indicating a current practical limitation that motivates the multi-hop and automated intersection-detection extensions.

titulo: “Lost-In-The-Later”: Framework for Quantifying Contextual Grounding in Large Language Models
autores: Y. Tao; A. Hiatt; R. Seetharaman; A. Agrawal
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are capable of leveraging both contextual and parametric knowledge but how they prioritize and integrate these sources remains underexplored. We introduce CoPE, a novel framework for systematically quantifying contextual grounding in LLMs. CoPE distinguishes between contextual knowledge (CK) and parametric knowledge (PK), enabling fine-grained attribution across languages and tasks. Using our newly created MultiWikiAtomic dataset in English, Spanish, and Danish, we analyze how LLMs integrate context, prioritize information, and incorporate PK in open-ended question answering. We find that across models and languages, only around 50 to 76 percent of outputs are grounded in the given context, even in knowledge-consistent settings. Grounding drops further in counterfactual scenarios, but not drastically. Our analysis uncovers a phenomenon we call lost-in-the-later, where LLMs tend to overlook information that appears later in a given context, revealing a strong positional bias that affects contextual grounding. We further find that reasoning models, as well as nonreasoning models prompted with Chain-of-Thought (CoT), use context even less than non-reasoning models without CoT and fail to mitigate the lost-in-the-later effect. CoT prompting, in particular, results in lower context recall and shorter responses, leading to degraded contextual grounding. Based on these insights, we design training-free prompt-based methods to effectively leverage input context, consistently improving contextual grounding on average by 12 % across all three languages.

titulo: Grounded Multi-modal Conversation for Zero-shot Visual Question Answering
autores: M. R. Zarei; A. Akkasi; M. Komeili
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics (SMC)
abstract: Zero-shot visual question answering (VQA) poses a formidable challenge at the intersection of computer vision and natural language processing. Traditionally, this problem has been tackled using end-to-end pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs). However, recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) demonstrate their exceptional reasoning and comprehension abilities, making them valuable assets in multi-modal tasks, including zero-shot VQA. LLMs have been previously integrated with VLMs to solve zero-shot VQA in a conversation-based approach. However, while the focus in VQA tasks is often on specific regions rather than the entire image, this aspect has been overlooked in previous approaches. Consequently, the overall performance of the framework relies on the ability of the pre-trained VLM to locate the region of interest that is relevant to the requested visual information within the entire image. To address this challenge, this paper proposes Grounded Multi-modal Conversation for Zero-shot Visual Question Answering (GMC-VQA), a region-based framework that leverages the complementary strengths of LLMs and VLMs in a conversation-based approach. We employ a grounding mechanism to refine visual focus according to the semantics of the question and foster collaborative interaction between VLM and LLM, effectively bridging the gap between visual and textual modalities and enhancing comprehension and response generation for visual queries. We evaluate GMC-VQA across three diverse VQA datasets, achieving substantial average improvements of 10.04% over end-to-end VLMs and 2.52% over the state-of-the-art VLM-LLM communication-based framework, respectively. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/mrzarei5/GMC-VQA.

titulo: VeriChat: An Agentic Conversational AI Assistant for Hardware Security Verification
autores: D. Saha; K. T. Hasan; S. Tarek; S. K. Saha; M. Tehranipoor; F. Farahmandi
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Omni Layer Intelligent Systems (COINS)
abstract: Hardware security verification is a multi-stage process in which engineers must navigate complex design analyses, threat considerations, and verification strategies. They often need security-focused guidance, yet current verification environments provide little structured support for such assistance. Although conversational AI could offer such on-demand assistance, directly using general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT or Gemini is risky due to their tendency to hallucinate and their reliance on static, outdated knowledge. We present VeriChat, a domain-specialized conversational assistant designed to support, rather than replace, existing verification workflows by providing context-aware security guidance. VeriChat employs a retrieval-augmented, multi-agent workflow in which three specialized agents collaboratively minimize hallucinations while improving the transparency and reliability of the response. Beyond question answering, VeriChat integrates open-source EDA tools, including Icarus Verilog, Yosys, and SymbiYosys, to perform syntax checking, synthesis analysis, simulation, and formal verification directly on user-provided RTL designs. Evaluated using a comprehensive methodology, VeriChat achieves a Faithfulness score of 87.73%, significantly outperforming the leading proprietary models. We demonstrate the framework through a hardware Trojan detection case study on an AES S-Box IP, where VeriChat autonomously identifies, simulates, and formally proves a covert key-leakage vulnerability through a multi-turn conversational workflow.

titulo: Building AI Benchmarks from Exam Documents
autores: B. Kressig; N. Koller; I. Schlag
venue: 2026 IEEE Swiss Conference on Data Science and AI (SDS)
abstract: Current AI benchmarks often focus on abstract reasoning and logic rather than the applied skills that professional human workers need on their job. They also frequently suffer from data contamination, as public test sets are often included in model training data. To address this, we present a proof-of-concept pipeline that automatically converts PDF exams into structured AI benchmarks and apply this framework to nonpublic Swiss Federal Professional Exams, representing a first step toward systematic national-level assessment of AI capabilities across professional domains. Our approach uses multimodal Large Language Models to convert the exams into standardized machine-readable formats and an LLM-as-a-judge system to grade a model candidate's answers against official solutions. We evaluated a range of frontier and open-weight models, finding a clear performance hierarchy where frontier models significantly outperform smaller open models. Additionally, we explored the impact of RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG), observing that while it substantially benefits smaller models, it offers limited gains for frontier models which likely already possess more domain knowledge. This work describes a reproducible method for creating robust AI benchmarks from suitable exams in PDF format, and we provide our pipeline as an open-source tool for the community.11Repository: https://github.com/bkressig/exam-to-ai-benchmark

abstract: With the rapid development of aerospace technology in our country, news reports in related fields are increasingly common. titulo: An Intelligent AIOps Framework Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration and Dual-Context Retrieval
autores: Z. Jia; S. Wu
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
abstract: Enterprise operations and maintenance knowledge and runtime evidence are often scattered across manuals, incident reports, monitoring records, and emergency plans. Conventional keyword retrieval is weak in semantic matching and evidence localization, while a single question-answering model often struggles to integrate heterogeneous operational signals for fault-assisted diagnosis. To address these issues, this paper proposes an intelligent AIOps framework based on multi-agent collaboration and dual-context retrieval. The framework first performs document-level global recall to preserve scenario background and then chunk-level local ranking to identify actionable evidence. A unified orchestrator coordinates knowledge, monitoring, decision, notification, and host-management agents to interpret tasks, invoke bounded skills, aggregate cross-source evidence, and return traceable results. A FastAPI and React prototype is implemented and evaluated on a reproducible benchmark built from the open-source Rootly logs dataset and project runbooks. On 85 retrieval cases, dual-context retrieval reaches Recall@5 of 0.98, improves MRR from 0.90 to 0.92, and reduces average retrieval latency among hybrid methods. On 94 fault-diagnosis cases, the full workflow improves Top-1 accuracy from 0.57 to 0.79, action correctness from 0.68 to 0.86 and evidence completeness from 0.47 to 0.91. These results provide preliminary, reproducible evidence that the proposed framework improves evidence grounding and traceable diagnosis in a practical prototype setting.

abstract: This paper provides a comparative study of two major language model (LLM) strategies (instruction-based fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)) for corporate financial question answering. titulo: Personalizing LLMs for Financial Regulation Using RAG and Knowledge Graphs: A Case Study at Regnology

venue: 2026 IEEE 50th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: Financial regulatory documents are characterized by their fine-grained complexity and pronounced heterogeneity, featuring specialized domain-specific content and diverse structural formats that vary across different regulatory frameworks and jurisdictions. titulo: Agentic AI in Healthcare and Medicine: A Seven-Dimensional Taxonomy for Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Agents
autores: S. Vatsal; H. Dubey; A. Singh
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents that plan, use tools and act has begun to shape healthcare and medicine. Reported studies demonstrate competence on various tasks ranging from EHR analysis and differential diagnosis to treatment planning and research workflows. Yet the literature largely consists of overviews which are either broad surveys or narrow dives into a single capability (e.g., memory, planning, reasoning), leaving healthcare work without a common frame. We address this by reviewing 49 studies using a seven-dimensional taxonomy: Cognitive Capabilities, Knowledge Management, Interaction Patterns, Adaptation & Learning, Safety & Ethics, Framework Typology and Core Tasks & Subtasks with 29 operational sub-dimensions. Using explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria and a labeling rubric (Fully Implemented ✓, Partially Implemented  $\Delta $ , Not Implemented ✗), we map each study to the taxonomy and report quantitative summaries of capability prevalence and co-occurrence patterns. Our empirical analysis surfaces clear asymmetries. For instance, the External Knowledge Integration sub-dimension under Knowledge Management is commonly realized (~76% ✓) whereas Event-Triggered Activation sub-dimenison under Interaction Patterns is largely absent (~92% ✗) and Drift Detection & Mitigation sub-dimension under Adaptation & Learning is rare (~98% ✗). Architecturally, Multi-Agent Design sub-dimension under Framework Typology is the dominant pattern (~82% ✓) while orchestration layers remain mostly partial. Across Core Tasks & Subtasks, information centric capabilities lead e.g., Medical Question Answering & Decision Support and Benchmarking & Simulation, while action and discovery oriented areas such as Treatment Planning & Prescription still show substantial gaps (~59% ✗). Together, these findings provide an empirical baseline indicating that current agents excel at retrieval-grounded advising but require stronger adaptation and compliance platforms to move from early-stage systems to dependable systems.

titulo: UQA-RAG: Enhancing Urdu Question-Answer Retrieval With Semantic Similarity and LLMs
autores: T. F. Khan; M. Arslan; F. Alturise; A. H. Almutairi; M. T. Raza
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Urdu Question Answering (QA) systems struggle with limited annotated resources and linguistic complexities. These are significant hurdles for traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) that rely on static, pre-trained knowledge. This paper introduces UQA-RAG, a new framework to enhance Urdu QA by using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over the multi-domain UNQA dataset. It fuses results from OpenAI’s text-embedding-3-small vectors (Semantic) with BM25 (Lexical) using the Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) algorithm. titulo: Rethinking Retrieval: A Hybrid Contextual Pipeline for Open-Domain QA with LLMs
autores: Z. Rizwan
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) perform well in open-domain question answering but often suffer from factual errors and loss of context when using flat chunk-based retrieval. Candidate results are fused, reranked, and used to generate grounded answers. Evaluated on a 100,000-document Wikipedia corpus, our approach outperforms baseline hybrid retrieval, showing consistent gains in recall and speed, while also improving efficiency. The results demonstrate that integrating contextualized chunking with query expansion strengthens retrieval-augmented generation, making it more robust and precise open-domain QA.

titulo: Leveraging Metadata and LLM Context to Overcome RAG Challenges and Limitations
autores: S. Mukherjee
venue: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering (ICBDSE)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has gained prominence for developing chatbots interacting with document repositories, yet substantial empirical evidence indicates critical failures due to inherent vector search limitations, context fragmentation from chunking, and high maintenance complexity. titulo: When Not to Answer: Confidence-Aware Response Control for Hallucination Reduction in Consumer Rights Question Answering
autores: A. K; K. V; D. G
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as legal assistance and consumer rights support, where response accuracy is of paramount importance; however, a critical challenge in such deployments is hallucination-the generation of factually incorrect or unverified statements that may mislead users and cause tangible harm. This work introduces the notion of a confidence-aware response control system that aims to improve the robustness of consumer rights questions answered through the use of large language models by combining RAG with multi-signal confidence assessment, which uses three different signals: semantic similarity, lexical overlap, and context coverage. These scores are then aggregated using a weighted scoring function to obtain a final confidence score, where if the confidence score is below a certain threshold value determined experimentally through grid search using F1-optimal values then the system chooses not to reply. The threshold selection process and weight configurations are empirically justified through sensitivity analysis and an ablation study. The interpretable and scalar-valued confidence indicator also offers a lightweight version of explainability, making the decision process of the system easily understandable for the operators. In an experimental setup conducted using 30 questions related to consumer rights, the system achieved 90% accuracy and hallucinations to only $\mathbf{1 0 \%}$, thus outperforming a baseline LLM (63.3% accuracy, 36.7% hallucination rate) and a RAG-only system (80% accuracy, 20% hallucination rate). This approach requires no model retraining and introduces negligible computational overhead (under 100 ms additional latency), making it practical for real-world deployment and establishing abstention-based response control as an effective safety mechanism for LLM-based legal applications.

titulo: Agentic Graph RAG: Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Retrieval and Reasoning Over the MITRE ATLAS Knowledge Graph
autores: S. Solanki; B. Kumar
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Combining large language models (LLMs) with structured knowledge graphs can be a potential way of addressing issues with reliability and explainability of question answering systems in particular domains. While LLMs have been shown to be effective at natural language understanding, they may still hallucinate or fail to perform well on structured tasks because of a lack of grounding. In contrast, although knowledge graphs explicitly represent entities and their relationships, accessing them through query languages such as Cypher requires specialized expertise. In this paper, we propose an Agentic Graph RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG) framework that combines implicit and explicit retrieval within an agentic pipeline. Specifically, our framework includes (i) implicit retrieval, which relies on semantic similarity over vector embeddings to identify relevant information contextually, and (ii) explicit retrieval, involving natural language-to-Cypher query generation and its execution to obtain precise results from the knowledge graph. The explicit retrieval pipeline incorporates validation and correction loops to ensure schema-compliant Cypher query generation, and both retrieval strategies are integrated into a unified agentic workflow. Our framework operates on a semi-structured knowledge graph constructed from MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems) YAML data and deployed in a Neo4j database. The proposed framework is evaluated using an LLM-as-a-Judge setup based on the correctness metric. Experimental results demonstrate that implicit retrieval achieves correctness scores between 0.51-0.58, while explicit retrieval improves performance to $0.73-0.91$. The proposed hybrid agentic framework achieves the best performance, reaching correctness scores of up to 0.98, demonstrating that integrating implicit semantic retrieval with explicit Cypher-based knowledge graph querying significantly improves answer correctness.

autores: K. Zou; Y. Bai; B. Liu; Y. Chen; Z. Chen; Y. Zhou; X. Yuan; M. Wang; X. Shen; X. Cao; Y. C. Tham; H. Fu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Medical phrase grounding is crucial for identifying relevant regions in medical images based on phrase queries, facilitating accurate image analysis and diagnosis. titulo: ConCise: Training-Free Conclusion-Chain State Compression for Cost-Efficient Multi-Step RAG Services
autores: K. Yan; Z. Tang; T. Wang; W. Jia
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
abstract: Multi-step retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has been widely deployed as LLM-powered web services for complex question answering, where iterative retrievalreasoning rounds deliver strong multi-hop accuracy. However, this paradigm causes historical documents and reasoning traces to accumulate across rounds, inflating cumulative input tokens approximately as $O\left(N^{2}\right)$ with progressively increasing noise density. In API-based service architectures, such growth directly amplifies per-request billing cost, network payload, and response latency. Existing compression approaches rely on pretrained modules or GPU-level KV cache access, introducing model hosting overhead incompatible with API-native, Serverless, and edge-side deployments. To address this issue, this paper proposes ConCise, a training-free state-layer protocol that restructures cross-round context transmission for multi-step RAG services. Specifically, ConCise replaces raw-text accumulation with an append-only chain of structured conclusions, compressing cumulative context growth from $O\left(N^{2}\right)$ to approximately $O(N)$. Furthermore, a fused generation mechanism is introduced to jointly emit reasoning and conclusions in a single API call, eliminating repeated input billing from serial dual-invocation overhead. Extensive experiments across twelve paired configurations spanning three models, two datasets, and two representative frameworks demonstrate that ConCise achieves 64.63% average token savings while maintaining acceptable accuracy, providing a plug-and-play, deployment-friendly solution for cost-efficient multi-step RAG service optimization.

The synthesis reveals that LLM-based systems dominate recent developments, offering enhanced contextual understanding and adaptive feedback. However, challenges remain regarding scalability, error interpretation, and alignment with instructional design principles. Findings indicate that NLPpowered chatbots significantly improve learner engagement, motivation, and conceptual understanding by enabling natural language query generation and real-time feedback. Nonetheless, pedagogical grounding and long-term learning evaluation are limited. The review identifies key future directions, including pedagogically informed feedback mechanisms, scalable model design, and integration into learning management systems. titulo: Mitigating Bias and Hallucinations in LLMs Through Prompt Engineering and Knowledge-Grounded Approaches in Healthcare Domain

venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Advanced Research in Computing (ICARC)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in healthcare for clinical question answering and information support, yet their deployment is constrained by risks of hallucinated content and embedded bias that can compromise patient safety. This study proposes an integrated mitigation framework that combines advanced prompt engineering with knowledge-grounded approaches, specifically Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), without modifying underlying model parameters. titulo: Evaluating Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Context for Multiple-Choice Question Answering
autores: M. Ghanbari; R. Dividino
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Knowledge Graph (ICKG)
abstract: Despite their impressive capabilities, Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to access knowledge not encoded during pre-training. In-context learning (ICL) addresses this limitation by embedding relevant information directly in the prompt, enabling LLMs to use external knowledge without updating their parameters. Recent research has explored integrating knowledge from knowledge graphs (KGs) into prompts, as KGs offer structured and factual representations of concepts and their relationships. A common strategy involves identifying key concepts in the task, grounding them in the KG, extracting subgraphs that connect question and answer concepts, and incorporating the corresponding statements into the prompts. However, a major challenge in ICL is selecting appropriate knowledge, that is, information that supports the model's reasoning and improves performance, while minimizing irrelevant or noisy content that can reduce accuracy. This study investigates how the representation of knowledge in prompts and the relevance and scope of task-grounded KG knowledge affect LLM performance on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) tasks. We compare triple-based versus path-based representations, assess relevance filtering strategies, and evaluate different knowledge processing approaches. Our findings show that path-based representations outperform triple-based approaches but are more sensitive to noise. While KG-based knowledge can enhance LLM reasoning, imprecise selection of relevant knowledge can degrade performance below the zero-shot baseline (where no additional context is provided), highlighting the challenge of integrating KG knowledge without task-specific selection strategies. Expanding the scope of extracted subgraphs increases recall (retrieving more relevant information) but reduces precision (as more noise is also included). These findings underscore the critical importance of balancing informativeness with noise reduction in KG-enhanced LLM systems. Source code is publicly available at https://github.com/maryam-ghanbari/KGSweetSpot.

titulo: CTIS-QA: Clinical Template-Informed Slide-Level Question Answering for Pathology
autores: H. Lu; Z. Qian; Y. Li; Y. Zhou; B. Wei; Y. Xu
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated strong performance in patch-level pathological image analysis; however, they often lack the holistic perceptual capability necessary for comprehensive Whole Slide Image (WSI) interpretation. Recent approaches have explored constructing slide-level MLLMs using VQA datasets that are entirely generated from pathology reports by large language models (LLMs). However, these datasets suffer from critical limitations: hallucinated content, information leakage in question stems, clinically irrelevant or visual independent questions, and the omission of essential diagnostic features-issues that undermine both data quality and clinical validity. In this paper, we introduce a clinical diagnosis template-based pipeline to collect pathological information. In collaboration with pathologists and guided by the the College of American Pathologists (CAP) Cancer Protocols, we design a Clinical Pathology Report Template (CPRT) that ensures comprehensive and standardized extraction of diagnostic elements from pathology reports. We validate the effectiveness of our pipeline on TCGA-BRCA. First, we extract pathological features from reports using CPRT. These features are then used to build CTIS-Align, a dataset of 80k slide-description pairs from 804 WSIs for vision-language alignment training, and CTISBench, a rigorously curated VQA benchmark comprising 977 WSIs and 14,879 question-answer pairs. CTIS-Bench emphasizes clinically grounded, closed-ended questions (e.g., tumor grade, receptor status) that reflect real diagnostic workflows, minimize non-visual reasoning, and require genuine slide understanding. We further propose CTIS-QA, a Slide-level Question Answering model, featuring a dual-stream architecture that mimics pathologists' diagnostic approach. One stream captures global slidelevel context via clustering-based feature aggregation, while the other focuses on salient local regions through attention-guided patch perception module. Extensive experiments on WSI-VQA, CTIS-Bench, and slide-level diagnostic tasks show that CTIS-QA consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art models across multiple metrics. We will fully release both CTIS-Bench and CTIS-QA as open-source resources.
