autores: S. Agarwal
venue: 2026 IEEE 13th International Conference on Intelligent Systems (IS)
abstract: While there is some evidence that large language models (LLMs) can facilitate psychoeducation, symptom monitoring, structured self-help, and between-session care, evidence from the previous generation of rule-based or retrieval-based chatbots does not necessarily carry over to generative models. LLM chatbots therefore should be assessed as a change in clinical-technical systems of care and an additional supervised tool, not as a substitute for professional care.

venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications are rapidly moving from general capability demonstrations to domain-specific engineering applications. Unlike public benchmark evaluations, project acceptance testing emphasizes whether a delivered system can provide correct retrieval, faithful generation, traceable evidence, and operationally usable answers under fixed business data, knowledge-base boundaries, and delivery requirements. Existing evaluation practices are often insufficient for Text-to-SQL, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and GraphRAG systems because their retrieval outputs differ substantially in structure and are difficult to evaluate under a unified criterion. To address this problem, this paper proposes a standard-constrained evaluation framework that combines automatic assessment and expert scoring for engineering-oriented LLM applications. The framework converts heterogeneous retrieval outputs into answer semantic units (ASUs), aligns predicted ASU lists with gold ASU lists, and computes retrieval-stage precision, recall, and F1-score using a unified true-positive, false-positive, and false-negative protocol. For the generation stage, ROUGE-L is adopted to measure the sequence-level similarity between system answers and reference answers, while domain-expert scoring is used to complement automatic metrics in terms of business correctness, completeness, traceability, and usability. A prototype experiment on a desensitized government intelligent question-answering system demonstrates that the proposed framework can reduce repetitive assessment cost while maintaining high agreement with expert judgment. The framework provides a reusable, interpretable, and auditable basis for acceptance testing, model selection, and iterative optimization of engineering-oriented LLM applications.

titulo: UniRS-Instruct: A Principle-Guided Unified Instruction-Following Dataset for Remote Sensing Understanding
autores: L. Xu; Y. Wang; L. Zhao; W. Guo; Q. Li; K. Long; K. Zou; W. Yang; D. Zhou
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
abstract: Driven by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), remote sensing image (RSI) understanding is undergoing a paradigm shift, evolving from learning a domain-specific model to learning a general foundation model with domain adaptation (LaGD). Under the LaGD paradigm, conventional datasets, such as DOTA and RSICD, which fueled progress in RSI understanding over the past decade, are no longer adequate for emerging tasks because their annotation formats are task-specific and lack the language-level supervision required by MLLMs. We argue that a new dataset must be purposefully designed to support three core capabilities: First, generalization, enabling models to learn shared knowledge across tasks through a unified annotation format; Second, complex scene understanding, training models to capture fine-grained object attributes and spatial relationships and to describe scenes in detailed natural language; Finally, reasoning, equipping models with high-level visual reasoning through multiturn dialogues. To this end, we present UniRS-Instruct, a high-quality, diversified, and unified multimodal instruction-following dataset for RSI understanding. UniRS-Instruct unifies diverse tasks, including image captioning, visual question answering, visual grounding, and region-level captioning, into a consistent (question and answer) format. To construct fine-grained and context-aware instruction data, we propose a hierarchical prompting strategy: at the local level, objects are identified via rotated bounding boxes to describe their fine-grained attributes and spatial relationships; at the global level, local information is integrated with the full image to generate detailed scene-level instruction descriptions through GPT-4 V. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that MLLMs fine-tuned with UniRS-Instruct achieve superior performance in image captioning, visual question answering, and visual grounding tasks, and exhibit stronger capabilities in describing fine-grained information, uncovering implicit knowledge, and conducting complex reasoning compared with models trained on existing datasets.

titulo: Trustworthy Natural-Language Analytics Over Private Smart Home IoT Data via Time-Aware RAG
autores: Q. Dan; F. Bellù; S. B. Felix; M. Cerutti; M. Brambilla
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Applications, Communications and Networking (SmartNets)
abstract: Natural-language question answering over private Internet of Things (IoT) data is a promising interface for smart home analytics, but existing large language model (LLM) assistants remain unreliable because they cannot directly access sensor logs, and conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) does not adequately embed temporal constraints. As a result, retrieval may be dominated by evidence that is semantically relevant but temporally incorrect, leading to plausible yet untrustworthy answers. To address this limitation, we propose TA-RAG, a time-aware RAG architecture that treats time as a first-class execution constraint across temporal parsing, indexing, retrieval, and grounded response generation. Our method converts multivariate IoT logs into hourly textual evidence, normalizes temporal expressions into executable retrieval plans, restricts retrieval to the relevant temporal partitions, and enforces timestamped citations in the final answer. Evaluated on real smart home sensor logs, compared with standard RAG, TA-RAG improves temporal plan correctness from 20.83% to 66.67%, increases retrieval precision and coverage while reducing temporal leakage, and achieves 96.96% citation compliance with only 3.87% unsupported claims. These results show that plan-constrained retrieval is an effective design principle for trustworthy natural-language analytics.

titulo: Post-hoc Verification of LLMs with Knowledge Graphs for Medical Question Answering
autores: I. Boutra; H. Slimi; M. Y. Haouam; I. Bendib
venue: 2025 International Conference on Recent Advances in Mathematics and Informatics (ICRAMI)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in natural language processing and show strong potential for medical question answering (QA). Their ability to process biomedical literature and generate coherent responses makes them attractive for clinical and research applications. However, their deployment in high-stakes domains is limited due to critical issues such as hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and lack of verifiability. These shortcomings undermine reliability and highlight the need for mechanisms that can ensure factual grounding. We propose a lightweight post-hoc verification framework that integrates LLMs with biomedical Knowledge Graphs (KGs). Using the Gene Ontology (GO) as a domain-specific resource, our framework extracts factual statements from LLM-generated responses, reformulates them as KG queries, and validates them against curated biomedical knowledge. Unsupported claims are flagged or corrected through an optional refinement loop, improving factual consistency without requiring retraining or fine-tuning of the base LLM. We evaluate the framework on two datasets with different characteristics: PubMedQA, a benchmark of general biomedical questions derived from PubMed abstracts, and GO-QA, a domain-specific dataset constructed from Gene Ontology concepts. Results show consistent improvements in factual accuracy, with BERT-F1 increasing from 0.4110 to 0.4245 on PubMedQA and from 0.8242 to 0.8405 on GO-QA. These findings demonstrate that posthoc KG verification is a practical and generalizable strategy for enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of LLM-based medical QA systems.

titulo: Structure Pruning With LLMs for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
autores: M. Xu; K. Chen; X. Bai; M. Yang; T. Zhao; M. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
abstract: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) requires multi-step reasoning over a large, structured search space, where free-form LLM planning can hallucinate intermediate subgraphs or query sketches and yield unexecutable reasoning. READS constructs a token-level constrained decoding tree from KG-reachable candidates and uses LLM scoring to traverse and prune the search space, improving executability and faithfulness. READS obtains training supervision by parsing annotated SPARQL queries, assuming benchmark-provided topic entities. On WebQSP and CWQ, READS achieves 0.840/0.845 and 0.802/0.820 in Hits@1/F1, outperforming strong LLM-based baselines.

abstract: Recently, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown excellent reasoning capabilities in various fields. venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
abstract: Multimodal (MM) large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success in image- and region-level remote sensing (RS) image understanding tasks, such as image captioning (IC), visual question answering (VQA), and visual grounding. Extensive experiments verify the effectiveness and superiority of GeoPix in pixel-level segmentation tasks while also maintaining competitive performance in image- and region-level benchmarks. titulo: Cost-Aware LLM Invocation Strategies in Large-Scale Enterprise Systems
autores: S. C. Kumar Paidi
venue: 2026 International Conference Automatics, Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (ICARAI)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming central to production pipelines at companies of all sizes. At scale, however, a tradeoff emerges: more capable models complete individual tasks more successfully, but charge per-token rates linearly proportional to that capacity. Billions of tokens are served daily at production companies, making this tradeoff one of cost versus quality. Companies that serve millions of requests per day cannot afford cost overruns or spikes in latency. Routing all traffic through a single large model is costly because many requests are simple. In practice, companies use heuristic approaches or manual rulesets that do not transfer well between workflows. In this paper, we address this challenge by presenting CALLS (Cost-Aware LLM Load-balancing Strategy), a strategy for selecting one of a fleet of model tiers for each query based on its estimated complexity. CALLS offers: (i) a lightweight complexity classifier that uses features capturing the syntax and semantics of the input query, (ii) a simple yet expressive three-tier routing policy based on a formalization of the cost-utility tradeoff, and (iii) an online feedback loop that calibrates the complexity thresholds used in the classifier based on observed response quality. We evaluate CALLS on four classes of enterprise tasks: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), code assistance, long-document summarization, and question answering, and demonstrate that it decreases inference cost on a corpus of 48k production queries by 61.4% while losing only 3.2% of its quality relative to serving all traffic through a large model. Compared with state-of-the-art adaptive nearest cohort techniques, CALLS yields an additional 14.7% improvement with negligible quality loss.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities in general-purpose text generation although they face serious reliability challenges in financial analysis-a domain where precision and currency are non-negotiable. titulo: Towards Robust Clinical Reasoning in LLM-aided Clinical Decision Support
autores: S. Vuruma; S. Tang; D. Wu
venue: 2026 IEEE 14th International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI)
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated advanced reasoning capabilities, their deployment in safety-critical healthcare settings requires rigorous evaluation beyond predictive performance. In Clinical Decision Support (CDS), LLMs can act as reasoners that can process longitudinal patient data and explore the impact of hypothetical treatment scenarios. However, predictive accuracy alone is insufficient when such systems are used to simulate ‘what-if’ outcomes under alter-native interventions where ground truth observations don’t exist. Ensuring counterfactual robustness under input perturbations is essential for safe deployment.Counterfactual evaluation of LLMs, especially for time-series forecasting, is a growing but underexplored area. Existing work largely focuses on fairness auditing under demographic perturbations or on factual consistency in static question-answering settings. There is no established framework for evaluating LLM responses and reasoning to intervention-like perturbations in longitudinal clinical care where ground truth outcomes are unobservable and model consistency is the only available signal [1]. This gap is particularly consequential in HIV care where treatment decisions are sequential, confounded by patient history, and carry significant downstream consequences.In prior work, we conducted a case study in HIV care evaluating LLM behavior on a longitudinal forecasting task using structured patient histories. Using the HealthGym synthetic dataset [2], we evaluated four state-of-the-art LLMs on next step prediction of Viral Load (VL), CD4 and Relative CD4 under immutable perturbations to patient gender, ethnicity [3] and a mutable perturbation to base drug combination. Agreement-based analyses were used to characterize model behavior under controlled modifications to demographic attributes and treatment regimens. Findings indicated that counterfactual stability is strongly outcome-dependent and that numerical divergence can coexist with apparent clinical agreement, revealing failure modes that accuracy-based evaluations do not capture [4].Building on this, this research project aims to develop principled methodologies for both evaluating and improving counter-factual reasoning in LLM-based clinical systems. Specifically, our study aims are to address (1) How can stability and divergence across models be systematically quantified under intervention-like perturbations in longitudinal data? (2) Can targeted fine-tuning strategies that utilize synthetic trajectory data reduce the sensitivity of the model to clinical perturbations while maintaining predictive reliability? (3) Can the evaluation framework developed in HIV care be applied to other longitudinal clinical settings, and what adaptations are required?To address these questions, in the short term, we plan to construct controlled evaluation pipelines using publicly available longitudinal datasets, with perturbations grounded in clinically meaningful intervention scenarios. Fairness-aware analysis will be incorporated to audit sensitivity to demographic attributes. Synthetic data generation approaches will be explored both for stress-testing models and enriching training data. In the long term, we will investigate the portability of this evaluation frame-work to other longitudinal clinical settings where intervention effects are clinically meaningful, adapting perturbation design and stability metrics to domain-specific requirements.Expected contributions include: (1) a principled evaluation framework for counterfactual robustness in LLM-aided clinical decision support, (2) fine-tuning strategies to reduce model sensitivity while maintaining predictive reliability, and (3) empirical evidence on the portability of the evaluation framework across longitudinal clinical domains.This work has implications across three levels. For HIV care, it provides clinicians and system designers with concrete tools for auditing LLM reliability before deployment in treatment planning and treatment adherence support workflows. More broadly, the proposed evaluation framework offers a reusable methodology that can be extended to other longitudinal CDS tasks, establishing a standard for robustness assessment that complements existing accuracy-based benchmarks. From an AI methods perspective, this work contributes to the emerging literature on consistency-based reliability evaluation [5], positioning inter-model agreement under perturbation as a proxy for sensitivity evaluation in settings where ground truth is unavailable.

titulo: SARW: A Secure Semantic Watermarking Framework for Data Ownership and Attribution in RAG Knowledge Bases
autores: Y. Wang; Z. Zhang; Z. Qin; Z. Wang; Z. Li; L. Zhu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the factual accuracy and temporal relevance of large language model (LLM) outputs by integrating external knowledge sources, driving its widespread adoption in real-world applications. However, this explicit dependence on retrievable knowledge repositories introduces significant risks of intellectual property (IP) leakage and unauthorized reuse, elevating IP protection in RAG systems to a critical concern. While text watermarking techniques have advanced considerably, they often fail in RAG contexts. LLMs frequently rephrase, summarize, or semantically reorganize retrieved content during generation, severely degrading the persistence and detectability of conventional watermarks embedded directly in source documents or outputs. To overcome this limitation, we propose Semantic Atom-based RAG Watermarking (SARW), a distributed watermarking framework purpose-built for RAG ecosystems. SARW decomposes copyright statements into structured semantic graphs and extracts verifiable semantic atoms. These atoms are covertly embedded into knowledge base documents using natural language steganography, with topic-aware matching and retrieval-ranking optimization ensuring alignment with semantically relevant host documents. Extensive experiments demonstrate SARW's efficacy: it achieves most configurations exceed 90% detection accuracy across general and domain-specific question-answering benchmarks while exhibiting resilience against knowledge-base tampering, paraphrasing, and partial retrieval attacks, validating its practicality for secure attribution in RAG knowledge bases through retrieved-context-level verification.

titulo: Explain-RAG: An Explainable RAG Framework with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning, NLI Verification, and Source Attribution
autores: S. Nadaf; U. B. Chavan
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has brought a potent way of supplementing the factual accuracy of large language model (LLM) responses through external knowledge sources. Nevertheless, the conventional RAG pipelines tend to hide as black boxes, with not much information on how answers are produced, checked and justified through the retrieved content. We presented Explain-RAG, an explainable RAG framework that strives to improve trustworthiness and interpretability in question answering systems in the work. Its structure combines three fundamental elements: (1) Chain-ofThought (CoT) reasoning where the model articulates the step-by-step rationale of its logic prior to providing a final answer; (2) Natural Language Inference (NLI) validation, which checks to ensure that the presented evidence may clearly support the given answer that might include an entailment label and a confidence score; (3) Source Attribution that measures the contribution of each retrieved document to the generated response. Unison of these elements offers verifiable, readable, and understandable responses. Explain-RAG is domain-independent, flexible, and not a black-box generation system, means a more transparent solution to black-box generation system. We found that it makes both explainability and factual trust better without any domainspecific fine-tuning.

titulo: ADP: Answer-oriented Distinction Perception for End-to-end Clarification Question Generation
autores: Y. Chen; Y. Fan; Y. Li; C. Ding; Y. Hong
venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Clarification Question Generation (abbr., CQG) is crucial for ambiguous question answering. It produces the structured "clarification question" to reveal the intention and possible answers. Currently, the existing CQG approach is grounded on a pipeline mode, i.e., predicting possible answers first, and further performing CQG accordingly. This approach is applicable and obtains promising performance. However, it suffers from an unavoidable bottleneck that the distinctions among the answers are difficult to perceive, while such distinctions reveal significantly different intentions of questions. Without the ability of distinction perception and differentiation, the generator easily falls into the hallucination caused by distracting intentions. To address the issues, we construct an end-to-end CQG model using multitask learning. In particular, we propose an Answer-oriented Distinction Perception (ADP) approach to enhance the multi-task learning process. Specifically, ADP conducts comparison between a pair of possible answers, and instructs the Large Language Model (LLM) to summarize their distinction. We integrate ADP into the multi-task learning framework, progressively coupling it with possible answer generation and CQG to form different auxiliary tasks. The goal is to obtain the generalized distinction-aware CQG model. In our experiments, we use LLaMA3 as the backbone of CQG, and fine-tune it by multi-task learning. We leverage ChatGPT to produce the distinction descriptions among possible answers, and use them as observable evidence to fine-tune LLaMA3 for ADP. We evaluate our CQG model on the benchmark dataset CAmbigNQ. The test result shows that our ADP-based end-to-end CQG obtains substantial improvements compared to the pipeline CQG model. In addition, we apply our CQG model to the downstream ambiguous question answering task, and achieve an F1-score of 45.1% with an improvement of 5.9% at best (4.1% at worst).

titulo: PersonalAI: A Systematic Comparison of Knowledge Graph Storage and Retrieval Approaches for Personalized LLM Agents

abstract: Personalizing language models by effectively incorporating user interaction history remains a central challenge in the development of adaptive AI systems. titulo: VideoExpert: Augmented LLM for Temporal-Sensitive Video Understanding
autores: H. Zhao; G. -P. Ji; R. Yan; H. Xiong; Z. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
abstract: The core challenge in video understanding lies in perceiving dynamic content changes over time. However, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with temporal-sensitive video tasks, such as video temporal grounding, which requires generating timestamps to mark the occurrence of specific events. Existing strategies require MLLMs to generate absolute or relative timestamps directly. We have observed that those MLLMs tend to rely more on language patterns than visual cues when generating timestamps, affecting their performance. To address this problem, we propose VideoExpert, a general-purpose MLLM suitable for several temporal-sensitive video tasks. Inspired by the expert concept, VideoExpert integrates two parallel modules: the Temporal Expert and the Spatial Expert. The Temporal Expert is responsible for modeling time sequences and performing temporal grounding. It processes high-frame-rate yet compressed tokens to capture dynamic variations in videos and includes a lightweight prediction head for precise event localization. The Spatial Expert focuses on content detail analysis and instruction following. It handles specially designed spatial tokens and language input, aiming to generate content-related responses. These two experts collaborate seamlessly via a special token <LOC>, ensuring coordinated temporal grounding and content generation. Notably, the Temporal and Spatial Experts maintain independent parameter sets. This parameter decoupling design enables specialized learning within each part without mutual interference. By offloading temporal grounding from content generation, VideoExpert prevents text pattern biases in timestamp predictions. Moreover, we introduce a Spatial Compress module to obtain spatial tokens. This module filters and compresses patch tokens while preserving key information, delivering compact yet detail-rich input for the Spatial Expert. Extensive experiments conducted on four widely-used benchmarks (i.e. Charades-STA, QVHighlight, YouCookII and NextGQA) across four tasks (temporal grounding, highlight detection, dense video captioning and grounding question answering) demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of the VideoExpert.

autores: N. Frahm; P. Patel; Y. Zhang; S. Yu; M. Bansal; R. Sengupta

abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) have improved embodied question answering (EQA) agents by providing strong semantic priors for open-vocabulary reasoning. However, when used directly for step-level exploration, VLMs often exhibit frontier oscillations, unstable back-and-forth movements caused by overconfidence and miscalibration, leading to inefficient navigation and degraded answer quality. We propose Prune-Then-Plan, a simple and effective framework that stabilizes exploration through step-level calibration. Instead of trusting raw VLM scores, our method prunes implausible frontier choices using a Holm-Bonferroni inspired pruning procedure and then delegates final decisions to a coverage-based planner. This separation converts overconfident predictions into conservative, interpretable actions by relying on human-level judgments to calibrate the step-level behavior of VLMs. Integrated into the 3D-Mem EQA framework, our approach achieves relative improvements of up to 49% and 33% in visually grounded SPL and LLM-Match metrics, respectively, over baselines. Overall, our method achieves better scene coverage under equal exploration budgets on both OpenEQA and EXPRESS-Bench datasets. We provide additional visuals of results on our Project Page.

titulo: EvaRAG: Evaluating Advanced RAG Techniques With Indexing and Distance Metrics
autores: H. Elkiran; J. Rasheed
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge. Yet, the performance of RAG pipelines is susceptible to design choices across retrieval, similarity metrics, indexing, and reranking. Despite growing adoption, little systematic work has explored the trade-offs between retrieval quality, semantic accuracy, computational efficiency, and cost in RAG systems. This study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive evaluation of RAG configurations across multiple dimensions. We propose a benchmarking framework that systematically varies retrievers (Fusion, HyDe, Hierarchical, SCaNN), indexing methods (HNSW, IVF, Flat), similarity metrics (Cosine, Inner Product, L2), and rerankers (BGE, minilm) over datasets of three scales (small, medium, and large). Performance is assessed through coverage, recall, MRR, and nDCG, while semantic quality is measured using correctness, faithfulness, and relevance. Efficiency is quantified via latency, throughput, and computational cost. Our experiments reveal that HNSW–IP–Fusion–minilm achieves the strongest semantic performance, with Coverage Retrieval of 0.942, Correctness of 0.909, and Faithfulness of 0.970, making it ideal for accuracy-critical tasks. Conversely, IVF–L2–Hierarchical demonstrates the lowest latency (1.736 ns) and cost, making it suitable for real-time deployments. Reranker analysis shows modest but consistent gains for minilm over BGE, while HyDe excels in precision at the expense of efficiency. Notably, no single configuration dominates; optimal designs depend on the application’s needs, whether it is maximizing semantic accuracy, minimizing latency, or striking a balance between the two. By demonstrating concrete trade-offs, this work provides a practical foundation for scaling RAG pipelines across diverse domains, including information retrieval, enterprise search, and knowledge-intensive reasoning.

autores: H. Guo; Z. Liu; C. Tang; X. Zhang

abstract: With the wide application of large language models (LLMs) and the rapid growth of metaverse tourism demand, the digital tour and personalized interaction of historical sites have become the key to improving users’ digital travel experience. titulo: LexPulse: An Adaptive Relationship-Aware RAG System for E-Governance Legal Policy Retrieval
autores: L. Pallavi; P. V. Reddy; P. Harini; P. Chalamalasetti; P. Varshini
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has significantly improved question-answering systems; however, conventional RAG frameworks struggle to retrieve legally accurate information from evolving government policies because they treat legal documents as independent entities and fail to model relationships between laws and their amendments. Consequently, existing legal question-answering systems often produce outdated responses, overlook legislative amendments, and generate hallucinated information. To address these limitations, this paper proposes LexPulse, a relationship-aware RAG framework for e-governance policy retrieval that models amendment relationships using metadata-based document links. The proposed framework integrates hybrid retrieval using BM25, ChromaDB, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), together with a metadata-based relationship resolver for amendment-aware query expansion. In addition, automatic context tagging distinguishes active and superseded provisions, while an adaptive LLM fallback mechanism handles out-of-domain queries using the language model’s parametric knowledge. Experimental evaluation on 51 legal questions and 18 amendment-related benchmark questions achieved accuracies of 70.6% and 72.2%, respectively. These results indicate improved legal-policy retrieval compared with conventional RAG.

titulo: Islamic Questions Answering Systems for Arabic Language: A Survey of Approaches, Limitations, and Opportunities in the Era of Generative AI
autores: M. Al-Qahtani; B. Al-Khamees; M. Ykhlef
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Artificial Intelligence Applications (ISAA)
abstract: Arabic is spoken by more than 400 million people worldwide; however, its linguistic characteristics, including rich morphology and dialectal variation, pose significant challenges for natural language processing. Consequently, developing effective Arabic Islamic question answering (QA) systems remains difficult, particularly due to the linguistic complexity of Arabic and the limited availability of high-quality domain-specific datasets. In the Islamic domain, QA systems are increasingly important for facilitating access to religious sources. This paper presents a systematic survey of Arabic Islamic QA systems, analyzing existing approaches, datasets, and evaluation metrics. The review follows a structured literature selection process based on predefined criteria and PRISMA guidelines to identify relevant studies published between 2014 and 2025. The analyzed studies are categorized into traditional information retrieval approaches, pretrained language models (PLMs), large language models (LLMs) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frameworks. The comparative analysis shows a clear shift from keyword-based methods to transformer-based and LLM-driven architectures, which demonstrate improved performance on Quranic QA benchmarks, with reported results reaching F1-scores up to 95% and pAP@10 values of 0.637. Based on these findings, the paper highlights key challenges and recommends future research directions, including the development of robust Arabic Islamic QA datasets, instruction-tuned Arabic LLMs, and RAG-based architectures to improve factual grounding and reduce hallucinations.

titulo: Persistent Goal-Tracking and Instruction-Driven Reasoning in Sequential Conversation QA
autores: Q. -D. Ngo; Q. -D. Dang; L. -H. Phan
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Traditional conversational Question Answering (QA) systems focus on isolated information retrieval and lack the ability to maintain goal persistence across multi-turn interactions. Current Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches operate passively, retrieving information turn-by-turn without tracking whether the overall task objective has been achieved, and are typically evaluated using linguistic similarity metrics rather than functional task outcomes. We introduce GSC-QA (Goal-based Sequential Conversation QA), a framework that integrates three complementary components into a unified enterprise dialogue architecture: 1) persistent Goal Tracking Module (GTM) that maintains task state across turns in external databases (Redis + PostgreSQL), decoupled from the LLM context window; 2) Expert Instruction Layer that injects domain-curated procedural constraints into every response generation step; and 3) proactive slot detection that identifies and elicits missing required information before proceeding. Unlike prior task-oriented systems that assume static ontologies or session-scoped memory, GSC-QA combines retrieval, instruction enforcement, and goal persistence in a single coordinated loop built on LangGraph. Evaluated on 1,516 annotated dialogue records in Vietnamese spanning ten enterprise domains (principally beauty services, professional services, fashion & retail, spa & wellness, and language education, with smaller deployments in marketing, healthcare, banking, and lighting & electrical equipment), GSC-QA achieves a Task Success Rate (TSR) of 87.1% and a Goal Consistency Score (GCS) of 0.78 on the combined 1,516-record evaluation set, and an Error Recovery Rate (ERR) of 79.5% on 205 organic pivot transitions, substantially outperforming standard RAG (58.7% TSR, GCS 0.62). All baselines including Instruct-Only are evaluated on the same dataset for fair comparison. Cross-domain evaluation across 980 records from 14 enterprise deployments shows the mechanism transfers with little loss: on a curated 299-record subset scored under the same judge and rubric as the primary set, task success reaches 62.2% against 63.2% in-domain. Against four external baselines, including an agentic ReAct system, a memory-augmented long-context model, a SimpleTOD-style tracker and a graph-structured stateful agent, GSC-QA leads on task success, faithfulness and answer relevancy alike, and its lead in task success holds under four independent judge families. An LLM-as-judge metric (gpt-5.4) achieves 94% agreement with human annotations. Ablation studies confirm that goal persistence and expert instructions are complementary; removing either component causes significant performance degradation.

titulo: Aligning LLMs for the Classroom with Knowledge-Based Retrieval: A Comparative RAG Study
autores: A. Jain; L. Cui; S. Chen
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Teaching, Assessment, and Learning for Engineering (TALE)
abstract: Large language models like ChatGPT are increasingly used in classrooms, but they often provide outdated or fabricated information that can mislead students. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) improves reliability of LLMs by grounding responses in external resources. We investigate two accessible RAG paradigms, vector-based retrieval and graph-based retrieval to identify best practices for classroom question answering (QA). Existing comparative studies fail to account for pedagogical factors such as educational disciplines, question types, and practical deployment costs. Using a novel dataset, EduScopeQA, of 3,176 questions across academic subjects, we measure performance on various educational query types, from specific facts to broad thematic discussions. We also evaluate system alignment with a dataset of systematically altered textbooks that contradict the LLM’s latent knowledge. We find that OpenAI Vector Search RAG (representing vector-based RAG) performs well as a low-cost generalist, especially for quick fact retrieval. On the other hand, GraphRAG Global excels at providing pedagogically rich answers to thematic queries, and GraphRAG Local achieves the highest accuracy with the dense, altered textbooks when corpus integrity is critical. Accounting for the 10-20x higher resource usage of GraphRAG (representing graph-based RAG), we show that a dynamic branching framework that routes queries to the optimal retrieval method boosts fidelity and efficiency. These insights provide actionable guidelines for educators and system designers to integrate RAG-augmented LLMs into learning environments effectively.

titulo: CRITIC-RAG: Knowledge-Augmented Large Language Models With Verified Retrieval for Improved Medical Reasoning
autores: J. Li; L. Lu; Y. Miao; Y. Tian; J. Li
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: While retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) presents a promising solution for enhancing large language models (LLMs) in question answering (QA), particularly in knowledge-intensive domains like medicine, it continues to face challenges related to factual consistency and reasoning reliability. To address this challenge, we propose CRITIC-RAG, a verification-enhanced framework that integrates a small-size, instruction-tuned verifier throughout the RAG pipeline. Our method incorporates selective retrieval, evidence filtering, structured reasoning through self-consistency, and groundedness verification. This approach enhances the accurate utilization of external knowledge while reducing spurious generations. Comprehensive experiments across five medical QA benchmarks and multiple LLM backbones confirm the framework's broad applicability and plug-and-play adaptability. For instance, CRITIC-RAG improves accuracy from 41.3% to 48.8% on MedQA and boosts BERTScore from 68.1% to 74.4% on MedicationQA using LLaMA-3. Ablation studies further reveal that evidence filtering and structured reasoning are especially critical to robust performance. Case studies and retrieval analyses, including improvements in entailment-based similarity scores and factual accuracy, demonstrate how each stage of verification jointly contributes to generating more accurate, evidence-grounded responses. Overall, our work highlights verification as a key mechanism for enhancing trustworthiness in knowledge-intensive medical QA, a capability that is increasingly important for clinical decision support and other real-world healthcare applications.

titulo: Sustainable Energy Decision-Making with an RAG-LLM System

titulo: Quantifying Informativeness in Knowledge Graph-Augmented In-Context Learning for Multiple Choice Query Answering
autores: M. Ghanbari; R. Dividino
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Knowledge Graph (ICKG)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant challenges when attempting to utilize knowledge not encoded during pre-training. In-context learning (ICL) addresses this limitation by embedding relevant information directly into prompts, enabling LLMs to leverage external knowledge without updating their parameters. Recent advances have explored integrating knowledge graph (KG) information into prompts, taking advantage of the structured and factual representations of entities and relationships that KGs provide. A common approach involves identifying key concepts in a task, grounding them to KG nodes, extracting ego-subgraphs centered on these concepts, and incorporating them into prompts. However, not all subgraphs are equally relevant to the task, and selecting appropriate knowledge remains a critical challenge, as irrelevant or noisy subgraphs can reduce model accuracy. This study investigates how KG-based information related to task-specific concepts influences LLM performance on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) tasks. We implement a four-stage pipeline that (1) identifies key concepts from questions and grounds them in the KG, (2) extracts individual ego-subgraphs for each concept, (3) integrates these subgraphs into prompts, and (4) evaluates their impact on LLM reasoning via probability scoring. Our analysis highlights which concept-specific subgraphs enhance performance, which introduce misleading information, and which have neutral effects. We show that carefully selected KG subgraphs can substantially outperform others in semantic relevance. Furthermore, we examine how the size and connectivity of selected KG subgraphs influence model performance. Overall, this work deepens understanding of KG-based knowledge selection in ICL and informs the design of more effective, targeted prompting strategies. This project's source code is publicly available at https://github.com/maryam-ghanbari/InformativenessOfKGs.

titulo: V2V-LLM: Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Autonomous Driving with Multimodal Large Language Models
autores: H. -k. Chiu; R. Hachiuma; C. -Y. Wang; S. F. Smith; Y. -C. Frank Wang; M. -H. Chen
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Current autonomous driving vehicles rely mainly on their individual sensors to understand surrounding scenes and plan for future trajectories, which can be unreliable when the sensors are malfunctioning or occluded. To address this problem, cooperative perception methods via vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication have been proposed, but they have tended to focus on perception tasks like detection or tracking. How those approaches contribute to overall cooperative planning performance is still under-explored. Inspired by recent progress using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build autonomous driving systems, we propose a novel problem setting that integrates a Multimodal LLM into cooperative autonomous driving, with the proposed Vehicle-to-Vehicle Question-Answering (V2V-QA) dataset and benchmark. We also propose our baseline method Vehicle-to-Vehicle Multimodal Large Language Model (V2V-LLM), which uses an LLM to fuse perception information from multiple connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and answer various types of driving-related questions: grounding, notable object identification, and planning. Our work also creates a new research direction that can improve the safety of future autonomous driving systems. titulo: OPeMer: One-Shot LLM Prompting and Execution-Driven Multimodal Explainable Reasoning
autores: Z. Zhou; D. Xue; S. Qian
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Knowledge Graph (ICKG)
abstract: The Visual Question Answering (VQA) task requires not only accurate answers but also interpretable reasoning processes, particularly in real-world applications where transparency is critical. To reduce annotation and computational costs while maintaining interpretability, the Few-shot Multimodal Explainable VQA (FS-MEVQA) task has been introduced, which aims to generate explanations with limited supervision. In this work, we propose OPeMer (One-shot Prompting and Execution-driven Multimodal Explainable Reasoning), a code-based framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate executable Python programs for multimodal reasoning in a oneshot setting. These programs interact with a lightweight Python API to process visual inputs, capture intermediate reasoning artifacts—such as object crops and spatial relations—and optionally call external tools for open-world visual understanding. The resulting execution traces are serialized and provided to the LLM via a secondary prompt, enabling the generation of coherent multimodal explanations grounded in both visual and textual evidence. Designed without reliance on handcrafted rules or large-scale supervision, OPeMer offers an efficient and extensible approach to explainable multimodal reasoning. Experimental results on the SME dataset demonstrate that OPeMer achieves strong answer accuracy and explanation quality, even when using cost-effective LLMs under limited supervision, suggesting its potential for scalable and interpretable VQA.

titulo: Balancing Object Recognition and Spatial Reasoning in 3D Vision Via Intent-Aware Vision-Guided Language Refinement
autores: L. Shi; G. Zhang; S. Kan; L. Zhang; Z. Lin; Y. Cen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
abstract: 3D scene understanding is fundamental to embodied AI, and recent 3D Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have improved visual comprehension in complex environments. However, their appearance-centric visual encoders and weakly coupled vision-instruction architecture jointly lead to predictions that are accurate in appearance yet unreliable in spatial reasoning. In this paper, we propose $V^{3}$-LLM, a generalist 3D MLLM that integrates an appearance-spatial dual-perspective vision perception system with an intent-aware vision-guided language refinement mechanism, enabling the model to adaptively reconcile appearance information and spatial visual cues according to task requirements. Specifically, the dual vision memory system encodes instance-level appearance attributes while simultaneously capturing spatially enhanced visual features, producing a comprehensive 3D scene representation. Building upon these representations, the intent-aware vision refinement LLM (IVR-LLM) employs a staged information injection schedule that first processes appearance and instruction tokens through standard decoder layers to form preliminary hidden representations, then iteratively injects intent-aware spatial preferences at later decoding stages, enabling the model to dynamically integrate appearance and spatial cues for scene reasoning. Considering the multi-granular alignment required in 3D scene descriptions, we introduce a hierarchical alignment loss that enforces consistency from token-level attributes to sentence-level spatial relations, leading to more coherent and semantically reliable scene descriptions. Extensive experiments on 3D dense captioning, visual question answering, and visual grounding benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of $V^{3}$-LLM.

titulo: SRSA: A Cost-Efficient Strategy-Router Search Agent for Real-world Human-Machine Interactions
autores: Y. Wang; H. Xu
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW)
abstract: Recently, as Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive emerging capabilities and gained widespread popularity, research on LLM-based search agents has proliferated. In real-world situations, users often input contextual and highly personalized queries to chatbots, challenging LLMs to capture context and generate appropriate answers. However, much of the prior research has not focused specifically on authentic human-machine dialogue scenarios. It also ignores the important balance between response quality and computational cost by forcing all queries to follow the same agent process. To address these gaps, we propose a Strategy-Router Search Agent (SRSA), routing different queries to appropriate search strategies and enabling fine-grained serial searches to obtain high-quality results at a relatively low cost. To evaluate our work, we introduce a new dataset, Contextual Query Enhancement Dataset (CQED), comprising contextual queries to simulate authentic and daily interactions between humans and chatbots. Using LLM-based automatic evaluation metrics, we assessed SRSA’s performance in terms of informativeness, completeness, novelty, and actionability. To conclude, SRSA provides an approach that resolves the issue of simple serial searches leading to degenerate answers for lengthy and contextual queries, effectively and efficiently parses complex user queries, and generates more comprehensive and informative responses without fine-tuning an LLM. titulo: SiQA: A Large Multi-Modal Question Answering Model for Structured Images Based on RAG
autores: J. Liu; Y. Tao; F. Wang; H. Li; X. Qin
venue: ICASSP 2025 - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Existing Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) demonstrate excellent performance in handling visual tasks in everyday scenarios. However, they still face challenges in understanding structured images, such as flowcharts and organizational charts, which are characterized by text-rich and complex hierarchical components. In this paper, we propose SiQA, a knowledge construction and Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG)-based multimodal Question-Answering model designed for Structured Images. SiQA operates in three stages: Knowledge Graph (KG) generation, retrieval-augmented, and answer generation. First, a KG representing the semantics of the structured images is generated through component analysis. We then performed similarity retrieval between the KG and queries, using a node-first algorithm to construct the most relevant subgraph. Finally, after performing an encoding alignment on the multimodal information, it is fed into the LLM to generate the answer. Additionally, we introduce a new dataset, OCQA1, which includes 5,112 questions derived from 1,000 Organizational Charts. We evaluated SiQA’s structured image detection and question-answering capabilities on the FD-DETR (a flowchart dataset) and SCQA, and verified its effectiveness and strong generalization ability through comparisons with existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

titulo: Performance Optimization of Mllm-Based 3D Spatial Perception Tasks Via Sam
autores: Z. Jia; Y. Zhao; T. Li; H. Li; M. Zhou; J. Su; C. Li
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning (PRML)
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong performance in general visual understanding, yet they remain limited in complex 3D visual question answering tasks that require explicit object grounding, spatial relation modeling, and occlusion-aware reasoning. To address this challenge, we propose a modular segmentation-enhanced reasoning framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM), Grounded-Segment Anything Model(SAM), and an MLLM for Open3DVQA. The framework consists of three stages: (1) structured semantic parsing, in which an LLM converts naturallanguage questions into compact object-centric prompts to improve grounding reliability; (2) explicit visual grounding and segmentation, where Grounding DIstillation with NO labels(DINO) and SAM generate object labels, bounding boxes, confidence scores, and pixel-level masks; and (3) segmentation-guided multimodal reasoning, in which these structured visual cues are injected into the MLLM together with the original image and question. Experiments on Open3DVQA show that the proposed prompting strategy improves segmentation success from below 90% with raw questions to 97.35%, while segmentation-enhanced inference increases overall answer accuracy from 47.1% to 48.9%, improves qualitative reasoning from 59.3% to 61.6%, and reduces the refusal rate from 4.48% to 0.28%. The results indicate that explicit segmentation provides a practical and interpretable scaffold for multi-modal reasoning, offering a fluently low-training-cost pathway for improving MLLM performance in spatial perception tasks. At the same time, limited gains on quantitative questions suggest that segmentation alone is insufficient for full 3D reasoning, highlighting the need for future integration of geometric and depth-aware representations.

titulo: N-CATS: A Neural Network Classification Automatic Taxonomy System
autores: C. Carthen; L. Lac; R. White; T. Braun; J. Ochoa; A. Tavakkoli; F. C. Harris
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACIS 29th International Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD)
abstract: The rapid evolution of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) has made it difficult to organize and compare model architectures under a unified framework. Automatic taxonomy construction (ATC) is a promising approach for algorithmically organizing knowledge domains, but existing frameworks struggle with the structural complexities of ANNs. To address this, we introduce Neural Network Classification Automatic Taxonomy System (N-CATS), a structured, ontology-driven framework for ATC that enables comparison across diverse ANN topologies. N-CATS extracts contextual information from semi-structured sources, including academic publications, source code, and serialized formats such as ONNX to populate an ontology schema-based on ANNETT-O. The system leverages Large Language Models (LLM) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to support the ontology population and organize extracted information in a graph database, enabling on-demand categorization and comparison of ANNs. To demonstrate feasibility, we developed a web application that provides ontology visualization, proof-of-concept taxonomy generation, and a chatbot using GraphRAG and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for intelligent querying. We compare N-CATS with existing neural network ontologies such as FAIRnets, Artificial Intelligence Ontology (AIO), and ANNETT-O. Finally, we outline advantages and limitations, demonstrating a proof-of-concept knowledge system that facilitates more efficient discovery and comparison of deep learning models as a tool for researchers.

titulo: RFSensingGPT: A Multi-Modal RAG-Enhanced Framework for Integrated Sensing and Communications Intelligence in 6G Networks
autores: M. Zakir Khan; Y. Ge; M. Mollel; J. Mccann; Q. H. Abbasi; M. Imran
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
abstract: We present RFSensingGPT, an integrated framework for radio frequency (RF) sensing that combines technical question-answering, code retrieval, and spectrogram analysis through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Our framework addresses the fundamental challenge of applying large language models to RF sensing applications, where specialized domain knowledge is underrepresented in general training corpora. The system leverages a filtered RedPajama dataset containing RF-relevant technical documents, processed through a hybrid retrieval mechanism that combines vector-based similarity search with best match (BM25)-based query fusion. Performance evaluation using document collections ranging from 5K to 80K demonstrates that RAG consistently maintains superior faithfulness across all dataset sizes (0.9033-0.9779 vs 0.8162-0.8506, average improvement of 13.0%) compared to baseline LLM implementations. Our hierarchical chunking approach using MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter achieves optimal precision (0.31-0.32) at lower k-values while maintaining correctness scores of 4.0-5.0. The framework integrates CLIP-based vision models for RF pattern recognition, achieving 93.23% accuracy in radar data analysis tasks. Implementation benchmarks show efficient processing with minimal GPU memory requirements (0.66GB) even at scale. Through a comprehensive evaluation of the embedding models, RFSensingGPT establishes a new benchmark for technical query understanding and RF spectrogram analysis in the emerging field of integrated sensing and communications systems for 6G networks.

titulo: RIPE-II: Retrieval In-Place Poisoning Evaluation with Indirect Injections
autores: G. Malladi; G. Thamilarasu
venue: 2026 56th Annual IEEE International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks (DSN)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have enhanced the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) by effectively addressing challenges such as hallucinations and generating irrelevant responses. However, integrating the RAG technique into LLMs introduces privacy risks and potential data leakage issues from the retrieval pipeline. Indirect Prompt Injections (IPIs) occur when hidden instructions inside retrieved documents slip into a model’s context as trusted evidence, exploiting weak guardrails in RAG systems and leading to unauthorized data leaks, ambiguous outcomes, and policy overrides. Existing defenses rely on brittle delimiter heuristics or limited retriever adjustments, leaving RAG systems vulnerable to adversarial directives blended seamlessly into retrieved content.In this paper, we present RIPE-II, a corpus-level benchmark that evaluates IPIs under a realistic content-poisoning threat model. RIPE-II constructs delimiter-free, position-aware poisoned corpora across multiple domains and includes both textual and visual injections. Our design explicitly models mid-document placement, chunking, truncation, and cross-component propagation, reflecting how enterprise RAG systems ingest and process content. We introduce a two-stage evaluation framework that separates retrieval exposure from generation-time compliance and distinguishes embedding-based similarity from semantic override using a calibrated LLM-based judge. Across biomedical, financial, scientific, open-domain question answering, including multi-hop reasoning and web passage retrieval settings, we find that poisoned documents can reach the final model context in up to 97% of queries and rank first in up to 94% of cases, showing that retriever and reranker choices substantially shape RAG security exposure. We further show that cosine-based attack scoring can underreport semantic compromise by more than 5×, demonstrating that lexical or embedding similarity alone is insufficient for evaluating indirect prompt injection risk.

titulo: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
autores: C. Xiang; T. Wu; Z. Zhong; D. Wagner; D. Chen; P. Mittal
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is susceptible to retrieval corruption attacks, where malicious passages injected into retrieval results can lead to inaccurate model responses. We propose RobustRAG, the first defense framework with certifiable robustness against retrieval corruption attacks. The key insight of RobustRAG is an isolate-then-aggregate strategy: we isolate passages into disjoint groups, generate LLM responses based on the concatenated passages from each isolated group, and then securely aggregate these responses for a robust output. To instantiate RobustRAG, we design keyword-based and decoding-based algorithms for securely aggregating unstructured text responses. Notably, RobustRAG achieves certifiable robustness: for certain queries in our evaluation datasets, we can formally certify non-trivial lower bounds on response quality—even against an adaptive attacker with full knowledge of the defense and the ability to arbitrarily inject a bounded number of malicious passages. We evaluate RobustRAG on the tasks of open-domain question-answering and free-form long text generation and demonstrate its effectiveness across three datasets and three LLMs.

autores: M. Dhifallah; Y. Liu
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
abstract: Biomedical question answering remains a challenging task due to the complexity of clinical knowledge and the limitations of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) in providing accurate, domain-specific responses. We introduce Chimera-3X, a hybrid cognitive engine that orchestrates multiple specialized LLMs (DeepSeek, BioGPT from Microsoft, and Exone 3.0 from LG), each fine-tuned and adapted as an independent medical sub-toolkit. Chimera-3X integrates external biomedical knowledge graphs such as UMLS, SNOMED CT, and Wikidata via retrieval-augmented generation techniques, enhancing the system's factual accuracy and reasoning capabilities. Each engine processes clinical queries independently while the orchestrator coordinates their outputs, leveraging SPARQLbased queries to ensure precise knowledge retrieval. Preliminary evaluations demonstrate significant improvements in clinical answer accuracy, coherence, and interpretability compared to standalone LLM approaches. We propose an architecture that provides a scalable, transparent and effective framework for biomedical consulting, advancing the integration of knowledgedriven AI in healthcare applications. titulo: Knowledge-Augmented Language Models for Intelligent Information Retrieval
autores: H. Kohli; R. Challa; M. R. Muthirevula; S. R. BasiReddy; S. R. Sagili; J. N. Kola
venue: 2026 International Conference on Data Science for Cyber-Physical Systems Resilience using Advanced Applications (ICDCA)
abstract: As unstructured and semi-structured data proliferate in digital platforms, the need for intelligent information retrieval systems that can provide accurate, context-aware, and explainable results is growing. Conventional information retrieval methods have limited success in handling semantic relationships and domain knowledge, and do not perform well in complex queries. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper presents a Knowledge-Augmented Language Model (KALM) framework which combines LLM and structured knowledge resources like knowledge graphs, ontologies, and external databases. The proposed approach integrates the three techniques of processing queries and ranking documents: contextual reasoning, entity linking and semantic enrichment, to increase the effectiveness of the retrieval. The architecture is designed as a multi-layered pipeline that comprises of query understanding, knowledge augmentation, hybrid retrieval, and response generation modules. It uses transformer-based language models along with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods to dynamically integrate relevant external knowledge. Moreover, attention mechanisms and graph-based embeddings are used to enhance the semantic matching of queries to documents. The evaluation is done experimentally on some benchmark datasets and reported by precision, recall, F1-score and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). Results show that the proposed KALM framework can significantly outperform the retrieval baselines on the accuracy, contextual relevance, and robustness on various domains. The study emphasizes the need to combine symbolic knowledge with neural language models to address the shortcomings of data-driven models. The proposed framework provides scalable and flexible solutions in the applications such as search engine, question answering system, digital assistant, enterprise knowledge management, etc. Future research involves further optimizing real-time knowledge integration, optimizing computational costs, and increasing explainability in knowledge-driven retrieval systems.

titulo: SpatialGeo: Boosting Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Geometry-Semantics Fusion
autores: J. Guo; Q. Zhu; J. Zeng; X. Wu; C. He; W. Wang
venue: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Multimedia Signal Processing (MMSP)
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in image and language tasks due to the strong reasoning capability of large language models (LLMs). Nevertheless, most MLLMs suffer from limited spatial reasoning ability to interpret and infer spatial arrangements in three-dimensional space. In this work, we propose a novel vision encoder based on hierarchical fusion of geometry and semantics features, generating spatial-aware visual embedding and boosting the spatial grounding capability of MLLMs. Specifically, we first unveil that the spatial ambiguity shortcoming stems from the lossy embedding of the vision encoder utilized in most existing MLLMs (e.g., CLIP), restricted to instance-level semantic features. This motivates us to complement CLIP with the geometry features from vision-only self-supervised learning via a hierarchical adapter, enhancing the spatial awareness in the proposed SpatialGeo. The network is efficiently trained using pretrained LLaVA model and optimized with random feature dropping to avoid trivial solutions relying solely on the CLIP encoder. Experimental results show that SpatialGeo improves the accuracy in spatial reasoning tasks, enhancing state-of-the-art models by at least 8.0% in SpatialRGPT-Bench with ∼50% less memory cost during inference. The source code is available via https://ricky-plus.github.io/SpatialGeoPages/.

titulo: A Review of Faithfulness Metrics for Hallucination Assessment in Large Language Models
autores: B. Malin; T. Kalganova; N. Boulgouris
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing
abstract: This review examines the means with which faithfulness has been evaluated across open-ended summarization, question answering and machine translation tasks. We find that the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) as a faithfulness evaluator is commonly the metric that is most highly correlated with human judgement. The means with which other studies have mitigated hallucinations is discussed, with both retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and prompting framework approaches having been linked with superior faithfulness, whilst other recommendations for mitigation are provided. Research into faithfulness is integral to the continued widespread use of LLMs, as unfaithful responses can pose major risks to many areas whereby LLMs would otherwise be suitable. Furthermore, evaluating open-ended generation provides a more comprehensive measure of LLM performance than commonly used multiple-choice benchmarking, which can help in advancing the trust that can be placed within LLMs.

titulo: RTLExplain: A Structured Approach to RTL Code Summarization and Question Answering for Medium-to-Large Designs Using LLMs
autores: T. -H. Chi; C. Mackin; L. Shi; P. Vijayaraghavan; H. Tsai; E. Degan
venue: 2025 ACM/IEEE 7th Symposium on Machine Learning for CAD (MLCAD)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in assisting with Register Transfer Level (RTL) design tasks, including code summarization, documentation, and question answering. However, directly applying LLMs to entire RTL codebases often leads to low accuracy in these tasks. This is primarily because LLMs are less exposed to RTL code during pretraining, limiting their ability to understand RTL-specific semantics and structural dependencies. To overcome this challenge, we propose RTLExplain, which builds project-specific knowledge bases to enhance LLM performance on RTL design tasks. Our method is entirely offline and requires no additional training or fine-tuning. Experiments on code summarization using the generated knowledge bases demonstrate consistent improvements across various medium-to-large RTL projects, even when variable names are obfuscated. Furthermore, we use these knowledge bases to support Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for question answering tasks. Results show that our enhanced knowledge bases, when combined with RAG, improve question-answering accuracy by 37% compared to naïve prompting and 27% compared to conventional RAG.

titulo: Learnable Contrastive Decoding for Dehallucination in LLMs
autores: J. -T. Chien; C. -C. Li
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel in the tasks such as text generation for question answering and reasoning, but still remain prone to hallucination due to semantic drift, factual errors, and verbalized repetition, which restrict the reliability when building the knowledge-grounded applications. Existing remedies such as fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and retrieval-augmented generation improve the performance but suffer from high computational cost, architectural complexity, and limited transferability. This paper presents the learnable contrastive decoding (LCD), a decoding-time editing that enhances the semantic fidelity without altering parameters. Inspired by the locate–edit paradigm in model editing, LCD identifies the semantically critical intermediate layers via a trained selector and edits the outputs through an attention-based fusion module that contrasts these layers with the final-layer distribution. This dynamic and learnable reasoning corrects the biases and improves the alignment. Experiments on WritingPrompts, TruthfulQA, and GSM8K show LCD outperforms the other methods in factuality, consistency and diversity, while the ablations confirm the necessity of both layer selection and fusion. Overall, LCD provides a lightweight, semantically aware intervention that mitigates hallucination without fine-tuning, advancing the controllability and reliability of LLM based on state-space model using RWKV.

titulo: LLM-Assisted Task-Adaptive Semantic Communication over Non-Ideal Channels for Vision–Language Systems
autores: O. Orimoogunje; S. Sarker; X. Li; L. Qian
venue: 2026 35th International Conference on Computer Communications and Networks (ICCCN)
abstract: Semantic communications aim to transmit task-relevant meaning instead of raw data, enabling bandwidth reduction under non-ideal channel conditions, which is a critical requirement across bandwidth-constrained and noise-impaired systems, such as satellite links and resource-limited wireless networks. This paper proposes a task-adaptive semantic communication framework for visual question answering (VQA) over bandwidth-constrained additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels. The proposed system achieves 9× compression by transmitting a compact 16k-dimensional semantic map instead of 150k-dimensional raw image data, while maintaining task performance under severe channel noise. The proposed method contains two key contributions: (i) a multi-SNR encoder training strategy that improves low-SNR VQA accuracy by 6.3% at −20 dB compared to training under ideal channel conditions, and (ii) a semantic judge feedback mechanism using REINFORCE policy gradients, where embedding-based judges (GTE-Qwen2-7B, SBERT, BERT, and GPT-2) yield 1.9–2.1% accuracy gains over a supervised cross-entropy baseline. Experiments on the VQAv2 dataset with a ResNet-50 semantic encoder demonstrate that text-based semantic-similarity judges outperform both heuristic exact-match feedback and vision-based judges, confirming that text-grounded reward signals are better suited for bandwidth-constrained semantic VQA under realistic noisy-channel conditions.

titulo: Mitigating Understanding Bias: Explicit Meta Enhancement in LLM-based Table Reasoning
autores: J. Lin; Q. Mao; M. Cheng; Q. Liu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data and Smart Computing (BigComp)
abstract: In recent years, table reasoning has attracted significant attention, with extensive studies that leverage the advantages of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their multi-step prompting paradigm. Existing approaches manage to produce high-quality reasoning procedures through the inspirations of operation decomposition and tool utilization. However, they place less emphasis on explicit understanding of the tabular data and pose potential risks of chaotic logical lines. We hold that robust table reasoning fundamentally depends upon a thorough comprehension of table metadata. To this end, we adopt the perspective of Explicit Meta Enhancement (EME) by building a structured semantic scaffold with explicit, well-formatted contextual knowledge for LLM-based table reasoning. This augmentation provides more comprehensible textual grounding, improving its understanding of the table schema and reducing the uncertainty in downstream reasoning. Finally, we conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations over a public table reasoning benchmark. The results fully demonstrate the effectiveness of EME in table understanding, especially in reasoning tasks with higher difficulty.

autores: D. Pedro José González; A. Orjuela Duarte; W. M. Rojas; J. Luz Marina Santos
venue: 2024 IEEE Colombian Conference on Applications of Computational Intelligence (ColCACI)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are a type of artificial intelligence capable of processing and generating natural language. These models are trained on vast amounts of data, such as text and code, which enables them to perform various tasks like text generation, language translation, question answering, text summarization, etc. The purpose of this research was to find an LLM that meets the following requirements: 1)easy to implement with an understanding of the Spanish language, and 2)accurately answers diagnostic questions and action plans related to Industry 4.0 (I4.0). titulo: Towards Automated 5G Configuration: Design and Evaluation of a RAG-Enhanced AI Pipeline
autores: S. Fricke; J. Wang; J. Jasperneite
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: The growing complexity of modern wireless networks motivates the need for intelligent and automated approaches for network configuration and management. This paper proposes a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) pipeline for translating high-level user intents into low-level 5G network configurations. Existing RAG and fine-tuning approaches for AI-assisted telecommunication systems are surveyed, revealing a critical gap: most prior work focuses on question answering rather than actionable configuration generation. To address this gap, a conceptual architecture and a proof-of-concept implementation are presented, comprising a web-based frontend, a Flask Application Programming Interface (API), the Qdrant vector database for a RAG-system, lightweight Large Language Models (LLMs) such as Phi-2 and Qwen-3-8B-Instruct, a verification component, and a time-series database. Finally, the system evaluates 50 prompts, assessing the syntactic correctness and semantic accuracy of generated configurations against a ground truth, thereby demonstrating the fundamental feasibility of LLM-driven intent-to-configuration translation in 5G networks.

titulo: Decoupled Seg Tokens Make Stronger Reasoning Video Segmenter and Grounder
autores: J. Dang; X. Wu; H. Yan; H. Zheng; W. -S. Zheng; J. Lai; B. Hu; T. -S. Chua
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Existing video segmenter and grounder approaches, exemplified by Sa2VA, directly fuse features within segmentation models. This often results in an undesirable entanglement of dynamic visual information and static semantics, thereby degrading segmentation accuracy. To systematically mitigate these issues, we propose DeSa2VA, a decoupling-enhanced prompting scheme integrating text pre-training and a linear decoupling module to address the information processing limitations inherent in SAM-2. Specifically, first, we devise a pre-training paradigm that converts textual ground-truth labels into point-level prompts while generating corresponding text masks. These masks are refined through a hybrid loss function to strengthen the model’s semantic grounding capabilities. Next, we employ linear projection to disentangle hidden states generated by a large language model into distinct textual and visual feature subspaces. Finally, a dynamic mask fusion strategy synergistically combines these decoupled features through triple supervision from predicted text/visual masks and ground-truth annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks, including image segmentation, image question answering, video segmentation, and video question answering.

titulo: An Interpretable Therapy-Informed Dialogue Chatbot for Older Adults Guided by Hierarchical Linguistic Feature Inference and Social Buffering
autores: H. -C. Chen; Y. -C. Chang; Y. -X. Chen
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: Population aging increases the need for scalable mental-health support tailored to older adults, yet LLM-based chatbots may provide non-specialized or unsafe guidance in sensitive situations such as aggressive venting or nostalgia-driven distress. We present an interpretable therapy-informed dialogue chatbot for older adults, guided by Hierarchical Linguistic Feature Inference and Social Buffering. The system combines retrieval-augmented generation with an inference-based planner that maps six clinically motivated linguistic dimensions (Time Focus, Cognitive Complexity, Emotional Tone, Social Orientation, Repetitive Patterns, and Absolutist Language) to a quantified therapy ratio vector across four therapeutic schools: CBT, PCT, SFBT, and RT. A Hierarchical Decision Algorithm (HDA) first performs cognitive screening to avoid high-load interventions, then activates a Social Buffer mechanism when rigidity markers (e.g., absolutist expressions) are detected, prioritizing emotional validation before further guidance. Persona-based simulation results show appropriate buffering behavior (higher PCT/RT for aggression) and reminiscence-oriented support for loneliness, offering a transparent alternative to end-to-end black-box dialogue systems.

titulo: RAG for Question-Answering for Vocal Training Based on Domain Knowledge Base
autores: C. -h. J. Leung; Y. Yi; L. Kuai; Z. Li; S. -k. A. Yeung; K. -w. J. Lee; K. -h. K. Ho; K. Hung
venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Behavioural and Social Computing (BESC)
abstract: Although Large language models (LLMs) are well-known due to their superior capacity for text generation and logical inference, they are found to be inaccurate in domain-specific question-answering tasks. The powerful generator still tends to generate content even when the LLM does not have sufficient knowledge at all, which is known as the hallucination problem. We find there is a research void in applying LLMs in the vocal training industry, which requires intensive expert knowledge in any chatbot or intelligent tutor services. This paper details employing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology to develop a domain-specific language model, addressing inherent challenges such as hallucination, where large models generate plausible but inaccurate content, and lack of domain specificity. By segmenting the knowledge base and establishing semantic similarities between user queries and knowledge data, the project lays a solid foundation for integrating RAG, significantly improving response accuracy and contextual relevance. The report highlights the successful implementation of RAG, enhancing system intelligence and personalization for user-specific needs, discusses challenges and solutions during the implementation process, and outlines future directions to expand RAG capabilities and improve user experiences.
