venue: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Cryptography, Informatics, and Cybersecurity (ICoCICs)
abstract: Equitable access to emergency services is a core requirement for urban resilience, yet population-aware spatial audits typically demand expert GIS workflows. We present SiagaJakarta, a reproducible and automated end-to-end spatial analysis system for Jakarta through a Telegram chatbot. The system follows a multi-agent design-LLM Orchestrator, OSM Facility Retrieval, Boundary Retrieval, Population Retrieval, and Analysis & Reporting–that translates natural-language prompts into population-normalized adequacy maps and narratives per sub-district (kecamatan). We evaluate the system on $N=180$ prompts (44 sub-districts $\times 4$ services plus synonym variants). Our contributions are: (i) a practical multi-agent architecture that unifies LLM, and geospatial analysis; (ii) a Jakarta case study producing static maps and narratives per sub-district; (iii) a multi-metric evaluation suited to governance; and (iv) a reproducible blueprint that cities can adapt with minimal coding. In our experiment, SiagaJakarta processed 100% of the 180 queries (pipeline success 100%), found facilities in 96.1% of cases, and exported static basemap figures for 100% of runs. Facility retrieval results were deterministic and consistent across repeated queries. Responses were fast (median latency $=9.17 ~\mathrm{s}$; mean $=16.12 ~\mathrm{s}; \mathbf{p 9 0}=20.42 ~\mathrm{s}; \mathbf{p 9 5}=79.39 ~\mathrm{s}$). The pipeline surfaced actionable gaps (e.g., low fire-station adequacy in industrial districts) and generated consistent cartography with embedded textual insights. These results indicate that agentic GeoAI can make population-aware spatial intelligence usable by non-experts and provide a scalable foundation for policy-oriented deployment.

autores: S. Razak; S. Adikesavulu; V. Reddy; K. Sudeep; A. Khan
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a conversational chatbot that closes this divide by coupling YOLOv8-based object detection, Tesseract driven optical character recognition, and Google Gemini dialogue generation inside one unified framework. titulo: Multi-Agent Medical Debate System for Clinical Reasoning
autores: S. Bhoyar; A. Ansari; N. Saxena
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence, and Communications Technology (IAICT)
abstract: Clinical deployment of large language models (LLMs) for medical question answering faces three primary challenges: (1) models frequently produce unsupported or hallucinated claims because their parametric knowledge is not verified against biomedical evidence; (2) single-pass inference prevents iterative self-correction, leading to incomplete differential diagnoses; and (3) poorly calibrated confidence scores undermine clinician trust. To address these challenges, we introduce a retrieval augmented multi-agent model whose components are specifically designed to generate medical answers through three stages: hypothesis generation, adversarial debate, and independent judgment, wherein evidence conditioned hypotheses are generated, contested by an adversarial process, and finally evaluated by an independent model. Each of these models utilizes a semantic retrieval system to access medical literature from PubMed, explanations of answer benchmarks from MedQA, and medical records from MIMIC III. The model is evaluated using the MedQA USMLE benchmark and a collection of prompts created from MIMIC III data, as well as by comparing the performance of the system against a general purpose LLM and a fine tuned medical LLM. Results indicate that the approach described improves the supported sentences rate, the precision and recall of the attributed sentences, and the groundedness of the answers provided while also reducing the number of unsupported claims, hallucinations, Brier score, and expected calibration error, while maintaining the same accuracy in medical diagnosis. Thus, these findings indicate that the incorporation of adversarial and verification models during inference can improve the model’s ability to align with the evidence and to calibrate uncertainty in its predictions without requiring any adaptation to the models with supervised training data.

titulo: SmartEduNotes: A Retrieval-Augmented Platform for Personalized Note-Taking, Revision, and Career Guidance
autores: V. Singh; T. K. Pradhan; S. SS; K. Upadhayay; S. S. Kumar
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
abstract: Effective learning in modern education requires tools that not only store information but actively help learners retain knowledge and plan future careers. We present SmartEduNotes, a web-based, retrieval-augmented platform that enhances personal note-taking through dense semantic search, provenance-aware question answering, automated flashcard generation, and concept-graph-driven career guidance. The system integrates Sentence-BERT embeddings, FAISS vector search, and LLM-based generation to provide accurate, context-grounded answers from personal notes, while automatically converting content into cloze-style flashcards scheduled with our novel Adaptive SM-2 algorithm for optimized spaced repetition. Central concepts extracted via a concept graph inform personalized skill recommendations based on real-world job postings. Pilot evaluation on 150 lecture note documents demonstrates up to 87 % QA accuracy, 85% 7-day flashcard recall (compared to 62 % manually), and effective identification of career-relevant skills. The architecture supports modular expansion, multi-modal input (audio, text), on-device privacy, and adaptive learning strategies. This work contributes a reproducible framework for personalized learning, knowledge retention, and career-aligned skill development.

autores: A. M. Cavasin; A. R. T. Benedetti; E. A. Bellei; A. C. B. De Marchi
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Artificial intelligence in healthcare has concentrated on clinical applications, while support for the managerial work that sustains health services is yet underexplored. Health system managers decide against large, dispersed, and frequently revised bodies of official guidance, a task that differs from clinical question answering in the nature of its corpus. In this context, we developed and evaluated a policy-informed AI assistant for management decision support, using Brazil’s Unified Health System as a demanding instance of a decentralized system with a large policy corpus. Following a mixed-methods design, we (i) mapped and indexed 106 official Ministry of Health documents into a curated knowledge base, spanning primary care operational documentation, management portals, and national health planning instruments; (ii) developed a LLM-based assistant that grounds its answers in that base through retrieval, displays the consulted sources, constrains its scope regarding health management, and offers suggested questions; and (iii) evaluated exploratory user experience with 12 municipal health managers, who completed standardized use-case scenarios and then answered the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ+) and open-ended questions. All seven UEQ+ scales were rated positively (means 1.08 to 1.69), with Efficiency, Dependability, and Perspicuity highest and Novelty lowest; every scale was above the neutral midpoint. Content analysis produced three categories: positive aspects (speed, ease of use, clarity, and practical usefulness), obstacles and constraints (conditional trust and a need to verify content), and security and transparency (data protection and source transparency). The quantitative and qualitative evidence converged, indicating adequate usability alongside a conditional, verification-oriented form of trust. A policy-informed AI assistant that cites its official sources proved feasible and was well-received as a decision-support tool for SUS management. Trust was conditional, and responsible adoption depends on source transparency, human verification, and constant refinement. The findings are exploratory and motivate larger, longitudinal, and comparative studies.

titulo: Systematic Literature Review of Explainable LLM-Powered ChatOps for CI/CD Pipeline Diagnostics and Developer Support
autores: A. M. A. D. Abeysinghe; W. M. J. I. Wijayanayake
venue: 2025 International Conference on Advances in Technology and Computing (ICATC)
abstract: This systematic literature review examines how explainable Large Language Models (LLMs) transform chat-ops applications for CI/CD pipeline diagnostics and developer support. Analyzing contemporary research from 2021–2025, this review synthesizes findings from studies on conversational AI agents, LLM-driven DevOps automation, and explainable AI techniques in software development. Key methodological approaches include Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) for chatbot development, multi-agent orchestration frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and two-staged LLM frameworks for detecting and remediating failures. Key findings reveal significant advancements in automating root cause analysis, orchestrating pipelines intelligently, and creating natural language interfaces for complex DevOps operations. Integrating explainable AI principles with conversational interfaces improves developer productivity, reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR), and enhances collaboration between development and operations teams. However, persistent interpretability, security governance, integration complexity, and maintaining human oversight in automated decision-making processes. This review provides a comprehensive roadmap for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage explainable LLM-powered chat-ops solutions for enhanced CI/CD pipeline management and developer support.

titulo: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Architecture for Schema-Aware Data Mining in Intelligent Information Systems
autores: M. Canzaniello; S. Amitrano; A. Borrelli; L. Qiu; S. M. A. Huda; F. Piccialli
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Machine Learning and Intelligent Systems Engineering (MLISE)
abstract: Heterogeneous operational data ecosystems often contain multiple event sources, registry tables, implicit join paths, and domain specific field semantics, making natural language analytical access difficult for non technical stakeholders. This paper presents an LLM-based multi-agent architecture for schema-aware data mining in intelligent information systems. The proposed framework transforms natural language analytical requests into grounded and executable computations through semantic intent classification, adaptive orchestration, registry driven dataset routing, schema-constrained join derivation, retrieval supported schema grounding, and controlled Python code execution. Unlike direct question-answering or text-only retrieval approaches, the system explicitly separates query interpretation, source selection, schema grounding, executable computation, and stakeholder facing reporting. The workflow is implemented as a stateful multi-agent architecture in which each execution step produces inspectable intermediate artifacts, including selected data sources, candidate joins, grounding context, generated analytical plans, executed code, structured outputs, and final responses. This design supports inspectable data mining operations over heterogeneous structured sources and helps reduce structurally inconsistent analyses caused by invalid source selection, missing bridge tables, or incorrect aggregation levels. The framework is evaluated on a proprietary urban parking analytics case study involving heterogeneous operational sources, including payment transactions, control events, enforcement records, spatial registries, and IoT derived occupancy signals. A 45 query benchmark is used to assess functional robustness, structured analytical correctness against gold artifacts, and answer level decision support quality. Results show zero crash cases, 40 execution successful runs, an artifact level gold-success rate of 71%, an answer relevance of 0.780, and strong clarity in LLM-as-a-judge evaluation (4.62/5). These findings suggest that schemaaware orchestration can support bounded operational analytics in the considered urban parking case study, while also showing that compositional queries involving time series, grouped ratios, and matrix-style outputs require stronger validation mechanisms.

titulo: Personalized Social Robot that Chat based on Autobiographical Memory
autores: J. -M. Wu; Z. -X. Guo; C. -H. Liao; X. Qian; L. -C. Fu; T. -R. Huang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
abstract: In an aging society, the introduction of robots into the field of elderly care has become an effective approach, as the elderly can receive emotional companionship through interactions with robots. However, existing human-robot conversations often lack depth because of the robots’ lack of memory capabilities. This limitation prevents robots from engaging in personalized conversations based on previous user-provided information during long-term conversations. To address this gap, this paper presents a solution that integrates autobiographical memory into chatbots. Conversations between robot and user are stored in our memory bank using an autobiographical memory framework. The system utilizes a hierarchical autobiographical memory system to fetch the most relevant memories according to the ongoing dialogue. Subsequently, these memories, along with the conversation context, are fed into the generative module to produce responses. Within this module, we introduce a personalized prompting strategy and ranking mechanism based on a large language model, ensuring the delivery of appropriate, personalized responses to users. The experimental part of this paper is divided into three sections: memory retrieval experiments, memory-grounded dialogue generation experiments, and human-robot interaction experiments. Experimental results show that the system can effectively retrieve memories of past conversations and naturally integrate them into everyday conversations, thus allowing the robot to provide long-term personalized companionship.

titulo: Physically Grounded Vision-Language Models for Robotic Manipulation
autores: J. Gao; B. Sarkar; F. Xia; T. Xiao; J. Wu; B. Ichter; A. Majumdar; D. Sadigh
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have led to improved performance on tasks such as visual question answering and image captioning. Consequently, these models are now well-positioned to reason about the physical world, particularly within domains such as robotic manipulation. However, current VLMs are limited in their understanding of the physical concepts (e.g., material, fragility) of common objects, which restricts their usefulness for robotic manipulation tasks that involve interaction and physical reasoning about such objects. To address this limitation, we propose PHYSOBJECTS, an object-centric dataset of 39.6K crowd-sourced and 417K automated physical concept annotations of common household objects. We demonstrate that fine-tuning a VLM on PhysObjects improves its understanding of physical object concepts, including generalization to held-out concepts, by capturing human priors of these concepts from visual appearance. We incorporate this physically grounded VLM in an interactive framework with a large language model-based robotic planner, and show improved planning performance on tasks that require reasoning about physical object concepts, compared to baselines that do not leverage physically grounded VLMs. We additionally illustrate the benefits of our physically grounded VLM on a real robot, where it improves task success rates. We release our dataset and provide further details and visualizations of our results at https://iliad.stanford.edu/pg-vlm/.

titulo: GPT-2++: An Optimized GPT-2 for RAG by Integrating BERT, Prompt Engineering, and Fine-Tuning
autores: F. Yamout; H. A. Hasan
venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) by allowing them to answer questions from specific knowledge sources, thereby reducing hallucinations and improving factual accuracy. While powerful models like GPT-3 and GPT-4 excel in RAG frameworks, their high computational requirements preclude their use on resource-constrained hardware, such as Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Smaller models like GPT-2 are more suitable for such environments but typically struggle to produce meaningful output in RAG tasks. This paper proposes GPT-2++, a novel framework to significantly improve GPT-2's question-answering capabilities for RAG. Our approach involves two key contributions: first, we fine-tune GPT-2 on a custom-built, high-quality dataset to create an optimized model, GPT-2-FT, which generates more contextually relevant answers. Second, we introduce a dual-model architecture, GPT-2++, that integrates GPT-2-FT with a BERT model. BERT is leveraged for its superior answer extraction capabilities, providing a concise answer that GPT-2-FT then expands into a comprehensive, human-readable response. We evaluate GPT-2++ against the original GPT-2 and GPT-3.5, using GPT-4 as an impartial evaluator. The results demonstrate that GPT-2++ outperforms the base GPT-2 in 90.6% of cases and shows competitive performance with GPT-3.5, validating its efficacy as a resource-efficient solution for advanced RAG systems.

titulo: Synthetic Data Generation Using Large Language Models: Advances in Text and Code
autores: M. Nadǎş; L. Dioşan; A. Tomescu
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This survey reviews how large language models (LLMs) are transforming synthetic training data generation in both natural language and code domains. By producing artificial but task-relevant examples, these models can significantly augment or even substitute for real-world datasets, particularly in scenarios where labeled data is scarce, expensive, or sensitive. This paper surveys recent advances in leveraging LLMs to create synthetic text and code, highlighting key techniques such as prompt-based generation, retrieval-augmented pipelines, and iterative self-refinement. We examine how these methods can enrich low-resource tasks (e.g. classification, question answering) and facilitate code-centric applications (e.g. instruction tuning, code translation, bug repair) through automated verification of functional correctness. Alongside potential benefits—cost-effectiveness, broad coverage, and controllable diversity—we discuss the accompanying challenges, including factual inaccuracies in generated text, insufficient stylistic or distributional realism, and risks of bias amplification. Proposed mitigation strategies range from filtering and weighting synthetic outputs to reinforcement learning with execution feedback in code domains. We conclude by outlining open research directions, such as automated prompt engineering, cross-modal data synthesis, and robust evaluation frameworks, underscoring the growing importance of LLM-generated synthetic data in accelerating AI development while emphasizing ethical and quality safeguards.

titulo: CoherentDrive: Conflict-Aware World-State Grounding for Hallucination-Resistant Autonomous Driving Reasoning
autores: S. Liu; L. Shi; J. Xu; Y. Gao; Y. Shi
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support language-based interaction in autonomous driving, including scene question answering and risk explanation. Yet a critical reliability failure persists: when prompted with long, redundant, and mutually inconsistent perception logs from heterogeneous sensors, LLMs may produce fluent but unsupported statements, hallucinate non-existent traffic agents, and amplify false premises. We address this problem from an interface perspective. We present CoherentDrive, a prompt-ready grounding framework that compiles multi-source perception facts into a compact, conflict-resolved Coherent World State (CWS) with entity identifiers, provenance, and uncertainty flags. CoherentDrive further enforces a grounding-first answering protocol that restricts responses to CWS-supported entities and relations, enabling explicit refusal when evidence is missing. On nuScenes-QA under a zero-shot setting with multiple LLM backbones, CoherentDrive consistently improves answer correctness while substantially reducing hallucinated entity mentions, and in a single-pass CWS prompting setting it also shortens prompt length and reduces inference latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that conflict-resolved world-state prompting provides an effective and reliable foundation for hallucination-resistant driving question answering.

titulo: Can Language Models Enable in-Context Database?
autores: Y. Pan; H. Yu; T. Zhao; J. Sun
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are emerging as incontext learners capable of handling a variety of tasks, including comprehension, planning, reasoning, question answering, arithmetic calculations, and more. At the core of these capabilities is LLMs' proficiency in representing and understanding structural or semi-structural data, such as tables and graphs. Numerous studies have demonstrated that reasoning on tabular data or graphs is not only feasible for LLMs but also gives a promising research direction which encodes these types of data as in-context data. The lightweight and human readable characteristics of in-context database can potentially make it an alternative for the traditional database in typical RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) settings. However, almost all current work focuses on static in-context data, which does not allow dynamic update. In this paper, to enable dynamic database update, delta encoding of database is proposed. We explore how data stored in traditional RDBMS can be encoded as in-context text and evaluate LLMs' proficiency for CRUD (Create, Read, Update and Delete) operations on in-context databases. A benchmark named InConDB is presented, and extensive experiments with model fine-tuning are conducted to show the performance of different language models in enabling in-context database by varying the database encoding method, prompting method, operation type and input data distribution, revealing both the proficiency and limitations.

titulo: LATEE: An Intelligent Tutoring System with AI Assistant and Virtual Patients for Clinical Diagnostic Reasoning Training
autores: T. Nguyen; T. Dang; D. Nguyen; C. Vo
venue: 2026 14th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Clinical diagnostic reasoning is a core medical competency, but traditional training is constrained by limited exposure to diverse real-world cases. On the other hand, although well known for question answering, large language models (LLMs) often fail as realistic training simulators due to premature diagnosis revelation or unnatural medical jargon. Therefore, we systematically analyze these limitations and construct Lavender Teeducation (LATEE), an intelligent tutoring system, for simulation-based clinical training. Using the MIMIC-IV database as the primary data source, narratives from the History of Present Illness were transformed into natural conversational dialogues to construct a diverse clinical case repository. The proposed system then integrates two core agents: (1) a High-Fidelity Virtual Patient, fine-tuned from Llama-3.1-8B using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) to simulate layperson behavior, and (2) a Pedagogical AI Assistant using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and an 8B-parameter LLaMA model retrieving knowledge via internal protocols such as American Academy of Family Physicians and Nguyen Tri Phuong Hospital, governed by a sixlayer prompt for safety. Applying the Multi-Judge Triangulation framework with three automated evaluators yielded consistently favorable outcomes across both components. As a result, our study sheds light on the optimal practices to repurpose general-purpose LLMs for specialized medical education tasks. By synergizing high-fidelity simulation with intelligent tutoring, the system extends clinical insight training beyond physical boundaries and resource constraints, effectively enabling clinical diagnostic reasoning practice and ensuring scalable benefits for medical education.

titulo: Comparative Analysis of Multimodal RAG Deployment Strategies for Medical Image Understanding: API-Based, Local Fine-Tuning, and Hybrid Approaches
autores: K. -C. Yang; H. -T. Chu
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Medicine, Health and Care (AIxMHC)
abstract: The advancement of clinical decision support systems depends on the essential integration of medical images together with their corresponding textual reports. The paradigm of Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) shows promise because it uses external knowledge sources to support Large Language Model (LLM) responses. Recent advances such as MMed-RAG demonstrate up to 43.8% improvement in factual accuracy for medical vision-language tasks. Through a conceptual case study and decision framework, we analyze the trade-offs for typical healthcare institutions. The research establishes particular medical use cases which demonstrate the best fit for each approach under strict Institutional Review Board (IRB) regulations and data privacy standards including HIPAA and GDPR. This research establishes a decision framework for healthcare ecosystem MRAG solution selection and implementation to address specific healthcare challenges.

titulo: RAILL: Retrieval-Augmented Instruction Tuning for Low-Resource Language Model Training
autores: Y. Choi; S. Lim; M. Park; J. Jung; T. Kim; E. Kim; C. -s. Kim; K. Lee; H. Choi; K. Song
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong performance across a wide range of tasks, yet their effectiveness remains limited in low-resource and domainspecific contexts where annotated data are scarce. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) partially mitigates this issue by providing external knowledge, but its reliance on retrieval only during inference restricts domain adaptation. To address this, we propose RAILL (Retrieval-Augmented Instruction Tuning for Low-resource Language Model Training), a unified framework that integrates retrieval into both training and inference. By exposing the model to domain-relevant documents during instruction tuning, RAILL enables contextual grounding and internalization of domain knowledge, enhancing adaptability under limited supervision. We validate RAILL in the education domain by developing Edu-LLaMA, a model trained on bilingual (Korean-English) educational materials. Edu-LLaMA achieves substantial improvements, including applications like question answering and text generation, producing outputs that are both factually consistent and pedagogically aligned. Further experiments in the biomedical domain confirm that RAILL generalizes effectively across specialized low-resource settings. Overall, RAILL provides a general and efficient framework for building domain-adapted LLMs that maintain reliability, factual grounding, and cross-lingual robustness even when domainspecific data are limited.

autores: W. Huang; L. Liu
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
abstract: Knowledge base question answering (KBQA) answers natural language questions by executing structured queries over a large knowledge base, returning verifiable answers and explicit reasoning traces. Classic approaches span knowledge retrieval methods and semantic parsing methods. Recent work reframes knowledge base question answering (KBQA) as a generate-then-retrieve framework: an instruction-tuned large language model first generates a logic form (S-expression), which is then grounded to entities and relations via unsupervised retrieval and executed as a SPARQL query, yielding interpretable answers and strong results on knowledge base QA benchmarks. Building on this paradigm, we present RKBQA, a plug-and-play revise-once module inserted between logic form generation and retrieval. RKBQA decides when the top predicted logic form is already reliable and when it should be minimally revised. It first uses relation-level priors to skip unnecessary revisions, and only when needed invokes a chain-of-thought reviser that proposes edits to the initial logic form. The original prediction is kept as a fallback, and downstream components select entities and relations and execute the first grounded query that returns a non-empty answer. Experiments on WebQSP and ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ) show that RKBQA consistently improves F1 and exact-match accuracy over a strong generate-then-retrieve baseline. We also release an out-of-sample revision set and a CoT-based revision dataset pairing questions and predicted logic forms with machine-audited minimal edits, along with code, to facilitate reproducibility. Code and revision datasets are available at https://github.com/WenboHuang3/RKBQA

titulo: Gen AI Driven FAQ Chatbot Using Advanced RAG Architecture for Querying Annual Reports

venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (ICCCT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving business landscape, stakeholders require timely and accurate access to financial and operational information from annual reports. However, the extensive and complex nature of these reports makes it difficult to efficiently extract key analytical trends, financial performance measures, and comparative insights. The traditional manual approach to analyse these documents is time-consuming, error prone, and inefficient. Stakeholders-including creditors, customers, suppliers, employees, government agencies, and industry analysts-rely on this data to make informed decisions. The absence of an automated mechanism to handle frequent queries regarding financial performance, operational metrics, and sustainability targets impedes large-scale informed decision making. This paper presents a Gen AI-driven solution that leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP), LangChain Framework and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Architecture to efficiently extract and analyze financial annual reports and its data. The approach involves utilizing PyPDF2 for data extraction, segmenting content using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, generating embeddings via FastEmbedEmbeddings module, and storing information in Qdrant for rapid similarity search. The response generation is powered by DeepSeek LLM, deployed locally via Ollama, ensuring privacy and computational efficiency. A Gradio-based UI is implemented for an intuitive interface. titulo: ReWind: Understanding Long Videos with Instructed Learnable Memory
autores: A. Diko; T. Wang; W. Swaileh; S. Sun; I. Patras
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are crucial for applications requiring integrated understanding textual and visual information. However, existing VLMs struggle with long videos due to computational inefficiency, memory limitations, and difficulties in maintaining coherent understanding across extended sequences. To address these challenges, we introduce ReWind, a novel memory-based VLM designed for efficient long video understanding while preserving temporal fidelity. ReWind operates in a two-stage framework. In the first stage, ReWind maintains a dynamic learnable memory module with a novel read-perceive-write cycle that stores and updates instruction-relevant visual information as the video unfolds. This module utilizes learnable queries and cross-attentions between memory contents and the input stream, ensuring low memory requirements by scaling linearly with the number of tokens. In the second stage, we propose an adaptive frame selection mechanism guided by the memory content to identify instruction-relevant key moments. It enriches the memory representations with detailed spatial information by selecting a few high-resolution frames, which are then combined with the memory contents and fed into a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate the final answer. We empirically demonstrate ReWind’s superior performance in visual question answering (VQA) and temporal grounding tasks, surpassing previous methods on long video benchmarks. Notably, ReWind achieves a +13% score gain and a +12% accuracy improvement on the MovieChat-1K VQA dataset and an +8% mIoU increase on Charades-STA for temporal grounding.

titulo: Prevalence Overshadows Concerns? Understanding Chinese Users' Privacy Awareness and Expectations Towards LLM-Based Healthcare Consultation
autores: Z. Liu; L. Hu; T. Zhou; Y. Tang; Z. Cai
venue: 2025 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly gaining traction in the healthcare sector, yet expanding the threat of sensitive health information being easily exposed and accessed without authorization. These privacy risks escalate in regions like China, where privacy awareness is notably limited. While some efforts have been devoted to user surveys on LLMs in healthcare, users' perceptions of privacy remain unexplored. To fill this gap, this paper contributes the first user study (n=846) in China on privacy awareness and expectations in LLM-based healthcare consultations. Specifically, a healthcare chatbot is deployed to investigate users' awareness in practice. Information flows grounded in contextual integrity are then employed to measure users' privacy expectations. Our findings suggest that the prevalence of LLMs amplifies health privacy risks by raising users' curiosity and willingness to use such services, thus overshadowing privacy concerns. 77.3% of participants are inclined to use such services, and 72.9% indicate they would adopt the generated advice. Interestingly, a paradoxical “illusion” emerges where users' knowledge and concerns about privacy contradict their privacy expectations, leading to greater health privacy exposure. Our extensive discussion offers insights for future LLM-based healthcare privacy investigations and protection technology development.

titulo: SAAP-GRID: Context-Aware Digital Assistant for Situational Awareness in Wildfire-Impacted Power Grid Operation Control Center
autores: S. Shrestha; C. I. Nwakanma; A. Srivastava
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Emergency operations in power grids require rapid interpretation of heterogeneous, time-varying information under dynamic and high-stakes conditions. Large Language Model (LLM) based digital assistants show promise for supporting situational awareness, but evaluating them safely under realistic emergency conditions remains challenging. We present Situationally Aware Assistant for Power Grid (SAAP-GRID), a simulation-grounded and context-aware orchestrator, along with an evaluation framework specifically in wildfire-related emergency scenarios relevant to power-grid operations. The developed framework uses physics-based simulations as controlled proxies for emergency conditions and benchmarks models through grounded question-answering tasks that require reasoning over time-varying system states. We instantiate the framework using a fire simulation engine and evaluate seven LLMs across factual retrieval, computational reasoning, trend analysis, comparative reasoning, temporal reasoning, and robustness tasks. Importantly, wildfire simulation outputs are treated as a dynamic hazard layer rather than as the final analytical target; the objective is to assess whether LLMs can translate evolving hazard conditions into power-grid-relevant situational awareness. We observe consistent gaps across computational, comparative, and temporal queries, indicating limitations in multi-step and spatio-temporal reasoning. While robustness is high for certain models, reliability remains inconsistent under complex scenarios. We also compare two external-grounding strategies, tool calling and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to assess their benefits in the studied emergency scenarios. Quantitatively, the best-performing model achieved perfect accuracy on factual, comparative, and temporal retrieval tasks, while computational reasoning remained the most challenging category (80%). External grounding through tool calling matched the strong direct-prompting baseline accuracy (93%) while improving robustness from 92% to 97%, whereas chain-of-thought prompting reduced overall accuracy to 85%, highlighting that structured grounding rather than unstructured reasoning improves LLM reliability in emergency power-grid scenarios. Overall, SAAP-GRID provides a scalable pre-deployment evaluation framework for assessing the performance and robustness of LLM-based assistants in safety-critical power-grid contexts.

titulo: FHRI: Scenario-Aware Reliability Scoring for Hallucination and Contradiction Detection in Financial LLM Responses
autores: Y. C. Teh; D. Mallikarachchi
venue: 2026 IEEE 9th International Conference on Signal and Image Processing Applications (ICSIPA)
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in financial question answering and advisory systems, but their responses may contain hallucinated facts, incorrect numerical claims, outdated information or cross-turn contradictions. This paper presents the Financial Hallucination Reliability Index (FHRI), a scenario-aware framework for detecting unreliable financial LLM responses. FHRI combines five complementary reliability signals, namely grounding, numerical or directional consistency, temporal validity, citation quality and entropy-based confidence, and augments them with natural language inference-based contradiction detection. abstract: Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) necessitates comprehension of both the spatial layout and the textual content. titulo: Exploring Human-like Explanation Strategies for Conversational Agents
autores: T. Zylowski; S. Mosa; M. Wölfel
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Human-AI Interaction and Experience Design (HAXD)
abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support human decision-making, the design of explanations that balance technical fidelity and human understandability becomes critical. Traditional Explainable AI (XAI) methods, such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), provide faithful feature attributions but are often difficult for laypeople to interpret, whereas Large Language Model (LLM)-generated explanations are fluent and intuitive, yet may lack grounding in the model’s true reasoning. Because explanation design directly shapes decision performance, explanation satisfaction, understandability, decision certainty, trust, and perceived workload, evaluating these human-centered outcomes is essential. To address this tension, we propose a modular explanation framework that integrates multiple human-centric strategies—including simple textual, detailed, expert SHAP-based, and counterfactual explanations—mediated by an LLM-based decision agent that adaptively selects the most suitable explanation based on task, user, and context. We evaluate this approach in a preliminary user study with 50 participants who classified news articles as real or fake, comparing traditional SHAP explanations with our framework. Results show that our proposed explanation framework improves human decision performance by 6.1% relative to SHAP-based explanations. In addition, our framework reduced perceived workload across multiple dimensions, with mental demand declining significantly. While these trends suggest promising potential for improving the explainability of conversational agents, further validation is needed to establish statistical robustness. Our findings highlight opportunities for future research to refine and expand upon faithful model explanations and usable, human-centered explanations in conversational agents.

titulo: AutoMedic: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Clinical Conversational Agents with Medical Dataset Grounding
autores: G. Oh; S. Park; B. -H. Kim
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) has recently emerged as a critical issue for safe and trustworthy application of LLMs in the medical domain. Although a variety of static medical question-answering (QA) benchmarks have been proposed, many aspects remain underexplored, such as the effectiveness of LLMs in generating responses in dynamic, interactive clinical multi-turn conversation situations and the identification of multi-faceted evaluation strategies beyond simple accuracy. However, formally evaluating a dynamic, interactive clinical situation is hindered by its vast combinatorial space of possible patient states and interaction trajectories, making it difficult to standardize and quantitatively measure such scenarios. Here, we introduce AutoMedic, a multi-agent simulation framework that enables automated evaluation of LLMs as clinical conversational agents. AutoMedic transforms off-the-shelf static QA datasets into virtual patient profiles, enabling realistic and clinically grounded multi-turn clinical dialogues between LLM agents. The performance of various clinical conversational agents is then assessed based on our CARE metric, which provides a multi-faceted evaluation standard of clinical conversational accuracy, efficiency/strategy, empathy, and robustness. Our findings, validated by human experts, demonstrate the validity of AutoMedic as an automated evaluation framework for clinical conversational agents, offering practical guidelines for the effective development of LLMs in conversational medical applications.

titulo: Fact-and-norm RAG: traceable question answering over regulated engineering documents with dual citations
autores: T. Ma; C. Li; H. Lai; H. Wang; F. Xu; L. Fang
venue: 2nd International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence Innovations (IS-AII 2026)
abstract: Structured artifacts in safety- and compliance-critical engineering encode meaning through both instance configurations and schema-scoped normative semantics (definitions, constraints, and guidelines). While long-context LLM prompting and generic RAG can retrieve supporting text, they often treat all evidence as untyped chunks and provide limited traceability for norm-grounded decisions. We propose a traceable QA framework that (i) represents a document as an instance graph (ABox) and a knowledge-augmented meta-model ontology (TBox+K) with typed, schema-scoped norm objects, (ii) performs schema-constrained meta-model linking to produce a replayable retrieval plan, (iii) retrieves evidence through separate fact and norm channels under an explicit scope filter, and (iv) generates answers as atomic claims with claim-level dual citations to retrieved facts and norms. A lightweight validator enforces index-range and existence constraints and maps citation indices to stable evidence identifiers for downstream verification. Beyond correctness, we evaluate attribution faithfulness with semantic perturbations that edit selected normative objects and test whether conclusions and norm citations track normative changes.

titulo: A Review of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Models for Knowledge Graphs
autores: B. M. Dube; J. V. Fonou-Dombeu
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Deep Learning (DL) has revolutionized Knowledge Graph (KG) construction and reasoning in the recent past. The integration of DL models with KGs has shown potential to offer numerous benefits in KG creation, completeness, analysis and applications. However, there is a lack of comprehensive reviews on the latest DL models designed explicitly for KGs. This paper addresses these gaps by thoroughly reviewing state-of-the-art DL models for KGs and their applications in leading areas such as question answering and recommender systems. Furthermore, this review paper provides a comprehensive overview of recent advancements in DL models applied to KGs. This review aims to deepen the understanding of the use of DL in KGs and investigate how DL can further enhance their effectiveness and utility across diverse domains. The reviewed models include translation-based models such as TransE, TransH, and TransR, Neural/Matrix factorization models such as ConvE, DistMult, TuckER and RotatE, GNN models such as R-GCN, GAT, GGNN, Large Language Models (LLMs) such as KG-BERT, KG-LLaMA, LLM4VKG, KoPA, and CPKGC, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models such as Graph-RAG and Cold-RAG and multimodal KG (MMKG) models such as MKGAT and MMKDGAT in the context of KGs. The review highlights key features and the effectiveness of these models in addressing domain-specific challenges, providing insights into their potential to advance KG research. We highlight key trends, including the rise of GNNs and hybrid LLM-KG systems, and identify unresolved challenges like dynamic KG updates and multimodal integration. The strengths and limitations of these models are also discussed in detail, along with their areas of application within the context of KGs.

titulo: LinkedOut: Linking World Knowledge Representation Out of Video LLM for Next-Generation Video Recommendation
autores: H. Zhang; Y. Lu; L. Wang; Y. Li; D. Chen; Y. Xu; Y. Fu
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
abstract: Video Large Language Models (VLLMs) unlock worldknowledge-aware video understanding through pretraining on internet-scale data and have already shown promise on tasks such as movie analysis and video question answering. However, deploying VLLMs for downstream tasks such as video recommendation remains challenging, since real systems require multi-video inputs, lightweight backbones, low-latency sequential inference, and rapid response. In practice, (1) decode-only generation yields high latency for sequential inference, (2) typical interfaces do not support multi-video inputs, and (3) constraining outputs to language discards fine-grained visual details that matter for downstream vision tasks. We argue that these limitations stem from the absence of a representation that preserves pixel-level detail while leveraging world knowledge. We present LinkedOut, a representation that extracts VLLM world knowledge directly from video to enable fast inference, supports multi-video histories, and removes the language bottleneck. LinkedOut extracts semantically grounded, knowledge-aware tokens from raw frames using VLLMs, guided by promptable queries and optional auxiliary modalities. We introduce a cross-layer knowledge fusion MoE that selects the appropriate level of abstraction from the rich VLLM features, enabling personalized, interpretable, and low-latency recommendation. To our knowledge, LinkedOut is the first VLLM-based video recommendation method that operates on raw frames without handcrafted labels, achieving state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks. Interpretability studies and ablations confirm the benefits of layer diversity and layer-wise fusion, pointing a practical way to better exploit VLLM world knowledge and visual reasoning for downstream tasks.

abstract: With the widespread use of multimodal data-such as images, videos, audio, and text-in real-world scenarios, efficiently and accurately extracting high-level semantic information has become a key challenge in artificial intelligence research. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated powerful capabilities in semantic understanding and generation, offering a new paradigm for multimodal semantic extraction. In this paper, we propose an abstractive description-based approach grounded in large language models. By transforming multimodal inputs into natural language descriptions and leveraging LLMs for semantic abstraction and structured output, the proposed method enables unified semantic representations of multimodal content. This approach not only preserves the rich information contained in the original data but also enhances the interpretability and generalization ability of downstream tasks, such as retrieval, question answering, and reasoning. We review the dominant technical paradigms in the literature, present our proposed framework, and discuss promising directions for future research.

titulo: Zero-Shot Visual Reasoning by Vision-Language Models: Benchmarking and Analysis
autores: A. Nagar; S. Jaiswal; C. Tan
venue: 2024 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown impressive zero-and few-shot performance on real-world visual question answering (VQA) benchmarks, alluding to their capabilities as visual reasoning engines. However, the benchmarks being used conflate "pure" visual reasoning with world knowledge, and also have questions that involve a limited number of reasoning steps. Thus, it remains unclear whether a VLM’s apparent visual reasoning performance is due to its world knowledge, or due to actual visual reasoning capabilities.To clarify this ambiguity, we systematically benchmark and dissect the zero-shot visual reasoning capabilities of VLMs through synthetic datasets that require minimal world knowledge, and allow for analysis over a broad range of reasoning steps. We focus on two novel aspects of zero-shot visual reasoning: i) evaluating the impact of conveying scene information as either visual embeddings or purely textual scene descriptions to the underlying large language model (LLM) of the VLM, and ii) comparing the effectiveness of chain-of-thought prompting to standard prompting for zero-shot visual reasoning.We find that the underlying LLMs, when provided textual scene descriptions, consistently perform better compared to being provided visual embeddings. In particular, 18% higher accuracy is achieved on the PTR dataset. We also ∼find that CoT prompting performs marginally better than standard prompting only for the comparatively large GPT-3.5-Turbo (175B) model, and does worse for smaller-scale models. This suggests the emergence of CoT abilities for visual reasoning in LLMs at larger scales even when world knowledge is limited. Overall, we find limitations in the abilities of VLMs and LLMs for more complex visual reasoning, and highlight the important role that LLMs can play in visual reasoning.

titulo: Securing Applications of Large Language Models: A Shift-Left Approach

venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electro Information Technology (eIT)
abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has brought forth remarkable capabilities in various domains, yet it also poses inherent risks to trustfulness, encompassing concerns such as toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, ethics, privacy, and fairness. However, ensuring robust security measures to mitigate potential security vulnerabilities is imperative. By adopting this security shift-left methodology, developers can confidently develop LLM-based applications with robust security protection, safeguarding against potential threats and vulnerabilities.

titulo: Augmented Knowledge Graph Querying leveraging LLMs
autores: M. Arazzi; D. Ligari; S. Nicolazzo; A. Nocera
venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Adopting Knowledge Graphs (KGs) as a structured, semantic-oriented, data representation model has significantly improved data integration, reasoning, and querying capabilities across different domains. This is especially true in modern scenarios such as Industry 5.0, where the integration of data from humans, smart devices, and production processes is crucial, not only for industrial innovation, but also for supporting the digital transition of government administrations and organizations. However, the management, retrieval, and visualization of data from a KG using formal query languages can be difficult for non-expert users due to their technical complexity, thus limiting their usage inside industrial environments. For this reason, we introduce SparqLLM, a framework that utilizes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solution, to enhance the querying of Knowledge Graphs (KGs). SparqLLM executes the Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) pipeline to construct KGs from raw data. It also features a natural language interface powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable automatic SPARQL query generation. By integrating template-based methods as retrieved-context for the LLM, SparqLLM enhances query reliability and reduces semantic errors, ensuring more accurate and efficient KG interactions. Moreover, to improve usability, the system incorporates a dynamic visualization dashboard that adapts to the structure of the retrieved data, presenting the query results in an intuitive format. Rigorous experimental evaluations demonstrate that SparqLLM achieves high query accuracy, improved robustness, and user-friendly interaction with KGs, establishing it as a scalable solution to access semantic data.

titulo: OpenClaw-Bench: Reproducible Evaluation of Multi-Agent Harnesses for Multi-Step Tool-Use Tasks
autores: S. Zhang
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computer Science, Machine Learning and Agents (CSMLA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to operate external tools, browse information, edit files, execute code, and deliver task artifacts. However, many practical tasks are not single-turn question-answering problems; they require multi-step planning, tool invocation, intermediate-state management, failure recovery, and result verification. This paper presents OpenClaw-Bench, a reproducible experimental protocol for evaluating governed multi-agent harnesses on multi-step tool-use tasks. The protocol is motivated by OpenClaw, a Supervisor-Worker runtime designed to make long-horizon tool use more governable without repeating implementation details in the abstract. We define a benchmark covering five task families: file and data processing, code repair, evidence-grounded web research, document generation, and cross-tool workflows. The proposed evaluation compares a single-agent tool user, a naive multi-agent baseline, the full OpenClaw harness, and five ablated variants. Metrics combine automated checks, LLM-as-a-judge scoring, human calibration, execution-cost accounting, tool-use correctness, collaboration quality, and error recovery. By formalizing task cards, system variants, scoring dimensions, and statistical procedures, OpenClaw-Bench provides an implementation-ready protocol for studying reliability in long-horizon tool-use tasks.

venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME)
abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) is pivotal for acquiring valuable knowledge in visual scene understanding, making it crucial for tasks such as visual question answering and visual reasoning. In recent times, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in object grounding and recognition. Nevertheless, constructing the scene graph directly poses a challenging task for MLLMs due to the intricate nature of predicting relationships between objects and the action states of objects. Simultaneously, reliance solely on the large language model (LLM) for achieving region understanding in complex scenes makes MLLMs susceptible to hallucinations, leading to potential errors in determining the coordinates of objects. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a large vision-language model (LVLM) within the Shikra framework for scene graph generation. Our approach involves the creation of an instruction-following SGG dataset for the fine-tuning of the LVLM. After SGG, we recognize that the scene graph generated by the LVLM can assist the LLM in answering visual questions. Thus, we evaluate LVLM-based question-and-answering models by leveraging the scene graph as a rationale, introducing a concept termed Scene Graph Chain of Thought (SGCoT). The proposed SGG method is rigorously evaluated through both quantitative and qualitative experiments on closed-set and open-set SGG tasks, affirming its effectiveness. Moreover, using the scene graph generated by fine-tuning LVLM as a rationale in the chain of thoughts results in a competitive performance on several vision-language compositional benchmarks.

titulo: A2RAG: Adaptive Agentic Graph Retrieval for Cost-Aware and Reliable Reasoning
autores: J. Liu; Z. Chen; S. Qiao; M. Ju; D. Zhang; B. Han; S. Yu; X. Shu; J. Wu; D. Wen; X. Cao; G. Liu; Z. Yang
venue: 2026 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Data Engineering Workshops (ICDEW)
abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Graph-RAG) enhances multihop question answering by organizing corpora into knowledge graphs and routing evidence through relational structure. However, practical deployments face two persistent bottlenecks: (i) mixed-difficulty workloads where one-size-fits-all retrieval either wastes cost on easy queries or fails on hard multihop cases, and (ii) extraction loss, where graph abstraction omits fine-grained qualifiers that remain only in source text. We present A2RAG, an adaptive-and-agentic GraphRAG framework for cost-aware and reliable reasoning. A2RAG couples an adaptive controller that verifies evidence sufficiency and triggers targeted refinement only when necessary, with an agentic retriever that progressively escalates retrieval effort and maps graph signals back to provenance text to remain robust under extraction loss and incomplete graphs. Experiments on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA demonstrate that A2RAG achieves +9.9/+11.8 absolute gains in Recall@2, while cutting token consumption and end-to-end latency by about 50% relative to iterative multihop baselines.

titulo: The Impact of Ontology Structure in the Performance of RAG Systems: a Medical Use Case
autores: D. Lin; A. Riquelme-García; J. T. Fernández-Breis; P. E. Anderson
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a widely used framework for circumventing the knowledge constraints of LLMs. General-purpose RAG systems are naive to domain-specific terminology and structure. As a result, prior work such as OG-RAG leverages ontologies to bake expert knowledge and domain understanding into RAG systems. However, the feasibility, effectiveness, and accuracy of OG-RAG is completely dependent on the ontology. In order to build new ontologies and modify existing ontologies for OG-RAG, it is critical to understand how structural aspects of an ontology impact performance. In this study, we systematically evaluate how the structure of an ontology determines performance across two key tasks: document-to-ontology mapping, and question-answering. To measure its performance, we applied OG-RAG across two specialized domains: chronic lower back pain and spinal cord injury rehabilitation. We measured how the specificity of the ontology classes can impact the performance of OG-RAG, finding that an ontology containing more general classes can reduce the risk of hallucinations during document-to-ontology mapping, while using specific instance-level classes can hinder accuracy. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of adding class descriptions on OG-RAG behavior, revealing an increase in performance when providing the additional context. Our results identify potential best practices when building ontologies for OG-RAG, enabling its application across domains.

titulo: Structured Interfaces for Automated Reasoning with 3D Scene Graphs
autores: A. Ray; J. Arkin; H. Biggie; C. Fan; L. Carlone; N. Roy
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: In order to provide a robot with the ability to understand and react to a user’s natural language inputs, the natural language must be connected to the robot’s underlying representations of the world. Recently, large language models (LLMs) and 3D scene graphs (3DSGs) have become a popular choice for grounding natural language and representing the world. In this work, we address the challenge of using LLMs with 3DSGs to ground natural language. Existing methods encode the scene graph as serialized text within the LLM’s context window, but this encoding does not scale to large or rich 3DSGs. Instead, we propose to use a form of Retrieval Augmented Generation to select a subset of the 3DSG relevant to the task. We encode a 3DSG in a graph database and provide a query language interface (Cypher) as a tool to the LLM with which it can retrieve relevant data for language grounding. We evaluate our approach on instruction following and scene question-answering tasks and compare against baseline context window and code generation methods. Our results show that using Cypher as an interface to 3D scene graphs scales significantly better to large, rich graphs on both local and cloud-based models. This leads to large performance improvements in grounded language tasks while also substantially reducing the token count of the scene graph content.

titulo: Edge-AdaptiveKG: Resource-Efficient Knowledge Graph Construction for RAG on Edge Devices
autores: Y. Du; J. Niu; C. J. Xue; N. Guan
venue: 2026 IEEE 32nd International Conference on Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems and Applications (RTCSA)
abstract: Integrating Knowledge Graphs (KGs) into Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can substantially improve LLM performance on complex question answering (QA) by reducing hallucinations and supplying structured context. However, building high-quality KGs over large corpora for edge scenarios is challenging: cloud-based processing introduces latency and dependency on remote services, while exhaustive on-device construction with LLMs is often computationally infeasible under limited hardware budgets. We observe that traditional non-LLM methods can efficiently capture explicit knowledge, and that real-world queries typically touch only a small, highly concentrated portion of the graph. As a result, static and exhaustive KG construction is redundant and inefficient. We propose Edge-AdaptiveKG, a resource-aware framework that combines an offline Seed KG (S-KG) with an online Query-driven KG (Q-KG). Lightweight non-LLM methods build the S-KG, while the LLM is invoked on demand during question answering to incrementally expand the Q-KG only when complex relations are needed. Experiments show that Edge-AdaptiveKG reduces computational overhead and inference latency, enabling KG-enhanced RAG on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive QA accuracy.

titulo: Agentic RAG for Structure Aware Long Document Reasoning
autores: D. Q. Lam; G. H. Tran; T. -D. Do
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Graph-based and multimodal retrieval frameworks provide a strong foundation for long-document question answering, but single-pass retrieval can remain brittle when queries are ambiguous, multi-step, or misaligned with the indexed evidence. This paper presents an Emotion-Aware Digital Therapy Assistant that combines large language models (LLMs), multimodal emotion detection, and agentic workflows to deliver context-sensitive and safety-conscious mental-wellness support. The assistant first estimates the user’s affective state from text and conversational context, then evaluates psychological risk using a healthcare-tuned LLM and rule-based safety graph, and finally chooses between therapeutic conversation, coping exercises, or escalation to emergency workflows (e.g., crisis alerts, human clinicians). We design a realistic benchmark—EMOThera—comprising 8,500 annotated utterances across seven emotion categories and three risk levels and report results on emotion classification, crisis detection, latency, and user experience. The proposed system achieves 89.7% macro accuracy and 0.88 macro F1 for emotion recognition, 0.91 AUC for high-risk detection, and a median end-to-end latency of 430ms per turn on commodity hardware, while 81.3% of participants in a small pilot (n = 32) report feeling "emotionally understood". These findings suggest that combining LLMs with structured safety workflows and lightweight multimodal modeling can yield an accessible, low-friction, and safer pathway between self-help tools and professional mental-health care.

venue: 2026 34th Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
abstract: Abstract-Recently, large language models (LLMs) have enabled significant advances across a wide range of domains. However, the training, adaptation, and evaluation of LLMs with a large number of parameters incur substantial computational and financial costs. This limits the ability of researchers with constrained resources to effectively leverage LLM-based approaches. In this study, we examine the performance of relatively small-scale LLMs for question answering and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on Turkish legal texts under limited computational resources. We investigate several factors affecting Turkish RAG performance and adapt embedding models to the target domain using automatically generated question-context pairs. The findings indicate that relatively small, domain-adapted models can achieve performance levels close to those of larger-scale or commercial models on the target dataset.

titulo: A Multi-Stage Agentic Approach to Factuality-Aware Long and Multi-Document Text Summarization
autores: P. V. Khandar; D. K. Mohanty; S. K. Baliarsingh
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovations in Communication, Geoscience and Robotics (ICICGR)
abstract: Abstractive summarization methods can produce fluent, readable summaries, but they do not always remain fully grounded in the source document. Previous work in this domain has repeatedly highlighted these factual inconsistencies and explored various ways to mitigate them. It includes reinforcement learning, contrastive objectives, and semantic modelling approaches. Despite these efforts, maintaining factual accuracy remains difficult, especially with long and information-rich inputs. To address this challenge, we introduce an agentic generation framework that divides the summarization process into four stages: planning, constrained generation, verification, and iterative refinement. This framework functions through a modular pipeline. First it identifies key factual units from the source. Then it generates structured summaries and evaluates their consistency using entailment-and question–answering-based signals. Finally, it refines the output to correct any detected inconsistencies. We assess our proposed model on standard benchmarks, including CNN/Daily Mail, Multi-News, WikiSum and DUC, using both ROUGE and factuality-focused evaluation metrics. The experimental results indicate consistent improvements in factual accuracy with ROUGE scores of R1 (45.5), R2 (22.8) and RL (42.6) achieved on CNN/Daily Mail, as well as average FactCC (0.86) and average QA-based score (0.84). Ablation analysis further demonstrates that each stage plays a significant role in the overall performance. These findings suggest that agentic summarization offers an effective approach to enhance the reliability of real-world summarization systems.

titulo: SAVE: Sparse Autoencoder-Driven Visual Information Enhancement for Mitigating Object Hallucination
autores: S. Park; S. Yoo; J. Mok; S. Yoon
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
abstract: Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have advanced substantially, they remain vulnerable to object hallucination caused by language priors and visual information loss. To address this, we propose SAVE (Sparse Autoencoder-Driven Visual Information Enhancement), a framework that mitigates hallucination by steering the model along Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) latent features. A binary object-presence question-answering probe identifies the SAE features most indicative of the model’s visual information processing, referred to as visual understanding features. Steering the model along these identified features reinforces grounded visual understanding and effectively reduces hallucination. With its simple design, SAVE outperforms state-of-the-art training-free methods on standard benchmarks, achieving a 10%p improvement in CHAIRS and consistent gains on POPE and MMHal-Bench. Extensive evaluations across multiple models and layers confirm the robustness and generalizability of our approach. Further analysis reveals that steering along visual understanding features suppresses the generation of uncertain object tokens and increases attention to image tokens, mitigating hallucination. Code is released at https://github.com/wiarae/SAVE.

titulo: NexaLearn: A Generative AI-Based Multimodal Framework for Interactive Video Learning Assistance
autores: H. Srivastava; D. Srivastava; J. Agrahari; A. P. Singh; A. Singh
venue: 2026 IEEE Madhya Pradesh Section Conference (MPCON)
abstract: The meteoric increase in popularity of video-based e-learning platforms has made learning more accessible; nevertheless, due chiefly to their passive nature, these platforms fail to foster interactivity between learners themselves, actual contextualization of information, and retention. In this paper, we present a multimodal generative AI learning assistant based on interactivity and personalized learning from videos. The working framework comprises automatic speech recognition for extracting transcripts aligned with video over time, transformer models for embedding-based semantic representation, and FAISS-based retrieval from an indexed corpus of dense vector representations supporting retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Multimodal content understanding gets realized by the application of optical character recognition and computer vision for extracting textual and visual information from lecture slides and diagrams. An interactive chatbot built using a large language model provides context-aware question answering using retrieved video segments tied to the exact timestamps. The system was built on scalable web architecture, with React.js as a front-end technology, Python Flask/FastAPI service as a back end for processing, and a cloud-hosted vector database for efficient indexing and retrieval. Experimental evaluation based on retrieval relevance and response accuracy metrics proves reduced information access time and increased learning efficiency. The proposed system converts the passive consumption of videos into an active intelligent and learner-centered educational experience.

titulo: MSKGCF: A Framework for Multimodal Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion
autores: A. Maoliniyazi; C. Ma; X. Meng
venue: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
abstract: Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) are foundational for automated discovery and reasoning. However, their construction faces critical hurdles due to the heterogeneity of scientific literature, where essential information is fragmented across complex text and unstructured visual modalities like figures and tables. Furthermore, the rapid growth of publications makes continuous updates necessary, as rebuilding from scratch is costly. To address this, we propose MSKGCF, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion. MSKGCF adopts a two-stage extraction strategy, first entity recognition, then relation classification, driven by a general-purpose Teacher LLM (GPT-4o) to capture information across text and visual modalities. A fine-tuned multimodal Student LLM (Qwen3VL) is then trained online via an uncertainty-driven active learning loop, which uses model entropy to identify low-confidence samples ("hard" examples) and prioritizes them as in-context references for few-shot learning. Furthermore, we introduce a logic-based fusion mechanism to integrate disparate sub-graphs via LLM-based conflict resolution, ensuring scalability. Experiments show that MSKGCF outperforms existing methods in extraction accuracy. A downstream case study on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) confirms that the resulting knowledge graph improves scientific question answering.

titulo: A Unified Framework for Structured Document Analysis, Visualization and Interactive Querying
autores: R. Pandey; A. Tyagi; P. Sharma; A. Srivastava
venue: 2026 IEEE 15th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The massive increase in digital documents like research papers, reports, contracts, and scanned records has rendered the process of analyzing documents manually to be more and more time-consuming and inefficient. Traditional document readers are mainly associated with searching using keywords and provide little assistance in the knowledge of document organization, numerical information, or semantic context. Despite the recent developments of Large Language Models (LLM), that allow engaging with documents through dialogue, a significant number of systems do not provide reliable support of the structured extraction, visualization and scanned document processing. In this paper, we introduce InsightScan, a single document analysis and interaction system that allows us to understand documents in a structured way, perform automated visualization and document-grounded question answering with a single system. The proposed method converts unstructured and semi-structured documents into a structured intermediate form, which is always re-purposed to provide analysis visualization and conversational queries. Such disintersection of extraction and reasoning enhances reliability, interpretability and consistency of data. InsightScan is a combination of text extraction via OCR, structured normalization, automatic charting and a natural language interaction web-based interface. Financial records are taken as representative evaluation examples because of their complexity in terms of structure and numerical aspects. Through experimentation, it has been found that the system yields correct structured outputs, viable visualizations and grounded conversational reactions without any numerical hallucination. InsightScan allows users to go through documents visually and through a conversational system, thus eliminating the manual work and enhancing efficiency of analysis. The suggested framework illustrates the viability of the general-purpose, single-document interaction system that may be applicable to research, scholarly education, and data-driven decision-making processes.

titulo: A Unified Framework for AR Indoor Navigation and Conversational Information Retrieval in Smart Campus Environments
autores: A. Magdy; A. Mohamed; A. A. Boghdady; B. Achraf; H. Mohamed; Z. Abd-El-Hamid; S. Ali; I. Hegazy
venue: 2025 Twelfth International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Navigating complex indoor environments like university campuses poses a significant challenge, compounded by the difficulty of accessing specific institutional information. While vision-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) offers continuous tracking, it suffers from cumulative drift. Sim- ilarly, standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for question-answering are prone to context collision. This paper presents a unified mobile application that integrates a robust AR indoor navigation module with an intelligent conversational assistant to address both challenges simultaneously. The pro- posed navigation system fuses the continuous motion tracking of SLAM with high-precision QR code markers for drift correction, providing accurate, real-time visual guidance. For information retrieval, a novel RAG architecture is proposed featuring an LLM-powered router that intelligently directs user queries to one of several specialized vector stores, effectively eliminating con- text collision and improving contextual accuracy. Experimental results confirm that the navigation module provides robust and accurate visual guidance in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, the chatbot's router-based architecture demonstrates a marked improvement in retrieval accuracy, consistently identifying more relevant information than a standard RAG system. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of synergistically combining spatial computing with advanced conversational AI to create a comprehensive smart campus assistant, enhancing the student experience by providing seamless access to both physical and digital resources.

titulo: EagleCare: Augmenting ICU Monitoring with LLMs and Knowledge Graph Reasoning
autores: J. Guo; Y. Gao; Z. Liu; Y. Rao; J. Hu; H. Wang
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Knowledge Graph (ICKG)
abstract: Recent advances in medical artificial intelligence have highlighted the potential of large language models (LLMs) in performing general clinical tasks such as medical report generation and question answering. However, their performance in intensive care units (ICUs) remains limited due to the sophisticated nature of the knowledge involved and the interactions among multiple organs. To address these issues, we propose EagleCare, a novel LLM-based Clinical Decision Support System that integrates knowledge graph reasoning to enhance multi-organ assessment and clinical inference in the ICU. EagleCare constructs an ICU-specific knowledge graph (ICU-KG) aligned with patient electronic health records (EHRs), from which our system retrieves clinically relevant reasoning paths. These reasoning paths are then synthesized with patient-specific data through retrieval-augmented generation(RAG) and LLM-based inference to support interpretable and context-aware decisions. This combination of symbolic medical knowledge and neural representation learning improves the reliability and transparency of the decision process. Experimental results on a real-world ICU dataset and two medical QA datasets demonstrate the superiority of our framework, achieving an average improvement of 5.3% compared to baselines with SOTA LLMs. Furthermore, EagleCare assessment outputs exhibit strong alignment with expert clinical reports, indicating its practical utility in high-stakes ICU environments.
